column32: Inclusion Criteria: Subjects with stage IV NSCLC (not recurrent or re-staged). Expected to receive at least 2 additional cycles (at least 6 total weeks) of first line myelosuppressive cyclic chemotherapy after randomization. Subjects should not be expected to receive only maintenance chemotherapy. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1 as assessed within 21 days prior to randomization. 18 years of age or older at screening. Life expectancy greater than 6 months based on the judgment of the investigator and documented during screening. Hemoglobin level less than or equal to 11.0 g/dL as assessed by the local laboratory; sample obtained within 7 days prior to randomization (retest in screening is acceptable). Adequate serum folate (greater than or equal to 2 ng/mL) and vitamin B12 (greater than or equal to 200 pg/mL) levels assessed by central laboratory (supplementation and retest acceptable) during screening. Subjects must have had a baseline scan (CT, MRI, or PET/CT) of the chest to assess disease burden before starting on first line chemotherapy for NSCLC and those images must have been reviewed by the investigator prior to randomization. If the scan was performed more than 28 days prior to randomization, an additional scan must be performed and reviewed by the investigator to confirm that the patient has not progressed before randomization. Before any study-specific procedure, the appropriate written informed consent must be obtained from the subject or a legally accepted representative .

Primary Objective: Change in HbAlc from baseline to 6 months of treatment between Wosulin and Novolin® USA (as surrogate indicator of change in insulin antibodies titers between the two treatment arms). Secondary Objective: Correlation between change in HbA1c from baseline to 6 and 12 months of treatment and change in anti insulin and neutralizing antibodies with insulin dose as covariate. column51: Note: There was no recruitment in the study. The study has also been terminated; notification regarding the same has also been submitted to DCGI. This is a phase II multi-centre, randomized, placebo-controlled, double blind trial to study low anticoagulant heparin (sevuparin/DF02) as adjuvant therapy in moderate falciparum malaria. The study will be conducted at one centre in India and will recruit 30-50 (15-25 in each treatment arm) male or female subjects, 18 to 65 years of age diagnosed with moderate to severe P. falciparum malaria according to the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The patient will be in the study for 28 days, including follow-up however patient presenting with neurological sequelae at discharge will be followed also at 3, 6 and 12 months. The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of sevuparin/DF02 when administered IV every 6 hours until patient recovery for a maximum of 3 consecutive days (minimum 5 doses) as adjunctive therapy to IV artesunate in patients with moderate to severe P. falciparum malaria. The secondary objectives are to access the efficacy of sevuparin/DF02, given as adjuvant therapy on: 1. Dynamics of different developmental stages of malaria parasites in peripheral blood 2. Reversal of hyperlactatemia as a measure of tissue hypoxemia 3. Normalisation of the plasma Base Excess (BE) as a measure of reversal of metabolic acidosis 4. Coma recovery time in patients with cerebral malaria as measured by the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 5. Improvement of microcirculatory flow as measured by Orthogonal Polarizing Spectrometry (OPS) 6. Improvement of retinopathy as assessed by retinal photography 7. Mortality rate 8. column28: PRF preparation requires a table centrifuge and collection kit comprising of vacutainer and attached needle. Under sterile precautions, 50 ml of whole blood will be drawn into vacutainer tubes without anticoagulant and immediately centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 10 minutes. A fibrin clot is obtained in the middle of the tube, just between the red blood cells at the bottom and acellular plasma at the top. 50 ml of whole blood will yield about 2.5 ml of fibrin clot. This clot will be removed from the tube under aseptic precautions with the help of sterile forceps and the attached red blood cells will be scraped off and discarded. Fibrin clot will be applied topically over the ulcer surface at a ratio of 1 ml of clot for every 10 ml of ulcer volume.THis is followed by application of secondary dressings with cotton pads and application of a plaster of paris slab for off loading the foot. This process is repeated weekly for 4 weeks. If the ulcer heals prior to 4 weeks then the application of the platelet rich fibrin is stopped. | The ulcer will be cleaned with 0.9% sterile saline. Saline soaked gauzes will be used for dressing.Plaster of paris cast will then be applied. A key hole window is cut over the ulcer and this process is repeated every 2 days for 4 weeks or till the ulcer heals which ever comes first

column51: Trophic ulcer is a type of chronic ulcer caused by external trauma to a part of the body that is in poor condition because of disease, vascular insufficiency, poor nutrition or loss of afferent nerve fibers. These factors, along with the mechanical stress associated with weight bearing, make the lower extremities vulnerable to the development of ulcers, slow healing and resistance to traditional methods of treatment.Platelet derivates have been used to accelerate tissue repair in orthopaedic surgery, ophthalmologic conditions, plastic surgery, and chronic diabetic ulcers.Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is a second generation platelet concentrate whose advantages over the better known platelet-rich plasma(PRP) include ease of preparation/application, minimal expense, and lack of biochemical modification (no exogenous thrombin or calcium is required. This study is planned to compare the efficacy of PRF over moist saline dressing in the management of trophic ulcers associated with leprosy.. The study design is a randomised , prospective, open label design. It is planned to recruit 33 participants in each arm at a single site. The participants included are between the age of 18 and 65 and have an ulcer size of 1*1 to 5*5 cms. Efficacy will be asessed weekly for 4 weeks. The measurements include area, and volume at each visit. column51: Background Pompe disease is a rare, autosomal recessive disease caused by the deficiency of lysosomal acid Î±-glucosidase (GAA), an enzyme that degrades glycogen. The resulting accumulation of glycogen in body tissues, especially cardiac, respiratory-specific, and major skeletal muscle groups, disrupts the architecture and function of affected cells leading to multisystemic pathology and ultimately death. In addition to being a lysosomal storage disorder, Pompe disease is also considered a neuromuscular disease, a metabolic myopathy, and a glycogen storage disorder. Pompe disease is an ultra-orphan disease, affecting some 5,000 to 10,000 individuals globally. Pompe disease has been classified into different subtypes based on age at onset of clinical manifestations, extent of organ involvement, and rate of progression to death. Essentially, the disease manifests as a broad clinical spectrum with a continuum of clinical manifestations, ranging from a rapidly progressive infantile-onset form to a more slowly progressive late-onset form with considerable variability and overlap between these 2 extremes . The majority of patients with Pompe disease are classified with the late-onset subtype. Late-onset Pompe patients manifest signs and symptoms of the disease anywhere from early childhood through the 6th decade of life and usually present with slowly progressive myopathy, predominantly of the proximal muscles in the trunk and pelvic and shoulder girdles, and a variable degree of respiratory involvement. While the heart is typically spared, cardiomegaly has been reported to occur in up to 4% of patients with late-onset Pompe disease (Hirschhorn, 2001, The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease) and other cardiac manifestations secondary to chronic respiratory failure have been observed . Initial myopathic signs can be very subtle and may include difficulty combing the hair, rising from a chair, climbing stairs, or rising from a squat. However, over time there is increasing involvement of proximal lower limb, truncal, and upper body muscles, and most patients ultimately become wheelchair bound. Initial respiratory symptoms may be related to sleep apnea and include somnolence and morning headache. As the disease progresses, orthopnea and/or exertional dyspnea develop and many patients eventually require noninvasive or invasive ventilation and ultimately progress to respiratory failure, the leading cause of death in these patients. Alglucosidase alfa has been developed as an enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for the treatment of Pompe disease. Clinical trials have been completed in patients with infantile- and late-onset Pompe disease, thus covering the extremes of severity of the disease spectrum Study Design This is a prospective, open-label, multicenter study of patients ranging from 8 to 18 years of age with Pompe disease who are naÃ¯ve to treatment with alglucosidase alfa. column51: This study is a randomized, double blind, sham controlled trail investigating the effect of neuronavigated- repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) to right inferior parietal lobule (rIPL) on the Schneiderian first rank symptoms (FRS), high resolution gamma oscillatory activity, serum BDNF levels and self monitoring function in schizophrenia. The study would be conducted in two concurrent segments: 1. Assessment of resting state gamma oscillatory activity, serum BDNF levels, self monitoring and minor physical anomalies in the three groups- schizophrenia patients with and without FRS and, healthy controls. 2. Randomization of the schizophrenia patients with FRS into two groups- active and sham. A repeat assessment of FRS, resting state gamma oscillatory activity, serum BDNF levels and self monitoring after completion of rTMS sessions. column51: The present study is an extension study of GENA-05, a study in which the Immunogenicity, Clinical Efficacy & safety of Human-cl rhFVIII in PUPs has been studied. GENA-15 is a prospective, multicentre, multinational, open label, non-controlled, phase-IIIb study with the objective to collect further long term data on the Immunogenicity, Safety & Efficacy of Human-cl rFVIII. Objectives: â€¢ To investigate the immunogenicity of Human-cl rhFVIII in patients who completed GENA-05 in accordance with the study protocol â€¢ To assess the efficacy of Human-cl rhFVIII during prophylactic treatment (based on the frequency of spontaneous break-through bleeds) â€¢ To assess the efficacy of Human-cl rhFVIII during treatment of bleeds â€¢ To assess the efficacy of Human-cl rhFVIII in surgical prophylaxis â€¢ To assess the safety and tolerability of Human-cl rhFVIII Dose and Dosing Schedule Prophylactic treatment is recommended, but finally, it is the decision of the responsible treating physician whether patients will be treated prophylactically or on-demand. Patients may switch from on-demand to prophylactic treatment, or from prophylactic to on-demand treatment during the course of the study. Prophylactic Treatment In case prophylactic treatment is chosen, the patients will be treated with a recommended dose of >20 IU FVIII/kg body weight (BW). The frequency of treatment will depend on the patientâ€™s clinical situation. In cases of inadequate response, Human-cl rhFVIII administration frequency or dose adjustments can be considered at Investigatorâ€™s discretion. On-demand Treatment In case of bleeds, the patients can be treated on-demand. The dosage and duration of treatment of spontaneous or traumatic bleeds depend on the location and the extent of bleeding as well as on the clinical situation of the patient. Dosage recommendations are given as follows: â€¢ Minor haemorrhage (superficial muscle or soft tissue and oral bleeds): 20-30 IU FVIII/kg BW to achieve an intended target peak level of about 40% to 60%. Repeat dose every 8-24 hours until BE is resolved. â€¢ Moderate to major haemorrhage (haemorrhage into muscles, into oral cavity; haemarthrosis, known trauma): 30-40 IU FVIII/kg BW to achieve an intended target peak level of about 60% to 80%. Repeat dose every 6-24 hours until BE is resolved. â€¢ Major to life-threatening haemorrhage (intracranial, intra-abdominal, gastro-intestinal or intrathoracic bleeds, central nervous system bleeds, bleeding in retropharyngeal spaces or iliopsoas sheath, eyes/retina, fractures or head trauma): initial dose of 50-80 IU FVIII/kg BW to achieve an intended target peak level of 100% to 120%. Repeat dose of >20 IU FVIII/kg BW every 6-12 hours until BE is resolved. Surgical Prophylaxis The dosage and duration of treatment with Human-cl rhFVIII will depend on the type of surgery and the patientâ€™s individual incremental recovery. Dosage recommendations are given as follows: â€¢ Minor surgeries including tooth extractions: 25-30 IU FVIII/kg BW starting within 3 hours prior to surgery to achieve an intended target peak level of >30%. Repeat one dose every 12-24 hours if needed. Trough levels should be maintained at â‰¥30%. - Major surgeries: >50 IU FVIII/kg BW within 3 hours prior to surgery to achieve an intended target peak level of approximately 100%. Repeat if necessary after 6-12 hours initially and for at least 6 to 14 days until healing is complete and recurrence to regular prophylactic treatment is possible. Trough levels should be maintained at >50%. Duration of Treatment: The patients are planned to stay in the study until the IMP is registered and launched in the individual countries, or for a maximum period of 2 years from screening, whichever comes first. In any event, the general clinical completion date is scheduled as per 31 December 2018. Study Outcome Parameters / Endpoints): Immunogenicity: Inhibitor activity will be determined by the modified Bethesda assay (Nijmegen modification), using congenital FVIII-deficient human plasma spiked with Human-cl rhFVIII at the following time points: â€¢ At Screening Visit, which can be the same sampling time-point as the completion visit of GENA-05 â€¢ Once every 6 months during the open treatment phase â€¢ At study completion â€¢ Any time in the case of suspicion of inhibitor development. In case of a positive inhibitor result, an inhibitor re-test using a second separately drawn sample should be performed, centrally. Efficacy: Efficacy of prophylactic treatment: The efficacy of Human-cl rhFVIII in the prophylactic treatment will be assessed based on the frequency of spontaneous break-through bleeds under prophylactic treatment. The dates and times of study drug infusions, details of dose(s) and product batch numbers used for the prophylactic treatment will be documented. Details of any BEs occurring under prophylactic treatment will be documented. Study drug consumption data (FVIII IU/kg per month, per year) per patient and in total will be evaluated. Efficacy of treatment of bleeds: The efficacy of Human-cl rhFVIII in the treatment of bleeds will be assessed based on an objective haemostatic efficacy scale. Details of the bleed (type, site and severity of the bleed, and the start and end date and time of the bleed), the amount of Human-cl rhFVIII needed and the number of injections necessary to stop the bleed will be documented. Efficacy of surgical prophylaxis: The efficacy of Human-cl rhFVIII in surgical prophylaxis will be assessed based on: â€¢ Overall efficacy assessment (taking the intra- and post-operative assessment into account) after the end of the surgical prophylactic treatment phase, done together by the surgeon and the haematologist. â€¢ Average and maximum expected estimated blood loss compared to the actual estimated blood loss. In addition, the location, severity, and type of surgery will be documented. Expected and actual duration of surgical procedure and details of administered dose(s) of Human-cl rhFVIII (pre-, intra- and/or post-operatively) will be recorded. FVIII plasma levels (pre-, intra-, and post-operatively) will be measured. Details of concomitantly administered products (except standard anaesthetics) along with a brief narrative describing the outcome of the intervention will be recorded. column51: Fluid retention is a common complication of critical illness, especially in the post-resuscitation phase, and is worsened by hypoalbuminemia, both of which are associated with worse clinical outcomes. Diuretics are often administered with or without albumin in these patients to achieve negative fluid balance. The addition of hypertonic albumin to diuretic therapy is a promising treatment in the post-resuscitation care of critically ill hypoalbuminemic children with fluid overload, based on a strong physiological rationale as albumin promotes redistribution of fluid from edematous peripheral tissues back into the vascular compartment from where the diuretic accelerates its removal by the kineys. However, there is paucity of compelling evidence for the routine use of albumin in this cohort to improve clinical and physiiological outcomes, thus warrenting a randomized control trial. The proposed study is intended to create priliminary evidence on the use of albumin and furosemide for fluid overload as practiced in many PICUs across the world. column51: Cognitive adverse effects of ECT include both ante grade & retro grade amnesia with loss of autobiographical memory, those related to orientation, verbal episodic memory, visual episodic memory, attention, psychomotor speed and executive functions. Recent studies show that by decreasing the pulse width, we can achieve cognitive advantage without compromising in efficacy in depression. Schizophrenia is the most common indication for ECT in Asia and India. No studies have seen the effect of decreasing pulse width in schizophrenia patients. Hence it is need of the hour to study the effects of decreasing pulse width on cognitive adverse effects as well as on efficacy in schizophrenia patients. In this study we aim to compare the short term cognitive adverse effects and the efficacy of 2 pulse widths (0.5 ms & 1.5ms) during Brief pulse ECT in bilateral electrode placement in patients with schizophrenia referred for ECT. And we hypothesize that those receiving 0.5 ms pulse width ECT will have lesser cognitive adverse effects than those receiving 1.5 ms pulse width ECT. column51: Androgenetic alopecia ia a very common hair loss disorder affecting both male and female. The hair loss is a dynamic process in androgenetic alopecia and Norwood Hamilton classification of grading is commonly used in male androgenetic alopecia. The hair loss may cause great psychological distress, low self-esteem in many patients. Platelet rich plasma (PRP) is defined as a volume of the plasma fraction of autologous blood having a platelet concentration above base line.The platelet rich plasma is prepared using different method for platelet concentration through centrifugation and cell separation.The application of autologous PRP has been safely used and documented in many fields including, orthopedics,sports medicine,dentistry,ENT,neurosurgery, ophthalmology,urology, and wound healing; as well as cosmetic, cardiothoracic, and maxillofacial surgery. PRP contains many growth factors which are stored in the alpha granules. The main growth factors are platelet derived growth factor(PDGF), transforming growth factor -b (TGF-b) and vascular endothelial growth factor with their isoform.The growth factor act on bulge area of hair follicle where the stem cells are located. In matrix, germinative cells of mesenchyme origin is found at the dermal papilla. Interaction between these two kind of cells as well as binding of the growth factors activate the proliferative phase of hair,i.e anagen cycle giving rise to the follicular unit. Recently there are many publications showing safety of PRP with variable efficacy in androgenetic alopecia. There is no adverse event reported with use of autologous PRP in the literature. Intradermal injection of autologous PRP is a common procedure widely done as treatment of androgenetic alopecia. However, there is no published randomized double blind placebo controlled study to show its real efficacy and benefit.There are two undergoing trials registered in clinical trials. gov Our study is a randomized double blind ;placebo controlled half head study which will help to generate new knowledge in management of androgenetic alopecia. Randomization was done to which side of scalp the patient will recieve intraderma injection of autologous PRP and itradermal injection of normal saline. All the patients were treated with minoxidil 5% lotion which is a standard care in androgenetic alopecia. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: The study will be conducted in 2 parts, Part I and Part II. Part I of the study is a Phase II multi-center, randomized, open label clinical study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Insulin Tregopil (2 dose levels: 30 mg, 45 mg) compared with IAsp in the treatment of T2DM patients. Part II of the study is the Phase III, multi-center, randomized, open label clinical study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Insulin Tregopil (30 mg or 45 mg based upon the outcome of Part I data) compared with IAsp in the treatment of T2DM patients. For Part I and Part II, the study duration will be approximately 37 weeks (3 weeks Screening, 8 weeks Run-in, 24 weeks Treatment, 2 weeks Safety follow-up). An Independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will evaluate the data from Part I of the study. column51: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune syndrome involving antibody- and cell-mediated destruction of platelets and suppression of platelet production by the bone marrow (BM) megakaryocytes that may predispose to bleeding. Romiplostim is a novel thrombopoiesis stimulating protein that has been developed as a treatment for adults with thrombocytopenia associated with ITP. Romiplostim provides an effective approach for the treatment of ITP. Romiplostim has been approved globally including US, EU, Canada, Australia etc since 2008. Romiplostim has not yet approved in India. Intas Pharmaceuticals has developed biosimilar Romiplostim, which is similar to Innovatorâ€™s product in terms for chemical and preclinical characteristics. Efficacy and safety of Romiplostim manufactured by Intas Pharmaceuticals Ltd has already proven in Indian population in a phase III clinical study. Aim of the current study is to evaluate pharmacokinetics of Romiplostim in Indian population. It is a Prospective, Assessor-blind, Randomized, Parallel group clinical study. The present study will be carried out to generate pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and safety data from 24adult patients (12 patients per arm) of both the genders aged 18 to 65 years (both inclusive) years with chronic refractory ITP at different clinical sites across India. Adult patients of both the genders with chronic refractory ITP will be screened for Inclusion/Exclusion criteria. The study will consist of a 1 week of screening period, dosing on day 0 and 4 weeks of follow-up period. Patients will be screened for eligibility over 1 week period. Physical examination, vital signs, and laboratory testing will be performed at the screening visit. All patients will be given 3 mcg/kg dose of Romiplostim on day 0. Total 25 blood samples (3 mL each) will be collected for pharmacokinetic assessment. Total 7 blood samples will be collected for pharmacodynamics assessment. Pharmacodynamic assessment will be performed at central lab using standard validated method. column51: There is no universally accepted dosing regimen of Rituximab in pemphigus and studies have found comparable efficacy of low dose Rituximab with the conventional dose used. column51: Menstruation is a natural event as a part of the normal process of reproductive life in females. Due to todayâ€™s sedentary lifestyle and lack of exercise, dysmenorrhoea is becoming todayâ€™s burning problem throughout the world. Dysmenorrhoea is defined as painful menstruation so as incapacitate day to day activities. Primary dysmenorrhoea is one where there is no identifiable pelvic pathology and secondary dysmenorrhoea is one where there is presence of pelvic pathology.In Ayurveda classics Kashtartava (Dysmenorrhoea) is not described as a separate disease but as a symptom in different diseases like Yonivyapad and Artavadusti. Hence, this study is particular about the description of Kashtartava explained in scattered classical references.As per Ayurveda classics, pain occurs in any part of the body is due to aggravation of Vata dosha. For this, the main two reasons are obstruction in the passage (Margavarodha) and depletion of body tissues (Dhatukshaya). Considering the symptomatology and etiological factors Kashtartava can be compared with primary dysmenorrhoea.Conventional medical treatment may relieve symptoms of dysmenorrhoea but it does not address the root of the problem. In modern dysmenorrhoea is treated by hormones, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, antispasmodic, analgesics etc. Long term use of these causes side effects like hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, headache, dizziness, vertigo, depression, skin rashes etc.So to minimize these complications, an attempt is made to find solution of this problem. column51: Transcranial direct current stimulation is a non invasive neuromodulatory technique whose role is being currently explored in recent studies from western countries, among subjects with nicotine dependence to test its effect on reducing craving to smoke and reduction in the number of cigarettes smoked.The current study is a randomised, single blind, parallel group sham controlled trial with primary objective to evaluate the effect of Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) on tobacco craving among 30 opioid dependent adult male smokers who have been stabilised on Tablet Buprenorphine for opioid dependence for at least 3 months. The study will be conducted at National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC) and Community clinics of NDDTC. The primary outcomes that will be measured in this study are 1) Baseline tobacco craving by Brief Questionnaire of Smoking Urges and 2),. Cue induced tobacco craving by Visual Analog Scale. The secondary objectives of the study are 1) To find the effect of tDCS on cigarette/beedi consumption among opioid dependent smokers maintained on Buprenorphine maintenance for at least 3 months and 2) To find the association of socio-demographic data and clinical parameters like severity of nicotine dependence, motivation to stop smoking, etc. with change in craving and tobacco consumption due to tDCS among opioid dependent smokers maintained on Buprenorphine maintenance for at least 3 months. Socio demographic data will be assessed using semi-structured proforma. Severity of nicotine dependence will be assessed using Fagerstromâ€™s test for nicotine dependence. column51: Pemphigus vulgaris is a chronic autoimmune muco-cutaneous blistering disease which presents as a dermatological emergency as it predisposes to widespread secondary infection and sepsis, thermal dysregulation, electrolyte imbalance and even death. Treatment of pemphigus vulgaris remains a challenge because of the chronic, persistent nature and high rate of disease recurrence. Dexamethasone pulse therapy has been the mainstay of treatment for PV in India with long term remissions, cost-effective and a good safety profile. However, certain limitations such as long duration of supervised treatment (1-2 years) left scope for an alternative treatment with better efficacy in shorter time with fewer side effects. Rituximab is anti CD 20 monoclonal antibody and has been successfully used as intravenous infusion to treat recalcitrant pemphigus vulgaris, with good safety profile and clinical remission rates approaching 75%. We propose to compare clinical efficacy of the standard pulse therapy with rituximab treatment, safety profile of the two regimens and cost-effectiveness between the two regimens in a randomized trial. In addition, we also propose to compare changes in various biochemical and immunological parameters both in skin and blood during different periods of disease activity to assess efficacy of the two regimens and predict disease relapse. These biomarkers will help us in identification of patients at risk of relapse to avoid unnecessary infusions and significant cost savings. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Atypical Haemolytic Uraemic Syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, genetic, progressive and life threatening disease which results from uncontrolled activation of the complement system leading to thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) and subsequently severe renal damage, loss of kidney function and sometimes death. The current standard of care in India is plasma exchange or plasma infusion, dialysis, and kidney transplantation. A humanized monoclonal antibody which inhibits the complement system by binding on C5 molecule has shown to be effective in the treatment of aHUS and has been approved for the treatment of aHUS in many countries globally since 2011 but is not available to patients in India currently. Eculizumab has been shown to improve the morbidity and mortality in aHUS patients significantly. rVA576 is a naturally derived compound (from tick saliva) that also acts as a complement inhibitor but binds to different site domain on C5 molecule. It is designed to be self-administered via a daily subcutaneous injection. The current standard of care in India for aHUS treatment is plasma exchange and dialysis. These treatment options are associated with significant morbidity and mortality and a complement inhibitor therapy has potential to change the treatment pathway for aHUS patients in India. column51: Psoriasis is an immune mediated genetically determined common dermatological disorder which affects skin, nails, joints and has various systemic associations. There is a growing number of population-based studies providing worldwide prevalence estimates of psoriasis. Prevalence of psoriasis varies in different parts of the world. According to published reports, prevalence in different populations varies from 0% to 11.8%. For most of the data given, the range extends from around 0.5% to close to 2.5%. In the USA, the prevalence of psoriasis was estimated to be around 4.6% while in Canada it was 4.7%. Data from Europe show little variation in countries with a range from 1.4% (Norway), 1.55% (Croatia) and 1.6% (UK). In East Africa, the figure was 0.7% and in the Henan district of China only 0.7% were found affected. Adalimumab is the first fully human, high-affinity, recombinant immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) anti-TNF monoclonal antibody. Adalimumab was created using phage display technology resulting in an antibody with human derived heavy and light chain variable regions and human IgG1:k constant regions. Adalimumab is produced by recombinant DNA technology in a mammalian cell expression system and is purified by a process that includes specific viral inactivation and removal steps. Because it is indistinguishable in structure and function from naturally occurring human IgG1, adalimumab has high selectivity and affinity for TNF; suitability for long-term chronic administration with a low degree of immunogenicity, with or without concomitant methotrexate (MTX) use; a low incidence of allergic reactions; and a half-life comparable to that of IgG1, allowing every-other-week dosing for patient convenience. column51: A prospective, randomized, open-label, controlled, clinical study to compare the clinical efficacy and tolerability of two highly purified human menopausal gonadotropin preparations administered subcutaneously in women undergoing in vitro fertilization. Primary Objective: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of two different highly purified (HP) human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG) preparations (GynogenÂ® HP and MenopurÂ®), when administered subcutaneously (s.c.) to female patients undergoing controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) for in vitro fertilization (IVF) on oocyte maturation and retrieval. Secondary Objective: To evaluate additional clinical efficacy, tolerability, and safety of two different HP-hMG preparations (GynogenÂ® HP and MenopurÂ®), when administered s.c. to female patients undergoing COS for IVF. This is a multicentre, prospective, randomized, open-label, controlled, parallel-group trial. The purpose of this non-inferiority study is to compare the clinical efficacy and general tolerability of two different HP-hMG preparations (GynogenÂ®HP; Sanzyme Pvt. Ltd. and MenopurÂ®, Ferring Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) when administered s.c. to female patients undergoing COS for IVF. column51: Background: Intra-articular (IA) infiltrations with platelet-rich plasma (PRP) are showing promising results in the treatment of OA Knee. IA infiltration only targets articular cartilage and synovial membrane without reaching subchondral-bone. Adding intra-osseous (IO) injections to target subchondral bone can provide more comprehensive treatment in OA Knee. Novelty: Study will be valuable in establishing affectivity of IO+IA-PRP injection and investigating several biomarkers, pertinent to various pathways of the OA process and ultrasonography findings after PRP infiltrations in OA. Objectives: To evaluate the changes in severity of pain after IO+IA-PRP and IA-PRP treatment in Knee OA, to analyze the changes in the concentration of biomarkers of cartilage turnover and inflammation in serum and urine and to explore the relationship (if any) between clinical findings, biological biomarkers, ultrasonography abnormalities after PRP injections. Methods: After obtaining informed consent, persons with painful OA Knee with 40-65 years age, will be randomly allocated into 3 groups. Persons in Group-I will receive 18 ml of IO+IA-PRP injection, in group-II, will receive 8 ml of IA-PRP injection and persons in group-III will receive a total of 8 ml of 0.9% IA-NS injection. VAS, KOOS and urinary and serum biomarkers of cartilage-turnover (u-CTX-II, u-NTX, s-COMP, s-PIIANP) and inflammation (ESR, hsCRP, s-HA) and ultrasonography of the knee joints will be assessed at the baseline visit, 6 and 12 weeks post-intervention. Expected Outcomes: The study will enable us to determine whether IO+IA-PRP injection is more or equally effective than IA-PRP injection and to find-out whether biomarkers and ultrasonography changes after PRP intervention can be used as predictive marker of OA progression. column51: PlatePlatelet rich plasma (PRP) is an effective concentration of multiple fundamental growth factors stored in the alpha-granules of platelets. These growth factors are platelet derived growth factors (PDGF), vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGF), transforming growth factor beta (TGF Î²) and Endostatin etc. Now a days PRP is becoming a very effective tool in regenerative medicine. Androgenetic alopecia is a progressive disorder of hair thinning and hair loss mediated by polygenetically inherited sensitivity to dihydrotestosterone. This metabolite of testosterone miniaturizes hair follicles by shortening the anagen (growth) phase and lengthening the telogen (resting) phase of the hair cycle. Periorbital hyperpigmentation (POH) is a common facial disorder of pigmentation. It is most commonly seen in young females. Etiological factors involved are hereditary, postinflammatory hyperpigmentation following allergic contact dermatitis, latanoprost eyedrops, atopy, ultraviolet radiation, stress, and excessive vascularity. Both the above mentioned conditions are difficult to treat with the conventional treatments available. PRP therapy has shown some good improvements in both AGA and POH. Conventionally PRP is made by the double spin method and activated by adding calcium. This conventional method is time consuming. We are introducing a new simplified method in which PRP is prepared by single spin method and activated by just chilling and not adding any other agent like calcium. A total of 45 patients will be selected who are suffering from AGA or POH. It will be a split scalp and face trial. One half of scalp or face will be injected with PRP prepared by conventional double spin method and activated by calcium. The other half will be injected with PRP prepared by single spin method and activated by chilling. total 3 injections will be given at an interval of 1 month. Assessment will be done by dermoscopy and clinical photography. Some part of PRP will be cryopreserved and will be analyzed for the growth factors like PDGF, VEGF, TGF and endostatin by ELISA. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: 20-30% schizophrenia (SCZ) patients struggle with auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) minimally responsive to pharmaceutical treatments. Add-on fronto-temporoparietal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is suggested to address persistent AVH in SCZ patients. High heterogeneity among existing randomized control trials for AVH treatment in SCZ and lack of empirical studies investigating tDCS action mechanism warrants a systematic investigation into the mechanistic basis of tDCS action. This study proposes and examines the brainâ€™s neuroplasticity potential as biological phenomena driving treatment effects of tDCS. Using a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled parallel-arm, pre-post design, changes in neuroplasticity potential with tDCS treatment for AVH in SCZ will be assessed. The four composite primary outcome measures of this study are: 1) changes in N100-derived event-related-potential waveforms (neurophysiological), 2) changes glutamine-glutamate levels (neurochemical), 3) changes in resting-state functional connectivity (neuroimaging), and 4) reduction in AVH severity (clinical). column51: Landry Guillain Barre Syndrome (LGBS) is a common cause of Acute Flaccid Paralysis (AFP) in children. The first description of this syndrome of ascending paralysis was given by Jean Baptiste Octave Landry in 1859. He described a disease of ascending weakness with or without sensory alterations in 5 of his patients and another 5 cases from literature. The entity was called Landry Paralysis until Guillain, Barre and Strohl published their findings in 1916 and described a syndrome of ascending paralysis with areflexia and the characteristic CSF picture of raised protein in the absence of cellular response. Since then, much has been published about this disease, but it remains an enigma. The global incidence of LGBS is about 1.3 (0.4-4.0) / 100000 population. The incidence varies marginally with regions. In Europe, it is about 1.2-1.9/100000 population while in China it is much less at 0.66/100000 population. There is a bimodal age distribution with a peak in late adolescence and early adulthood, and a second, bigger peak in the elderly. Mortality from LGBS in different studies has been reported to be between 3-13%. We have come a long way in understanding the pathophysiological basis of LGBS although it still remains an area of active research. It has been established that it is an immune mediated peripheral neuropathy. There are at least four recognised variants â€“ Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP), Acute Motor Axonal Neuropathy (AMAN), Acute Motor Sensory Axonal Neuropathy (AMSAN) and the Miller-Fisher Syndrome (MFS). AIDP is likely a T-cell mediated attack on the myelin proteins while the other three are antibody mediated. About a quarter of LGBS patients have evidence of a pre-existing Campylobacter jejuni infection which could be explained by cross-reacting antibodies and molecular mimicry. There seem to be some differences in the adult and pediatric patients with regard to presentation, course and prognosis of the illness. Children seem to have a lower incidence of sensory and cranial nerve involvement, lower time from onset to nadir of weakness and a higher incidence of pain. Before data emerged on the immunological nature of the disease, the care of these patients was primarily supportive. As most patients showed gradual recovery of neurological power, it was classified as a self-limiting disorder. Even with supportive care, a large portion of the patients had residual weakness and suffered prolonged hospital stays. With emergence of immunological basis of the disease, various forms of immunomodulatory therapies were tried. Corticosteroids were the first to be tried in 1952. Subsequent studies in adults have revealed little to no benefit of their use and thus they are no more recommended. Therapeutic Plasma exchange (TPE) was used for the first time in polyneuropathy in 1978. Subsequent large RCTs in adult patients demonstrated that TPE was an effective therapy for LGBS when used early in the course of the disease. Those undergoing TPE had shorter time to improve one clinical grade, shorter time to independent walking and better mobility at 6 months follow up. Intravenous Immunoglobulins (IvIg) are a relatively recent therapeutic strategy for LGBS. In 1988 a study on 8 adult patients with LGBS reported some clinical benefit. Subsequent trials demonstrated similar efficacy to TPE which was considered the gold standard therapy. TPE is considered to infer a greater risk of adverse events. These concerns, however, have never been replicated in any clinical trials. The safety of plasma exchange, even in children, has been well established. Western as well as Indian studies have found plasma exchange to be more cost effective when compared to IvIg. There have been only two studies which have compared plasma exchange and IvIg in LGBS in children. Out of these, only one is a randomized control trial (RCT) while the other is a retrospective data analysis. Both these studies concluded that the children with LGBS treated with plasma exchange had a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation and hospital stay as compared to those treated with IvIg, but the results were not significant enough to propose a change in practice. Robust data on the comparative effect of these two therapeutic strategies is lacking. Considering the significant clinical benefit and cost effectiveness of plasma exchange over IvIg in children with LGBS with an established safety record, we feel that a study is worthwhile in this regard. Thus, we hypothesize that, TPE, when used early in the course of LGBS in children, irrespective of severity of the disease, is better than IvIg in terms of reducing the duration of mechanical ventilation of these children. Our study will be an open label, prospective randomized control trial, that will add high quality data to the quest for finding the most efficacious therapy for LGBS in children. column51: This is a comparative study to investigate the effect of Vamana Karma and Triphala Churna and Guduchi Churna with Madhu on the gut microbiota and metabolite patterns in Prameha W.S.R to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Healthy Individuals as well as to compare the effect of Vamana Karma followed by administration of Triphala Churna and Guduchi Churna with Madhu and administration of Only Triphala Churna and Guduchi Churna with Madhu in the patients of Prameha W.S.R Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Diet and lifestyle modification being an integral part of Vamana Karma(therapeutic emesis for internal bio-cleansing) may lead to the modification of environmental microflora in a positive aspect for shaping the healthy human microbiota composition thus leading to the state of wellness. This whole information gives a lead that Vamana therapy aims at modulating the gut functioning and thereby restoring the state of homeostasis, improving digestion and metabolism in turn proved to be an effective treatment modality in many diseased conditions like Rheumatoid arthritis, skin disease, Type 2 diabetes mellitus, allergic conditions etc. Therefore, this study can investigate the role of classical Vamana therapy as described in Ayurveda by showing its impact in the modulation of dysbiosis and hence it can emerge as a proven modality of treatment in variety of metabolic, immune mediated, neuropsychiatric and musculo-skeletal diseased conditions. The study contains the following three groups- Group 1- Prameha Patients (Vamana Karma followed by Triphala and Guduchi Churna with madhu)- 15 subjects Group 2- Prameha Patients (Administration of only Triphala and Guduchi Churna with madhu)- 15 subjects Group 3 - Healthy Individuals (Vamana Karma followed by Triphala and Guduchi Churna with madhu)- 15 subjects The above mentioned three groups have been taken with an objective to compare the effect of Vamana Karma followed by Triphala Churna and Guduchi Churna with Madhu and administration of only Triphala Churna and Guduchi Churna with Madhu in the patients of Prameha W.S.R to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with respect to change in Sign and symptoms, Plasma Glucose Level and gut Microbiota and metabolite patterns i.e Group 1 and Group 2. Is there any difference in the impact of classical Vamana Karma followed by Triphala and Guduchi Churna with Madhu on the alteration of Gut Microbiota diversity and metabolite patterns in the patients of Prameha(T2DM) and healthy individuals as well as in the administration of direct Triphala and Guduchi Churna with Madhu in the patients of Prameha(T2DM) only. column51: Intervention / Procedure: Procedure performed by a single operator. The patientsâ€™ will be explained about the surgical procedures (Appendix I) and the possible outcomes in their vernacular language as well as written informed consent (Appendix II) shall be obtained. The demographic data of all the subjects will be recorded on the customized case history proforma (Appendix III). The study will be conducted in patients with single or multiple Millerâ€™s class I gingival recession defects. Clinical parameters like recession height (RH), the distance from the CEJ to gingival margin, recession width (RW), meiso-distal diameter at the CEJ, probing sulcus depth (PD), clinical attachment level (CAL), the sum of recession depth and probing depth, and width of keratinized tissue (KTW) i.e., distance from marginal gingiva to the mucogingival junction will be assessed. In case of semilunar coronally repositioned flap, a semilunar incision, will be given following the curvature of the free gingival margin. The incision will curve apically far enough mid facially to ensure that the apical part of the flap rests on bone after it is brought down to cover the exposed root. Incision will end into the papillae on each end of the tooth, but not all the way to the tip of the papillae, at least 2 mm will be left on either side of the flap. Using a 15c blade, split thickness dissection will be made from the initial incision line coronally, connected with an intrasulcular incision made mid facially. Mid facial tissue will be then coronally positioned to the CEJ or to the height of adjacent papillae in case of interproximal recession. Tissue will be held in place against the tooth with moist gauze for 5 min. In case of pin hole surgical technique, a minimal horizontal incision of 2 to 3mm will be made in the alveolar mucosa near the base of the vestibule apical to recipient site. Specially designed instruments [Transmucosal periosteal elevators right and left] are inserted through the entry of incision to elevate full thickness flap and will be guided by visualization of the shape and movement of the instruments through the mucosa and gingival tissue. This interproximal extension of the flap will result in a freely movable flap, which will be then positioned coronally to extend beyond the CEJ. column51: A AIMS: The proposed study aims to gain insights into the biology of this rare but aggressive cancer and identify clinically relevant molecular sub-classification of PABC through comprehensive genomic analysis and detailed clinicopathological and treatment outcome correlation. METHODOLOGY: All women who present with breast cancer during the pregnancy or within 1 year of delivery will be enrolled in the ongoing PABC registry with their informed consent for biobanking and OMICS analysis. Demographic and other health details, menstrual and obstetric history, prior use of hormonal agents and concomitant medication will be recorded. They will undergo standard clinical, pathological, and staging investigations (avoiding ionizing radiation) for breast cancer and evaluation of the pregnancy as per the gestational age. All cases will be jointly evaluated by a multi-disciplinary oncology team and obstetricians if the pregnancy is continuing. Clinical and histological annotation of the tumor sample for histological type, grade, ER, PR, HER2Neu, and Ki67 FISH will be done if HER2Neu IHC is equivocal. They will receive treatment for breast cancer as appropriate for the disease characteristics, stage, and gestational age. As pregnancy is associated with young age, all PABC cases will refer to the Cancer Genetics Clinic for evaluation by the Cancer Genetics Team. Based on age at breast cancer diagnosis, family history of cancer, and other features such as bilateral breast cancer or TNBC, the possibility of inherited predisposition to cancer from a germline mutation in a cancer-predisposing gene will be considered. After detailed pre-test genetic counseling and consent, they will be offered germline genetic testing for BRCA1/BRCA2 or targeted next generation sequencing as appropriate for the syndromic differential diagnosis. For OMICS characterization, the study will be undertaken on the tumor, adjacent normal breast tissue and blood sample in two phases â€“ the discovery set and the validation set. Patient Cohorts: We will recruit patients in two cohorts: the Discovery cohort and validation cohort. Each cohort will include 50 patients, for a total study population of 100 patients. We are accounting for a 50% attrition rate due to quality control check failure for OMICS assays, thus actual assays will be carried out on only 25 patients from both cohorts. If any OMICS capable samples exceed 25 patients in any cohort, we will consider using the samples for our study, provided we have funding available to carry out these assays. For the discovery cohort, comprehensive OMICS analysis on the DNA and RNA extracted from the tumor, adjacent breast, and blood will be undertaken in 25 PABC Cases. Omics data from 25 matched controls â€“ non-pregnancy associated breast cancer matched for age, Â± 3 years, stage and ER/PR/Her2 will be used from pre-existing studies where data is freely available and patients have already consented to use of their data for research purposes (eg. TCGA study, ICGC study, other TMH studies where Omics data is generated). The key genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic alterations identified in the PABC discovery cohort will be evaluated in the validation set of 25 PABC cases enrolled in the registry and for whom FFPE Â± fresh tumor is available. The cases and controls will be recruited from among the patients attending TMC for their breast cancer management. They will be recruited as part of a prospective IRB approved the PABC registry study if they provide written informed consent. A) Discovery Cohort: From each case in the prospective discovery cohort, we will collect, Tumour adjacent normal breast tissue, and Tumour tissue, either from the primary site, or most accessible metastatic site (including skin, subcutaneous lining, lymph node, liver, lung, abdominal or pleural effusion). A routine core biopsy or image-guided biopsy from the site of the local tumor or metastatic the site, to collect tumor tissue (including lymph nodes, subcutaneous tissue, other breasts, lung, liver, or fluid in abdominal or pleural cavity) would be performed. This will be compared with the historical matched controls (as described above in the methodology section) from pre-existing studies where data is freely available and patients have already consented to the use of their data for research purposes (eg. TCGA study, ICGC study, other TMH studies where Omics data is generated). Â· We will collect 10 ml blood in Pax Gene tubes to use as control normal tissue for identifying somatic alterations in tumor tissue. Â· Exome sequencing will be done for paired tumor /stroma/ blood samples for 25 PABC cases. Â· Transcriptome analysis will be done on paired tumor and stroma for 25 PABC cases Epigenetic assays (methylation) will be done on paired tumor and normal tissue for 25 PABC cases. B) Validation Cohort: Key genetic alterations identified in the discovery set, will be validated in the existing cohorts of 25 PABC patients. The genetic alterations identified in the PABC discovery cohort will be evaluated in the validation set of 25 PABC cases enrolled in the exiting PABC registry (TMC Project No:1722) and for whom FFPE Â± fresh tumor is available. Methodology for Exome, Transcriptome, and Epigenetic (Methylation) profiling analysis: Exome Sequencing: Exome sequencing will be carried out by a service provider either on Illumina or other validated NGS platform. The sequence data generated per run will be evaluated by FASTQC Ver. 0.10.1. Sequence reads will be mapped to 1000 Genomes phase 2 reference sequence using BWA v0.6.1. Following alignment, the generated. sai files will be used to create.sam (sequence alignment map) file. Reads that map to multiple regions of the human genome or to decoy sequences will be identified and removed. Duplicate reads will be filtered out using the PICARD 1.60 software. Base quality recalibration, local realignment around indels using known SNPs will be performed with GATK v. 1.4. Alignment SAM files will be converted to BAM files using Samtools 0.1.12a. BAM files were converted to pileup format by SAMtools for variant calling. Somatic base-pair substitutions will be called using GATK. We will identify driver genes that are significantly mutated by statistically comparing the observed numbers of mutations to the numbers expected to accumulate if the genes are evolving at background mutation rate (BMR). These calculations will be carried out using Genome MuSiC package, Ver. 0.4. PathScan module in GenomeMuSiC package will be used to discover significant pathways enriched with somatic mutations in annotated KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes) pathways. We will use a combination of three states of the art structural variation detection tools, namely - 1) CREST [Clipping REvealsSTructure], 2) Breakdancer and 3) Geometric Analysis of Structural Variants (GASV) to identify structural variations including inter-chromosomal translocations, intra-chromosomal translocation, inversion, deletion, and insertions. To detect CNVs, the genome sequence will be divided into fixed-base windows and the average coverage depth was calculated for each window. The window size will be set to be 100bp in the study. We will carry out simulations for varying length windows. The relative coverage depth will be defined as the ratio between the average window coverage and the median of the average window coverage on a set of reference chromosomes that have no gross CNVs based on chromosome-by-chromosome paired tumor/normal coverage analysis. The difference of the relative coverage depth between the tumor sample and its matching normal sample will be corrected for the GC content of the window and used as the signal for calling CNVs. RNA-Seq: RNA extracted from patient tumors treated will be extracted from the cells as previously described. RNA will be subjected to whole transcriptome sequencing on a next-generation sequencing platform as previously described. Libraries for RNA Sequencing will be prepared following the manufacturerâ€™s instructions (Illumina True-Seq RNA Sample Preparation Kit). Briefly, the steps include: random fragmentation of RNA, conversion to double-stranded cDNA, repair of the overhang ends resulting from fragmentation into blunt ends, and ligation of adapters. Libraries will be amplified using PCR. Fragment sizes will be validated with Bioanalyzer (Agilent) using High Sensitivity Kit or the Tape station High Sensitivity assay. KAPPA SyBr Green Assays for qPCR (ABI 7900HT) will be used for library quantification. Paired-end sequencing on HiSeq 4000 (Illumina) platform with 150 bp read length will be performed. At least 30 million x 2 100-bp long PE Reads per sample will be sequenced for a total of 60 million 150-bp reads. The quality of the raw sequence reads will be determined using FastQC. Bioinformatics Data Generation: The tuxedo suite pipeline comprising of Bowtie version 0.12.8, Tophat version 2.06, Cufflinks version 2.02, and Cuffdiff version 2.02 will be used for data generation as described by Trapnel and Roberts et al. Differential gene expression will be identified. Statistically significant differentially expressed genes will be determined on the basis of the statistical significance criteria for each gene as specified by Cuffdiff. Epigenetic Profiling: We will carry out genome-wide methylation profiling for the same set of samples on which RNA-Seq studies will be carried out using high definition methylation arrays. This will allow us to correlate the effect of these methylation patterns on gene expression. Briefly, genomic DNA will be extracted from tumor samples and the extracted DNA will be subjected to sodium bisulfite modification using Epitect Bisulfite Modification kit (Qiagen). Bisulfite-treated DNA will be fluorescently labeled and hybridized to Illumina 450K methylation arrays and the intensities of methylated and unmethylated probes will be measured. The obtained data will be processed using a mini package for various operations such as quality assessment, background error correction and type I and type II probe normalizations, normalize the data across samples, conversion of raw intensity values to beta values, mapping the probes to the human genome (hg19) and the differentially methylated positions between both the conditions will be fetched. Further, a bump hunter package will be used to fetch the differentially methylated regions (DMRs). Gene selection from these DMRs will be carried out as described. An F-test will be performed across all hormone-resistant and sensitive samples to identify genes with a significant difference in beta values between these conditions. Since the empirical p-values are generally calculated genome-wide, adjustment for multiple testing will be done. Rather than using a Bonferroni correction, which is very stringent, the p-values will be transformed into q-values, which are measures of significance in terms of the false discovery rate (FDR). Q-values are computed from the empirical p-values using the Benjamin and Hochberg correction. Probes with q-values less than 0.05 are deemed statistically significant and will be included in the final gene list. These analyses will be carried out using R version 2.11.1 We will try to ensure maximum overlap between these 25 patients; however, this cannot be guaranteed since each assay requires a certain amount of tumor tissue (eg: exome sequencing requires 1 mg of tissue, transcriptome will require 0.5 mg of tissue etc.) Genomic profiling: It has been very well established that cancer is a genetic disease, caused by changes in the genomic makeup of normal cells which results in an aberrant protein that leads to a transformed cellular phenotype. Multiple studies over the years have illustrated these genomic changes and aberrant proteins can be countered by drugs, with many of these drugs having USFDA authorization to treat patients. These drugs have changed treatment paradigms in many cancers, especially in breast cancer where Trastuzumab, Alpesilib, CDK inhibitors and PARP inhibitors are just a few of the therapeutics that are approved as targeted therapy. Based on this current knowledge of cancer genetics, we hypothesized that the genetic and cellular makeup of breast cancer during pregnancy may be different from that of breast cancer without pregnancy, and may open up new avenues for novel targeted therapeutics. Our study thus aims to characterize the genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic makeup of pregnancy-associated breast cancer (PABC), which has not been previously characterized optimally, and compare the same with breast cancer in women without pregnancy. In doing so, we hope to establish the genomic landscape of PABC that can inform us about novel therapeutic avenues and prognostic indicators. BENEFITS: The study could provide new molecular and biological insights on the etiopathogenesis and behavior of PABC and provide translational leads for targeted drug development and biomarkers which can potentially help future patients and care givers and hence this is worth despite no direct medical the benefit to the participants. STATISTICAL METHODS AND ANALYTICAL PLAN: The statistical analysis will be performed to filter the genes differentially expressed between experimental and control arms. The conventional t-test will be adopted. The family wise error rate will be counted to avoid the multiple testing errors. Further, the genes will be filtered based on differently expressed values between experimental and control arms. Filtered genes will be further considered in validating cohort study. column51: Benralizumab is a humanised, afucosylated, monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to the human interlukin-5 (IL-5) receptor alpha subunit (IL-5RÎ±) of target cells such as eosinophils and basophils (Takatsu et al, 1994; Toba et al, 1999; Pelaia et al, 2020). Interlukin-5, major pro-inflammatory cytokine, binds to IL-5R and results in an increased eosinophilic recruitment and activation resulting in airway inflammation (Takatsu et al, 1994; Toba et al, 1999; Pelaia et al, 2020). Targeting IL-5R by monoclonal antibodies such as benralizumab is a novel way to decrease eosinophilic airway inflammation (GINA, 2020). Severe eosinophilic asthma accounts for over 50% of cases with severe asthma, and is associated with increased disease severity, exacerbation frequency, and decreased lung function (Pavord, 2013; Walford et al, 2014; Gonzalez et al, 2019). Current guidelines recommend the addition of anti-IL-5 therapies such as mepolizumab or reslizumab or anti-IL-5 receptor therapy such as benralizumab for patients with severe eosinophilic asthma (GINA, 2020). Benralizumab was approved as an add-on maintenance treatment for patients of severe asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype by the United States (US) Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in November 2017 (for those aged 12 years and older) (FasenraÂ® [benralizumab] United Stated Prescribing Information [USPI], 2017), and by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in January 2018 (for adult patients) (FasenraTM [benralizumab] Summary of Product Characteristics [SmPC], 2019). As on August 2020 it has been approved in 58 countries. Benralizumab was generally well tolerated by patients in clinical trials, with no apparent safety concerns. This study shall be conducted at 10 centers across India. column51: Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) is the term used for a group of retinal dystrophies that are characterized by inherited, progressive degeneration of outer retinal layer primarily photoreceptors and bipolar cells. Visual impairment begins with night blindness and progresses to complete blindness over a period of time. Mutations in more than 240 genes are known to cause retinitis pigmentosa and related retinal dystrophies. It affects 1 in 3000-8000 people worldwide. column51: Smokeless tobacco (ST) is consumed by more than 300 million people worldwide. column51: Methods Proposed to be Used in the Thesis & Plan of Study and Techniques To Be Employed: describe procedure/material-method in brief BONE DONOR: Patient selection: Adequate number of patients will be selected from the Department of Orthopaedics, Institute of Medical Sciences, Banaras Hindu University based on the following inclusion and exclusion criteria, for procurement of bone for allograft preparation. Inclusion Criteria: Patients who have signed the informed consent. Patients undergoing femoral head resection as a part of their surgical protocol. Exclusion Criteria: Under aged donor (<18 years of age). Active or recent systemic infection or sepsis. Tested positive for infection with HIV(by ELISA), Hepatitis B virus(HBsAg), Hepatitis C virus, Treponema pallidum(VDRL). Recent (<4 weeks) vaccination with live vaccine (measles, yellow fever, mumps, polio, oral typhoid, rubella). Diffuse connective tissue disorders, autoimmune diseases or metabolic disorders. Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, systemic hypertension. History of chronic neurological disorders, treatment with growth hormones, chronic medication (especially corticosteroids). Active malignancies, radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Donor location has been exposed to radiation. Language barrier or when patient does not understand the information for any reason (e.g. psychiatric patients). Consent: Bilingual written consent will be received from the patient prior to the procedure. Procedure: The femoral head or its part will be resected by the orthopedic surgeon as a part of surgical protocol. The resected bone will be collected from orthopedician. Then, the bones will be disinfected, cleaned, washed thoroughly, defatted, processed and sterilized to make a human bone allograft. Sinus Lift: Patient Selection: Adequate number of patients will be selected from Outpatient Department (OPD) of Prosthodontics and Crown and Bridge unit of Faculty of Dental Sciences, Institute of Medical Sciences, Banaras Hindu University for the proposed study who are in need of tooth or teeth replacement in the posterior maxilla. This selection will be done after getting personal history, medical and dental history followed by proper intra-oral, extra-oral and radiographic evaluations of the edentulous areas or areas in posterior maxilla. Inclusion Criteria: Patients who have signed the informed consent. Patient who are cooperative, motivated and with good oral hygiene. Patients who want implant retained prosthesis in edentulous posterior area of Maxilla with less than 5mm residual ridge height as detected by the radiograph. Patients with no signs and symptoms of maxillary sinus study. Patients who are non-smokers. Exclusion Criteria: Patients with acute rhinosinuitis, oroantral fistula. Patient who had previously received bone graft on the site to be operated. Tested positive for infection with HIV(by ELISA), Hepatitis B virus(HBsAg), Hepatitis C virus. Patient taking intranasal medications. Patients with uncontrolled systemic diseases (diabetes mellitus, hypertension). Patients with autoimmune disorder, recent myocardian infraction. Patient with bleeding or coagulation disorder. Active malignancies, radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Consent: Bilingual written consent will be received from the patient prior to the procedure. Radiographic Examination: Cone beam computed tomography/ Dentascan will be done to evaluate the maxillary sinus and bone quality and quantity of residual ridge in the posterior edentulous maxilla and decide the size and postion of implant. Clinical Procedure: Antibiotic prophylaxis with Amoxicillin and Clavulanate is prescribed 1hour before surgery. Local anesthesia is given with 2% Lignocaine with adrenaline(1:100,000) and crestal incision is given over the edentulous ridge in posterior maxilla. Full thickness mucocutaneous flap is reflected and alveolar ridge was exposed. A window was created in the lateral wall of maxillary antrum and schneiderian membrane was elevated carefully. The space created by elevation of schneiderian membrane is packed with human bone allograft prepared in Banaras Hindu University. The flap is approximated and sutured. Patient is given post operative instructions and called for follow-up on the next day. Suture removal is done after 7 days. After 6 months, second surgery is performed in the site where bone was augmented. Antibiotic prophylaxis with Amoxicillin and Clavulanate is prescribed 1hour before surgery, local infiltration with lignocaine and 1:100,000 epinephrine is given and full thickness mucocutaneous flap is raised after crestal incision. column28: Anti-Coronavirus Hyperimmune IVIG contains polyvalent antibodies with neutralizing specificity for SARS-CoV-2. It has the potential to provide a standardized therapy to augment host immunity to SARS-CoV-2 and prevent disease progression in symptomatic patients. Hyperimmune IVIG differs from standard IVIG in its derivation from donors who have mounted an immune response to the infection of interest (natural infection as undertaken in this protocol, or following vaccination for other disease states), and its standardization as a product based on neutralizing antibody titers or similar assays demonstrating its activity against the infection of interest. Hyperimmune globulin requires plasma from otherwise healthy individuals in the convalescent phase of the infection, and it is clear that there will be many individuals fitting this criterion with most patients recovering from COVID-19 and therefore able to safely provide a plasma donation during convalescence. Therefore, this resource will be rapidly available and will serve as an accessible therapeutic modality across multiple jurisdictions globally The hIVIG product is administered as a single dose of 30 grams (g), or 300 mL at a concentration of 0.1 g/mL. This dose corresponds to 400 mg/kilogram (kg) for a 75 kg adult. | Participants assigned to the placebo group for hIVIG will be given infusions of a commercially available isotonic saline solution. There are color differences between the infusion preparations for hIVIG and placebo. Therefore, site pharmacists will be instructed to place a colored sleeve or other suitable covering over all infusion bags to mask the color of the contents and reduce the risk of unblinding. The volume used for hIVIG and for placebo will be comparable.

column51: Oral submucous fibrosis (OSMF) is a chronic, progressive, pre-cancerous condition of the oral mucosa with major etiological factor being betel quid chewing habit.[OSMF was defined as an â€˜insidious, chronic disease affecting any part of the oral cavity and sometimes the pharynx and esophagus, characterized by a mucosal rigidity of varying intensity due to the fibro-elastic changes of the juxtaepithelial layer, resulting in a progressive inability to open the mouth. It is accepted that areca nut plays a principal role in the etiology of OSMF. The copper content of areca nut is elevated, and the levels of soluble copper in saliva may go up in areca quid chewers. Numerous factors such as chili consumption, nutritional deficiency states, areca nut chewing, hereditary susceptibility, autoimmunity and collagen disorders have been suggested to be concerned in the pathogenesis of this condition. The disease begins with vesicle formation, followed by inflammation and increased hyalinization of the lamina propria. This results in extensive fibrosis of the subepithelial as well as submucosal tissue which represents as thick, vertical bands in the cheeks, faucial pillars and even surround the lips causing trismus and difficulty in protrusion of the tongue. The blanching of oral mucosa is due to impaired local vascularity, imparting it a marble like appearance. The most commonly involved site is buccal mucosa, followed by palate, retro molar region, faucial pillars and pharynx. Dysphagia (difficult swallowing) and dysphonation (difficult phonation) seen in advanced stages which results into malnutrition and poor oral hygiene. It is prepared through centrifugation to a concentrated form and then injected into the oral submucosa. column51: Autoimmune liver disorders (AILD) encompass a spectrum of disorders including autoimmune hepatitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, and primary biliary cholangitis. These represent a heterogeneous group with differing pathogenesis, patterns of hepatic injury and different clinical behavior and response to treatment. A subgroup of patients with AILD share common features relating to the different subtypes of AILD; these have been termed the â€˜overlap syndromesâ€™ Immunosuppression is the mainstay of treatment for autoimmune hepatitis and its overlap syndromes with PBC and PSC. All patients with AIH are candidates for immunosuppressive therapy, except those with an inactive disease defined by clinical, biochemical and histological criteria(4). Clinical guidelines, like the European Association for the Study of Liver (EASL) recommended that all AIH patients with advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis or active disease as defined by AST/ALT > 3x ULN, HAI >4/18) should be treated . The first line of recommended treatment options includes prednisone/prednisolone (1 mg/kg/day up to 40-60 mg/day) either alone or in combination with azathioprine (50-150 mg/day), or budesonide (9 mg/day) alone or in a combination with azathioprine. With first-line therapies, 80-90% of patients have a biochemical response in the form of a reduction of transaminase levels. Overall, 10-20% of patients may be refractory to the first-line drugs. Second-line immuno-suppressive drugs include mycophenolate mofetil, calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporin A), mercaptopurines, and methotrexate. There are case reports of the use of biologics such as infliximab and rituximab. There is no published data on the effect of FMT in patients with AIH. column51: Variceal bleed is the second most common decompensation in cirrhosis after ascites and is associated with an overall mortality of 15-25% at 6 weeks.1 Up to 42% and 72% patients with Child A and Child B/C patients respectively have varices on screening endoscopy.2 Varices develop at the rate of 7-8%/year, and progress from small to large varices at up to 22% at 1 year in patients with Child B/C cirrhosis.3 Elevated portal pressure correlates with the formation of varices, variceal rupture and the severity of the variceal bleed. Hepatic venous portal gradient (HVPG), the most reliable surrogate measure for portal pressure correlates linearly with the development of varices, variceal bleeding and uncontrolled bleeding, developing at an HVPG of 10, 12, and 20mm Hg, respectively. Albumin, the most abundant serum protein, is synthesized by the hepatocytes and is responsible for 75% of the plasma oncotic pressure.10 Its pleiotropic non-oncotic properties have enabled its use in the management of SBP, acute kidney injury-hepatorenal syndrome, and long-term treatment of decompensated cirrhosis.11 Albumin infusion is associated with a significant reduction in the levels of inflammatory cytokines without changes in the portal hemodynamics.12 In addition to its anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, albumin acts a potent scavenger of toxic metabolites.13 In principle, albumin infusion should decrease the inflammatory mediators and bacteremia associated with variceal bleed, irrespective of its effects on portal pressures. Previous studies have also shown no effect of albumin infusion on portal pressures, as estimated by the changes in HVPG.12,14 However, the role of albumin in the management of variceal bleed is still unclear. column51: Tympanic membrane perforation is the most commonly encountered problems in otorhinolaryngology in developing countries like India because of inadequate health care, infrastructure, education, low socio economic status of people leading to improper care and compliance to the treatment facilities. which can result in chronic infection to the middle ear cleft leading to TM perforation. TM perforation can also result from acute traumatic injury to membrane or from repetitive infection or unresolved infection of middle ear cleft. Tympanoplasty involves the use of various grafts material for the surgical closing of the tympanic membrane to maintain the integrity of the tympanic membrane. various graft material like skin, cartilage, facia, dura, vein, fat etc other bio graft which have been put in use of hyaluronic acid, gel foam, paper patch etc the graft uptake rate after tympanoplasty have found to range anywhere from 70 to 90 %.Various other modalities have tried to increase the graft uptake rate. The success rate of the graft uptake rate depends upon various factors like type of graft used, technique employed, material of the graft, age of the patents, op care etc. There has been use of various materials as an adjuvant to surgery to improve the success rate of the graft uptake and to provide better prognosis in the surgeries. The use of fibroblast growth factor, heparin, epidermal growth factor(EGFs), transforming growth factor (TGFs)etc.PRP ( platelet rich plasma )is a newer modality which is nowadays gaining more popularity as part of regenerative medicine. PRP has already been a very popular adjuvant which has been put into use in various head and neck surgeries, cosmetic surgeries, sport medicine, dentistry, craniofacial, orthopedics, pain management etc.PRP contains large number of proteins which act as a growth factor and promotes wound healing with addition property of clot formation, so it can be used as a bio adjuvant to surgery for better surgical outcomes. In India very few studies are done which have used PRP as an adjuvant to tympanoplasty to enhance the surgical outcome of the graft uptake.
