column51: Root canal therapy (RCT) is indicated in permanent mature teeth with pulpal and periradicular diseases. It involves complete removal of pulp tissues from the root canals, disinfection and restoring them with bioinert materials. Root canal treatment has a high success rate (86.02%). The survival rate of endodontically treated tooth was reported as 86% at 2-3 years, 93% at 4-5 years, and 87% at 8-10 years. Vital pulp therapies have been used in primary teeth and immature permanent teeth. However, with the advent of new bioactive material, the paradigm is shifting toward permanent teeth with mature apices of roots. There are many prospective and retrospective studies, randomized controlled trials, and systematic reviews that report coronal pulpotomy with bioactive material in permanent teeth with pulpal pathosis proved to be as successful as root canal therapy (RCT). Coronal pulpotomy is cost-effective, not very technical demanding like root canal therapy and less time consuming for both the dentists and patients. This treatment can be offered to the patient as an alternative to endodontic therapy. Root canal treatment is non conservative and non biological treatment which is expensive, time consuming and tooth becomes non vital. The current scenario of endodontology has been shifted towards avoiding non-biological treatment. Recent studies shows that there is a good correlation between the clinical symptoms of pulpitis and corresponding histological state of a diseased pulp. There is regenerative potential of pulpo-dentinal complex in a tooth associated with symptoms indicative of irreversible pulpitis. The process of pulp repair and regeneration is enhanced by the various growth factors like TGF-beta, ADM and IGF-1/2 which releases from the pulpo-dentinal complex. Pulpitis caused by caries is the main reason for root canal treatment. Instead of complete pulp tissue removal by pulpectomy, vital pulp therapy has been considered as an alternative approach. As a minimally-invasive approach, vital pulp therapy includes stepwise excavation of decayed tissues, direct/indirect pulp capping, partial/full pulpotomy and partial pulpectomy. This treatment option involves removing the partial and entire coronal pulp tissue and keeping the remaining pulp vital in the canal. This preserve the immunological function and conserve the tooth structure, simplifying the treatment procedures, avoiding treatment complications and reducing cost and inconvenience for the patient. column28: Extra-oral antisepsis will be done with 5% povidine iodine solution and intra-orally with chlorhexidine digluconate. The procedure will be performed under local anesthesia. Crevicular incision will be made in an attempt to preserve as much tissue as possible and full thickness mucoperiosteal flaps will be reflected. The flaps will be extended one tooth mesial and distal to the defect to provide full visibility and access to the denuded root surface and associated defect. Topical/local anaesthesia will be given to the patient as per the patients comfort. The tip of the laser will be placed 1mm coronal to the base of the pocket.The tip will be kept parallel to the root and it will be moved both horizontally and vertically, painting the tissue on the wall of the gingival sulcus from calibrated depth to gingival margin. The tip will be moved from apical to coronal direction and will not be kept stationary for more than 5secs. It will be followed by thorough saline irrigation to remove any remaining debris.No peridontal dressing will be given. Post-operative instructions will be given.This results in removal of target inflamed epithelial lining of the pocket.

column51: Complete mechanical debridement being the "gold standard" of periodontal treatment, still doesnâ€™t eliminate the bacterial deposits and toxins completely due to limited access to the site. Recently, diode lasers have become popular owing to advantages like anti-bacterial effect, promoting angiogenesis, providing haemostasis, accelerates wound healing and also have shown improved clinical outcomes when employed to de-epithelize the underneath lining of mucoperiosteal flap.Hence in this study, 980nm diode laser is used for pocket sterilization procedure to remove the target inflamed epithelial lining of the pocket. The pocket sterilization procedure using diode laser is compared with open flap debridement procedure. Open flap debridement is a surgical procedure that is used commonly in the treatment of periodontitis. The comparison of the above mentioned two treatment procedures is done by evaluating the levels of interleukin-36(IL-36) gamma in gingival crevicular fluid using Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay( ELISA) at baseline and 3 month after treatment . IL-36 gamma is a pro-inflammatory marker that belongs to the superfamily of IL-1 cytokines and plays important roles in various systemic inflammatory diseases as well as periodontitis. Clinical measurements are also taken to compare both the treatments. column51: PRP PREPARATION METHOD. â€¢ All the aseptic precautions will be taken and we will obtain 34- 45 ml of Whole Blood in 8.5 ml acid citrate dextrose (ACD) tubes by venipuncture from the antecubital vein. â€¢ Centrifugation of the blood will be done using a soft spin â€¢ @3000rpm/min for 3mins. column51: Title Role of PRP on endometrial receptivity in Recurrent Implantation Failure Purpose of study To study the effect of intrauterine instillation of autologous PRP on implantation rate in recurrent implantation failure. Research question Does Platelet-rich plasma derived from peripheral blood help in improving the implantation rate in cases of unexplained recurrent implantation failure? Hypothesis Intrauterine instillation of PRP that contains several growth factors and cytokines may contribute to improvement in endometrial receptivity. Rationale There is a scarcity of high-quality evidence to support the role of autologous PRP in endometrial receptivity. Study type RCT A randomized controlled trial. Sample size 154 Primary outcome Implantation rate 4 wks +2 wks after ET Secondary Outcome Biochemical pregnancy 2 wks +2 wks after ET Clinical pregnancy 4 wks +2 wks after ET Ongoing pregnancy 10 wks +2 wks after ET Delivery 22wks + 2 wks after ET Live birth more than 26 wks + 10 wks after ET Population: The patients with H/O recurrent implantation failure in the age group of 25-40 years visiting our designated centres. RIF is defined as no evidence of Gestational sac in TVS after 6 wks of gestation after transfer of â‰¥ 3 high-quality embryos in at least 3 fresh or frozen transfer cycles in an age group of < 40 years. (reference) 4. Grade of embryo 3/4/5/6/AA/AB/BA Exclusion criteria 1. Presence of endocrine disorders (uncontrolled diabetes mellitus / hyperprolactinemia, thyroid dysfunction) 2. Chronic Liver Pathology leading to impaired coagulation profile. column32: Participants are eligible to be included in the study only if all of the following criteria apply- 1 Participant or their legally acceptable representative must sign ICF indicating that he or she understands the purpose of, procedures and restriction required for the study Parent(s) (preferably both if available or as per local requirements) must sign an ICF indicating that he or she understands the purpose of, and procedures required for, the study and is willing to allow the child to participate in the study.2 Participant must be 2 to 65 years of age (both inclusive) at the time of providing the informed consent.3 Participants with documented clinical diagnosis of a primary immunodeficiency disease as defined by IUIS (International Union of Immunological Societies) and require treatment with IVIg. Confirmation of PID diagnosis may include a review of infection history, serum IgG concentration at diagnosis and prior to immunoglobulin therapy and responses (failure to achieve two fold rise in IgG antibody titre) to vaccination with polysaccharide and protein vaccines.4 Participants with documented agammaglobulinemia (defined as the total absence of one or more classes of antibodies) or hypogammaglobulinemia (defined as low levels of one or more classes [that is at least 2 standard deviations under the mean level per age) including but not limited to the following: humoral-based immunodeficiency syndromes (e.g., X-linked agammaglobulinemia, common variable immunodeficiency), and combined immunodeficiency syndromes without lymphocytopenia (e.g., hyper-immunoglobulin M [IgM] immunodeficiency syndrome) â€¢ Newly diagnosed participants- who are eligible to receive IVIg treatment as per the investigator discretion.â€¢ Participants already on IVIg treatmentâˆ’ Participants must be receiving IVIg treatment for primary immunodeficiency âˆ’ Participant must be receiving stable dose of an approved IVIg within 200-900 mg/kg (Â± 20% of the mean dose for the last 3 infusions) with established treatment intervals of 21- or 28-day (Â±3 days or Â±4 days, respectively) for at least 3 infusion cycles (one of which could be the screening visit result).âˆ’ At least 2 documented IgG trough levels while receiving an IVIg, of more than or equal to 450 mg/dL obtained at 2 infusion cycles within 12 months (1 must be within 6months) prior to enrollment.5 Participants who are otherwise medically stable on the basis of physical examination, medical history and vital signs, chest x-ray and 12-lead ECG performed at screening. Any abnormalities must be consistent with the underlying illness in the study population and this determination must be recorded in the participant source documents and initialed by the investigator.6 Participants who are otherwise medically stable on the basis of clinical laboratory tests performed at screening. If the results of the serum chemistry panel, hematology, or urinalysis are outside the normal reference ranges, the participant may be included only if the investigator judges the abnormalities or deviations from normal to be not clinically significant or to be appropriate and reasonable for the population under study. This determination must be recorded in the participant source documents and initialed by the investigator.7 A female participant is eligible to participate if she is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and at least one of the following conditions applies:â€¢ Is not a woman of childbearing potential (WOCBP) ORâ€¢ Is a WOCBP and using an acceptable contraceptive method during the intervention period. The investigator should evaluate the effectiveness of the contraceptive method in relationship to the first dose of study intervention.â€¢ A WOCBP must have a negative highly sensitive serum pregnancy test at screening and negative urine pregnancy test before IMP administration.â€¢ Additional requirements for pregnancy testing after study intervention are located in Appendix 10.2.â€¢ The investigator is responsible for review of medical history, menstrual history, and recent sexual activity to decrease the risk for inclusion of a woman with an early undetected pregnancy. A female participant must provide assurance to follow precautions to avoid pregnancy during the study period.8 Male participants are eligible to participate if they agree to the following during the intervention period and for at least 6 months after the last dose of study intervention:â€¢ Must agree not to donate sperm for the purpose of reproduction PLUS EITHERâ€¢ Be abstinent from heterosexual [or homosexual] intercourse as their preferred and usual lifestyle (abstinent on a long-term and persistent basis) and agree to remain abstinent ORâ€¢ Must agree to use contraception /barrier as detailed below:âˆ’ A male participant must wear a condom when engaging in any activity that allows for passage of ejaculate to another person âˆ’ Male participants should also be advised of the benefit for a female partner to use a highly effective method of contraception as condom may break or leak when having sexual intercourse with a woman of childbearing potential who is not currently pregnant.10 Participants must be willing and able to adhere to protocol requirements.
column33: Any potential participant who meets any of the following criteria will be excluded from participating in the study:1 History of clinically significant cardiac, vascular, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, endocrine, neurologic, rheumatologic, psychiatric, or metabolic disturbances. 2 Known allergies, hypersensitivity, or persistent reactions (urticaria, breathing difficulty, severe hypotension, or anaphylaxis) following human normal immunoglobulin intravenous or its excipients or following plasma-derived products (refer to the prescribing information of study intervention) OR known history of anaphylactic reactions to IgA found in other products.3 Exposure to blood or any blood product or derivative, other than commercially available human IVIg or human albumin within the past 3 months.4 Participant has known Selective Immunoglobulin A (IgA) Deficiency (with or without antibodies to IgA). (Note: exclusion is for the specific diagnostic entity. It does not exclude other forms of humoral primary immunodeficiency which have decreased IgA in addition to decreased IgG requiring immune globulin [IgG] replacement). 5 Participant with an acquired medical condition that is known to cause secondary immune deficiency, such as chronic lymphocytic leukemia, lymphoma, multiple myeloma, chronic or recurrent neutropenia (ANC less than 1000 cells/mm3), or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection/acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS).6 Participant having contraindication for intravenous immunoglobulin or has been diagnosed with dysgammaglobulinemia, isolated IgG subclass deficiency, isolated specific antibody deficiency disorder, or transien hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy.7 History of autoimmune hemolytic anemia.8 History of congenital impairment of pulmonary function. 9 The participant currently has a known hyperviscosity syndrome.10 Participant has a predisposition for acute renal failure (e.g. any degree of pre-existing renal insufficiency or routine treatment with known nephritic drugs) and/or has a history of acute renal failure; and/or is on dialysis.11 Participant has total protein >9 g/dL and/or participants with myeloma, macroglobulinemia (IgM) and paraproteinemia. 12 Participant (if less than 18 years of age) has non-controlled hypertension at a level of greater than or equal to the 90th percentile blood pressure (either systolic or diastolic) for their age and height or the adult participant has non-controlled arterial hypertension (systolic blood pressure more than or equal to 160 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure more than or equal to 100 mmHg).13 Participant has a known history, or is positive at enrollment, for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus.14 Participant with documented history of bleeding disorders or who are on anti-coagulation therapy.15 Participant has an active viral or bacterial infection or symptoms/signs consistent with such an infection (as documented by culture or diagnostic imaging and (or) a body temperature exceeding 38.5Â°C (101.3Â°F)), excluding chronic sinusitis or bronchiectasis, within the two weeks prior to the initial dose of investigational product. Participants may be receiving antibiotics as long as signs/symptoms of infection have been absent for two weeks prior to the initial infusion of IP.Note: If an viral or bacterial infection occurs during the screening period and prior to the first dose of study intervention, the participant will be a Screen Failure.16 The participant is receiving any of the following medications: (a) immunosuppressants including chemotherapeutic agents; (b) immunomodulators; (c) long-term systemic corticosteroids defined as daily dose more than or equal to 0.15 mg of prednisone equivalent/kg/day for more than 10 days.Note: Intermittent courses of corticosteroids of not more than 10 days would not exclude a participant. Inhaled or topical corticosteroids may be allowed at discretion of the investigator.17 Participant has a lifetime history of at least one thrombotic event including deep vein thrombosis, cerebrovascular accident, pulmonary embolism, transient ischemic attacks, unstable or advanced ischemic heart disease or myocardial infarction.18 Participant has significant protein losing enteropathy, nephrotic syndrome, or lymphangiectasia.19 History of Lymphoma, leukemia, or any malignancy except for basal cell or squamous epithelial carcinomas of the skin that have been resected with no evidence of metastatic disease for 5 years; carcinoma in situ of the cervix; or malignancy, which is considered cured with minimal risk of recurrence. 20 Participant has known substance or prescription drug abuse.21 Participant had major surgery within 4 weeks before screening, or will not have fully recovered from surgery, or has surgery planned during the time the participant is expected to participate in the study. NOTE: Participants with planned surgical procedures to be conducted under local anesthesia may participate. However, the same needs to be documented in the patient case-record files and will not be considered as serious adverse event. 22 Prior to screening, participants received an investigational intervention or used an invasive investigational medical device within 30 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, or has received any investigational blood product, with the exception of other IgG products, within the previous 3 months before signing informed consent.23 Congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association III/IV), cardiomyopathy, cardiac arrhythmia associated with thromboembolic events (e.g., atrial fibrillation), or any condition for which, in the opinion of the investigator, participation would not be in the best interest of the participant safety or that could prevent, limit, or confound the protocol-specified assessments.24 Participant with any condition for which, in the opinion of the investigator, participation would not be in the best interest of the participant (eg, compromise the well-being) or that could prevent, limit, or confound the protocol-specified assessments.

column51: Lung cancer is the most common cancer and the leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally. Nonâ€“small-cell lung cancer accounts for 85% to 90% of lung cancers . Based on the national cancer registry data, incidence of lung cancer is highest amongst all approved indication of Nivolumab in India. Nivolumab is a fully human IgG4 programmed death-1 (PD-1) immune checkpoint inhibitor antibody, that binds with high affinity to PD-1 receptors expressed on T cells and disrupts negative signaling induced by PD-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and PD-ligand 2 to restore T-cell effector function. In one of the Phase I study in patients with advanced NSCLC, Nivolumab monotherapy demonstrated a mean ORR of 17% and 18% in pateints with squamous and nonsquamous histologies, respectiely. Limited information is available in the literature on the mechanical vibration effects on the rate of OTM and on orthodontically induced root resorption (OIRR) in human. No study is done on the mechanical vibration effects on PGE2 production. column51: temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ OA) affects 5-12% of world population and is more prevalent in india with 22-29% occurrence and without intervention it negatively affects quality of life. primary TMJ OA is characterized by absence of distinct local or systemic factors. there are many trreatment options like occlusal splint, NSAIDs, I/A steroid injection, hyalouronic injection, but with recent advancement and studies coming up with platelet rich plasma (PRP) showing it’s anti- inflammatory and regenerative properties makes it novel treatment option for management of pain and function among patients suffering with TMJ OA . column51: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative disease of the joints which involves cartilage. Osteoarthitis of the knees is the most common joint disease. It is chronic progressive degenerative disease. It affects 30% of the people having age more than 50 years. Various studies have shown that osteoarthritis leads to a major burden on the economy of many developing countries.1,2,3 There have been various non-operative and operative modalities used in the treatment of osteoarthritis of knees. But early osteoarthritis is mostly treated with non-operative modalities. These modalities range from Oral analgesics i.e. Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) are most commonly used to intra-articular PRP injections and BMAC injections. All these modalities have their own plus points and drawbaks. NSAIDs are cheaper and more easily available than the others. They have short term good effect but on prolonged usage lead to systemic side effects. Various oral supplements like Glucosamine and Chondrotin sulfate are shown to have good results in treatment of osteoarthtitis of knees on prolonged use but these cannot be considered as ideal treatment for the same. Intra-articular injections of steroids are shown to have good short term effects but like NSAIDs on prolonged usage are known to cause systemic side effects as well as adverse effects on local cartilage. Intra-articular injections of viscosupplements particularly Hyaluronic acid is another modality. column51: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the outcome of excessive accumulation of triglyceride inside the liver (without frequent use of alcohol), due to which various metabolic disturbances occur and reflect the disease outcome.(1) Although the liver is not a prime location for storing fat i.e. triglyceride only 5 % of body fat mass is stored in the liver, and the rest is stored in the muscle and adipose tissue of the body.(2) NAFLD starts with the accumulation of fat in the hepatocyte, which causes inflammation and ballooning in the liver and progresses to NASH, which also leads to fibrosis and cirrhosis and may develop HCC (3) The global prevalence of NAFLD is estimated to be 24â€“30% and is higher among those with obesity and metabolic syndrome.(4â€“6) Although NAFLD is usually linked to obesity, NAFLD also occurs in non-obese/lean subjects with similar severities as in obese NAFLD patients. Approximately, 3â€“30% of non-obese populations have NAFLD.(7) There is evidence that the composition of the gut microbiota may play a role in the development and progression of NAFLD. The human body has millions of microorganisms, collectively known as the microbiota or microbiome. These microorganisms include bacteria, fungi, viruses, and protozoa, and they can be found in various parts of the body, such as the skin, mouth, gut, and reproductive tract. The microbiota plays an important role in human health, influencing various physiological processes, including digestion, immunity, and metabolism. The composition of the microbiota can be influenced by a variety of factors, including diet, antibiotics, and environmental factors. Disruptions in the microbiota have been linked to many diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease, obesity, and allergies. The alteration of gut microbiota is called dysbiosis. The dysbiotic state can lead to an imbalance of beneficial and harmful metabolites, contributing to the development and progression of liver diseases. In NAFLD, dysbiosis is associated with increased gut permeability, which allows bacterial toxins to enter the bloodstream and trigger inflammation in the liver.(9) The dysbiosis also leads to an increase in the production of lipopolysaccharides (LPS) production by gram-negative bacteria, which further promotes inflammation in the liver. Modulation of the gut microbiota through diet, probiotics, or fecal microbiota transplantation may provide a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing and treating liver diseases. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Background- Lower back pain is now regarded as the first cause of disability worldwide. The Global Burden of Disease (GBD) in 2015 reported that the global point prevalence of activity limiting LBP was 7.3% (540 million people in the world). Intervertebral disc degeneration accounts for almost 40% of lower back pain cases and is a common cause of pain in the general population which leads to varying disabilities and a high socioeconomic burden. Rationale- Disc degeneration results in the loss of proteoglycans, collagen fibers, and an increase in fibronectin fragments and enzymatic activity like metalloproteinase, capsins and aggrecanase. Due to the loss of proteoglycans, the osmotic pressure of the disc falls and the disc is not able to maintain hydration under load. As a result, they lose height and fluid more rapidly. This eventually leads to bulging of the disc, which further leads to protrusion, extrusion and sequestration of disc. Disc aggrecan has also been shown to inhibit neural ingrowth. Therefore, loss of aggrecan and proteoglycans in degenerate discs is associated with discogenic pain. Current therapeutic strategies for intervertebral disc degeneration mostly depend on physiotherapy, anti- inflammatory medications and spinal surgery to alleviate the symptoms, but these therapies cannot restore the degenerated disc and may even accelerate the degenerative progression of the adjacent intervertebral disc. These factors result in cellular and tissue proliferation and may help restore the normal physiology of the disc and alleviate pain. Novelty- There are only a handful of studies done on platelet rich plasma injection therapy for disc prolapse. Most of them are case series or prospective trials. Only one double-blinded randomized control trial has been published to date. column51: One of the most common causes of pain and disability worldwide is osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee. Its prevalence rises with age, and generally speaking, women are more impacted than males. It is one of the main factors limiting mobility, particularly in women. [1] The appendicular joints most frequently afflicted are the hands, hips, and knees. The entire joint is affected by OA, which results in discomfort, oedema, and a loss of normal joint function due to cartilage degeneration, bone remodelling, production of osteophyte, and inflammation of the synovium. Patients with OA are probably treated with various pharmacological and nonpharmaceutical therapies, frequently in varied combinations, because OA might last for decades in a patientâ€™s life. [2]. While having a total knee replacement has advantages, postponing or avoiding surgery is preferable from a medical and healthcare system standpoint. Reduced total knee replacement procedures will also mean fewer expensive revision procedures. [3]. Although up to 20% of patients are not satisfied, total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is a successful treatment. Identification of suitable TKA candidates prior to surgery is essential for increasing patient satisfaction.[3] Additionally, published research have demonstrated that individuals with Grade II or III knee OA (on the Kellgren-Lawrence scale) have worse outcomes following total knee replacement procedures than those with Grade IV OA. [3][4]. Many individuals are nonetheless symptomatic despite efforts to provide proper conservative therapy. Because the disease is not yet at its final stage, many patients may not be good candidates for total knee replacement due to medical fragility, obesity, youth, high activity level, or even just because they donâ€™t have surgery. A brand-new class of injectable "biologic" drugs has just lately become accessible for this subset of patients. . This class of injectables, which is not technically defined, consists of allogeneic placental products, adipose-derived stromal vascular fraction, platelet-rich plasma (PRP), bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC), and others. [10] Hyaluronic acid (HA) injections into the joints are being utilised to treat KOA. HA have been demonstrated to be superior in terms of effectiveness and safety when compared to Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications (NSAIDs) [5][6]. Injections of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) into the joints have gained popularity as a treatment for KOA in recent years. PRP offers an inexpensive and minimally invasive way to treat arthritic knees by delivering concentrated autologous growth factors and bioactive compounds. Platelets are utilised to treat a variety of disorders because they contain growth factors that control tissue healing and regeneration.[19] PRP, which is made from autologous blood, delivers bioactive molecules to control the pathogenic processes that cause joint deterioration. [8] PRP offers up to 300 bioactive molecules and is utilised as a therapeutic agent to treat a variety of musculoskeletal problems, according to basic science. [8]. There are drawbacks and potential adverse effects to traditional treatment approaches such activity moderation, physical therapy, and medicines like non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), corticosteroids, visco-supplementation, and opioids. [4] Therefore, other interventions are required for patients with Grade II or III knee OA. It has been suggested that platelet rich plasma (PRP) can effectively cure osteoarthritis of the knee. According to a review of recent trials, there is debate concerning the efficacy of PRP in the treatment of knee OA. Preclinical research supports the use of PRP injections to promote a favourable environment for joint tissue repair, targeting not just cartilage but also synovial and meniscal tissues, and has demonstrated effectiveness in delaying the progression of OA. Patients with total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and knee OA are hypothesised to respond differently based on growth factors in platelet granules.[10] In addition to comparing PRP injections to hyaluronic acid and a placebo, the Go rmeli et al. study looked into the ideal amount of PRP injections for the treatment of knee OA. Three PRP injections [11] were proven to be the preferred course of treatment for individuals with early-stage knee OA, while none of the aforementioned treatments were beneficial for patients with advanced OA. However no study has been conducted regarding the interval between which injections have to be given for better results in patients. column51: Asthma is a serious health problem that affects people of all ages throughout the world. The Global INitiative for Asthma (GINA) treatment guidelines emphasize that clinical management should be based on clinical control rather than asthma severity, which can change over time. Patients with severe asthma are at a high risk of asthma related hospitalization and mortality. In addition, both impairment in quality of life and economic burden increase with increasing asthma severity and are greatest in patients with inadequately controlled severe persistent allergic asthma. Meta-analyses of trials of anti-IgE therapy have shown that the use of omalizumab as an adjunct to ICS in moderate to severe asthma reduces the number of asthma exacerbations and allows dose reduction and withdrawal of ICS. Study design: Monocentric open label randomised controlled study. The study will be conducted in Department of Hepatology, ILBS. Study period: 1 year Sample size: Based on the previous studies on 5% albumin and 20% albumin on fluid resuscitation, assuming that the reversal rate is approximately 11% with 5% Albumin, and 40% with 20% Albumin plus plasmalyte with alpha 5 and power 90. column28: After live donor liver transplant, the patients will be randomized by simple randomization method into 2 groups to detect allograft rejection - Group 1 following cfDNA combined with liver enzymes monitoring and Group 2 following standard monitoring with liver enzymes alone. Group 1 (TEST GROUP )- cfDNA analysis will be done along with liver enzyme tests as a serial monitoring system in patients who have undergone transplant at a frequency of 14 days, 2 months, 4 months post transplant. At any point of the analysis, if the cfDNA levels are found to be elevated, a cfDNA analysis with DSA will be done to detect the risk of an antibody mediated rejection and the level of immunosuppressants will be modulated. Concurrently, if the liver function tests are also observed to be abnormal, rejection will be confirmed with a liver biopsy and rejection scoring will be done according to Rejection activity index (RAI). If the cfDNA levels are found to be normal, the patient will be followed up with standard immunosuppression. As cfDNA is not a standard method of detecting rejection, there is a chance of rejection going undetected. In this context, to minimize this risk, it is combined with the standard measure, which is assessment of liver function tests. ï¬Group 2 ( STANDARD GROUP)- The patients will be monitored solely by liver enzymes like transaminases, alkaline phosphatase, gamma-glutamyl transferase every week for the initial three months and then on monthly basis for a year. At any point of the study if a two-fold rise in liver enzymes are observed, a cfDNA analysis combined with DSA will be done. If the levels are seen elevated, liver biopsy will be done. In case of normal liver enzymes, they will be followed up. Liver biopsy will be performed on standard indication and rejection will be graded on RAI scoring .The indication for a liver biopsy includes more than 2 fold rise in liver enzymes with no evident alternate causes such as sepsis or graft technical issues(biliary or vascular problems) . ï¬Immunosuppression modulation includes maintain TAC level above 8 ng/ml. If TAC level already above 8 ng/ml, augment or supplement alternate immunosuppressants ( steroids or MMF). ï¬Both groups are followed up and Rejection Activity Index (RAI) correlated with cfDNA and DSA together as well as cfDNA individually. The randomized study will be done over a time period of one year and then the clinical outcome of both groups will be measured after 1 year post transplant with a fibroscan, ultrasound or CT MRI

column51: Post liver transplantation, both groups of patients will initially be started on immunosuppression as follows : l Tacrolimus will be started at 2mg/day in a divided or single dose depending on the formulation to aim for a trough level of 8ng/ml. The dosage will be altered depending on the renal function. l Methylprednisolone will be started at 250 mg IV on Day 1, 125mg IV on Day 2, 80mg IV on Day 3 and 40 mg IV on Day 4 . Subsequently, oral prednisolone is started at 30mg daily and tapered weekly by 5mg and stopped at 6 weeks. l Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF) will be started at 500 mg twice daily from day 1, provided the platelet count is more than 25,000/mm3. It will be stopped at 4-6 months. Due to the complexity of the interaction between immunosuppressants and other drugs and hepatic and renal function, some degree of immunosuppression â€œtweakingâ€ will be left to the physicianâ€™s discretion. On post-operative day 3, the participants will be randomly assigned into two groups using a computerized randomization technique. The assigned group will be enclosed in sealed, opaque envelopes opened only by the study coordinator. Group 1 (Test group): Blood samples (9ml) will be collected on the post-operative days 7,45,75,120 &180 and the dd-cfDNA will be quantified. At any point during the analysis, if dd-cfDNA levels are found to be elevated, this possibly suggests an early rejection, and immunosuppression will be adjusted as follows: l The primary goal of immunosuppression modulation is to maintain Tacrolimus (TAC) blood levels at 8 ng/ml. If TAC levels are already at this target level, immunosuppressive therapy will be intensified by either increasing the dosage or adding alternative immunosuppressants such as steroids or Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) depending on clinical parameters l Steroid dose will be increased by 10mg of prednisolone or Mycophenolate mofetil will be increased to 500mg thrice a day. l This will be based on the level of the platelet count and total WBC count. If the dd-cfDNA levels are elevated on post-operative day 45 or later, and the recipient is already on adequate triple immunosuppression, an mTOR inhibitor (Everolimus) will be added. This is a relative contraindication within the initial 30 days of transplant due to poor wound healing. Simultaneously, if liver function tests (LFTs) show significant abnormalities, particularly a more than two-fold rise in LFTs without evident causes like sepsis or graft-related issues (such as biliovascular problems), a liver biopsy will be performed to confirm a rejection. The biopsy results will be used to calculate the Rejection Activity Index (RAI) to quantify the severity of the rejection. Biopsy-proven rejection will be treated according to the protocol of the unit, namely methylprednisolone pulsed doses at 10 mg/kg for 3-5 days. If dd-cfDNA levels are found to be normal, the patient will continue with standard immunosuppressive therapy, with regular follow-up to ensure stable transplant function. dd-cfDNA analysis will involve the assessment of parameters like total cfDNA, dd-cfDNA percentage, integrity ratio, T-cell markers, and Granzyme-B to differentiate between infection, T-cell mediated rejection, antibody-mediated rejection, and normal profile .This will help in precisely identifying the presence and type of rejection in each patient. Group 2(Standard group): Patients are monitored using standard liver function tests alone. The biopsy will be performed if there is a two-fold rise in liver function tests (aminotransferases, alkaline phosphatase, gamma-glutamyl transferases) without evident causes like sepsis or graft-related issues (such as biliovascular problems). column28: Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) will be given in a supine position with the hip in slight abduction, external rotation and leg in extension, using a standard focused shockwave device of Cart Swiss Dolorclast Smart 20. At each session, 2000 pulses will be applied with a pressure of 3 bar. The treatment frequency will be 8 pulses per second. According to the principle of clinical focusing, the area of maximal tenderness will be treated in a circumferential pattern, starting at the point of maximum pain level. The tender area is marked before applying the sonographic gel. ESWT will be given once a week for 3 weeks | PRP will be prepared using the double spin method. Whole blood of 25ml will be drawn in a syringe by venipuncture which is then transferred to Acid Citrate Dextrose tubes. These tubes will be centrifuged using a soft spin at 2400 rpm for 10 minutes. The supernatant plasma containing platelets is then collected in a separate plain vial and then centrifuged again using a hard spin of 3600 rpm for 15 minutes to obtain a platelet concentrate. The lower 1/3rd is platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and the upper 2/3rd is platelet-poor plasma (PPP). 5ml of PRP is procured by removing the PPP. Patient in a supine position with hip in slight abduction, external rotation and leg in extension, the skin overlying the pubic symphysis will be prepared and draped in a sterile green sheet. Then a 5ml syringe with a 21-gauge needle will be inserted under ultrasound guidance using a linear transducer, with the needle in a plane (i.e., longitudinal axis) to the transducer and tendon fibres. A needle will be inserted through the skin in a cephalo-caudal manner, into the rectus abdominis tendon insertion site at the pubic crest between the pubic tubercle and the pubic symphysis. Then 5ml of PRP will be injected in two aliquots at the tendon insertion near the pubic crest and the musculotendinous junction with the rectus sheath. The needle will be removed and local homeostasis will be achieved by applying pressure over the injection site and a sterile bandage will be applied

column51: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is defined as a (silent) skeletal disorder characterized by compromised bone strength predisposing to an increased risk of fracture. Bone strength reflects the integration of two main features: bone density and bone quality. Osteoporosis has no warning signs. Often, the first indication of the disease is a fracture. Nearly all non-vertebral fractures are caused by a fall; however, vertebral fractures often occur without a fall, and need not necessarily be painful. Only roughly one third of vertebral fractures are painful, and two thirds are painless. Marked height loss over the years may be a sign of underlying vertebral compression fractures, even without significant associated back pain. Wrist or other fractures may occur at a younger age than vertebral or hip fractures and may also be early clinical expressions of osteoporosis. With increasing longevity of the Indian population, it is now being realized that, as in the West, osteoporotic fractures are rising. Osteoporosis is characterized by low bone mass with micro architectural deterioration of bone tissue leading to enhance bone fragility, thus increasing the susceptibility to fracture. Denosumab is a human monoclonal antibody with affinity and specificity for RANK ligand, thereby inhibiting osteoclast formation, function, and survival. column51: Introduction: Stress is an innate response of the body that may be either physical, mental, or emotional to an unforeseen event that occurs in the life of the individual. Academic life is one of the events in an individualâ€™s life that may have different stressors. Contemporary literature suggests that university life is subjected to different stressors arising from academic pressure, social problems, and personal issues. It may also involve living away from the family which brings social isolation and adds to personal vulnerability. Negative mental health leads to decreased energy, difficulty thinking, concentrating, and making career decisions. Students are a pillar of the future in building an educated society. Aromatherapy: Aromatherapy is the popular complementary therapy that uses essential oils (also known volatile oils) from parts of the plants for the improvement of physical, emotional and spiritual well-being. Lavender and lemongrass oil as an herbal remedy has been associated with anxiolytic properties. It was suggested that the anxiolytic and antidepressant effects could be associated with the suppression of the activity of the sympathetic nervous system and it is perceived as pleasant and displays a relaxing activity, it has been employed in aromatherapy in different therapeutic contexts. Study design: A Comparative Pre-Post study design will be adopted for this study. All the eligible subjects will be divided into two groups, Lavender group and Lemongrass group. Assessments will be done before the intervention, 15th day and after the intervention of 30 days. column51: Schizophrenia is a complex neuropsychiatric brain syndrome characterized by 3 core symptom domains: positive symptoms (e.g., hallucinations, delusions), negative symptoms (e.g., blunted affect, alogia, anhedonia, avolition, asociality), and cognitive impairment. Negative symptoms can be divided into two categories: primary negative symptoms, which are a hallmark of the illness, and secondary negative symptoms, which are brought on by or linked to psychotic symptoms, depression, or neurologic side effects brought on by excessive dopamine antagonism during antipsychotic therapy. (Keefe, R et al., 2007) Positive symptoms may go into remission, but negative symptoms can still be present and significantly increase the burden of the disease. They have been connected to poor social and occupational functioning, which has a significant impact on day-to-day life and contributes to the high unemployment rates that schizophrenia patients experience (Hunter, R. et al., 2012). Primary negative symptom-treating medications continue to be a critical unmet need in the treatment of schizophrenia. Oxytocin has long been studied as having a potential role in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia, given its effects on cognition, memory, and social functioning through inhibitory regulation of mesolimbic dopamine. Intranasal oxytocin can also influence key parts of the default mode network, most notably the medial prefrontal cortex, which may reflect an influence on salience-processing, emotion regulation, and also self-processing. column51: Approximately 90% of sepsis is caused by bacterial infection and 40-60% of septic patients experience sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). In the recent decades, the growing knowledge about the pathophysiology of sepsis and AKI has suggested that adenosine triphosphate (ATP), adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and adenosine play an essential role as extracellular signaling molecules in both sepsis and AKI. Several lines of evidence have shown the potential benefits of the conversion of extracellular ATP to adenosine in treating sepsis and the related organ injury. TIN816 is an engineered, highly effective, soluble, and stabilized human recombinant CD39 enzyme. The enzyme hydrolyzes extracellular ATP and ADP to adenosine monophosphate (AMP). TIN816 has been proven beneficial in preclinical models of acute organ injuries. TIN816 has also been studied in healthy volunteers. To date, 40 healthy participants have received either TIN816 (N=30) or placebo (N=10) in the phase 1 healthy volunteer study (CTIN816A02101). The study results showed that TIN816 was safe and well tolerated. Overall, based on the existing evidence of potential benefits by conversion of extracellular ATP to adenosine in treating sepsis and the related organ injuries, the accumulated data of TIN816 from the preclinical studies; as well as, the first in human (FIH) study, it is anticipated that therapeutic application of TIN816 will have potent anti-inflammatory, anti-thrombotic and tissue repair/protection activity in participants suffering from SA-AKI. This study is designed to characterize the dose-response relationship and evaluate the safety and efficacy of three single doses of TIN816 (1 mg/kg, 2 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg) compared to placebo in participants with SA-AKI. A total of approximately 320 participants will be randomized. Screening will take place during hospitalization in an intensive care unit (ICU) or intermediate/high dependency care unit (HDU) where potential participants will undergo screening to assess the presence of sepsis and AKI based on Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) and Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) scores. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: This study is a prospective, single-arm, open-label, multi-center clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of MyCART-01 in patients with CD19+ relapsed or refractory B cell malignancies. The trial encompasses two phases, I and II, with a total intended enrollment of 41 participants, including both ALL (Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia) and NHL (Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma) patients. Phase I involves the inclusion of 10 patients, comprising 7 adults (with at least 1 from either ALL or NHL) and 3 pediatric patients with ALL. Following Phase I, Phase II aims to enroll an additional 31 patients, distributed between Stage I (14 patients) and Stage II (17 patients). The investigational product under evaluation is Mycabtagene Autoleaucel, denoted as MyCART-01. This therapy falls under the category of CAR-T (Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell) and is designed to target CD19, a protein expressed on the surface of B cells. The study is currently in the I/II phase of development and is being conducted at approximately seven centers in India. The primary endpoint is to assess the safety and efficacy of MyCART-01 in treating CD19+ relapsed or refractory B cell malignancies. Following the CAR-T infusion, participants will be monitored for a period of two years during the follow-up phase. column51: Background Residual ridge resorption (RRR), which occurs after tooth extraction, is a chronic, continuous, irreversible, and accumulative type of bone resorption. Because of the continued resorption of alveolar bone, this causes multiple cosmetic and functional challenges in individuals who have missing teeth. Consequently, in order to maintain the existing alveolar ridge, a great deal of research has been conducted on methods to stop the loss of alveolar bone or encourage the development of new bone. In view of this, a study will be conducted to assess and compare the effectiveness of PRF and Simvastatin in terms of their ability to promote bone regeneration and their ability to repair wounds in the extraction socket of mandibular molars. Objectives â€¢ To evaluate the effects of Simvastatin-impregnated gel foam on regeneration of bone and wound healing in patients undergoing mandibular molar extractions against those using PRF. Methods Procedure will be performed in patients undergoing extraction of mandibular molars. Patients will be divided in 2 groups. Immediately after the extraction, In Group 1, extraction sockets will receive Gel Foam as a carrier for the medication Simvastatin (10 mg, crushed and dispersed into normal saline); in Group 2, PRF will be grafted. Expected results For individuals having their mandibular molars extracted, gel foams infused with simvastatin will promote improved wound healing and bone regeneration. Conclusion It is hypothesized that Simvastatin impregnated gel foam placed might give better results.In patients having mandibular molar extraction, if Simvastatin Impregnated Gel foam is shown to be superior to PRF in regard to regeneration of bones and wound healing, it will overcome the disadvantage related to PRF i.e, collection of blood via Phlebotomy, cost of Centrifuge machine used to make PRF. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Background :Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic progressive degenerative disorder consisting of degeneration and loss of articular cartilage with accompanying synovitis, subchondral bone remodelling, and osteophyte formation . It constitutes a major cause of disability with pain, stiffness, resulting in severe functional limitations . Although OA is a process of articular cartilage â€œwear and tearâ€, its changes are biochemically mediated , through an imbalance between intra-articular anabolic and catabolic cytokines . This results in cartilage loss, synovial inflammation and eventually leads to mechanical and biological dysfunction of the joint . The articular cartilage due to its avascular nature and the limited self-renewal capacity of chondrocytes has remarkably poorer regenerative ability than other tissues . Rationale :Current treatments for early phase of degenerative arthritis focus on relieving inflammation and pain , but have no effect on the natural progression of the disease because it does not improve the biochemical environment (homeostasis) of the joint. Conservative treatments including medications such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and steroids as well as supplements including glucosamine, chondroitin sulphate, omega-3 fatty acids , cannot alter the natural history of the disease.Steroids focus on relieving inflammation and pain Costly total knee arthroplasty (TKA) then follows when other treatment options have been exhausted , however patients experience a higher risk of death from mental and inflammatory musculoskeletal diseases, with a serious adverse event rate of 5.6% and a 0.2% mortality rate . Novelty:Recently, extraction of the mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) obtained from autologous bone marrow (BMA) followed by concentration was introduced represents the next generation of injectable intra-articular orthobiologic therapy for patients with cartilage disease . MSCs are multipotent cells that exhibit strong self-renewal abilities, combined with a differentiation capacity to form chondrocytes, adipocytes, and osteocytes . These cells also have very important local paracrine affects to alter their local microenvironment to conditions favourable for regeneration and repair . BMAC represents the safest and most feasible source of MSCs. Intra-articular application has resulted in pain reduction, functional improvement and/or tissue regeneration . BMAC is obtained through density gradient centrifugation of bone marrow aspirate (BMA) typically aspirated from the iliac crest . BMAC has been shown to provide elevated levels of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), MSCs, platelets, chemokines and cytokines including PDGF and TGF-Î² .These growth factors (GFs) are not only contained within the alpha granules of platelets, but they are also secreted by MSCs and can induce chondrogenesis of MSCs . GFs also initiate stem cell migration to the injury site and provide adhesion sites for the migrating stem cells . Moreover BMAC possesses in general, anti-inflammatory, angiogenic trophic and immunomodulatory properties that can potentially have anabolic and anti-inflammatory effects enhancing cartilage repair .There are only very few studies comparing steroids with BMAC. To date, there have been several studies that have looked at BMAC for the treatment of osteoarthritis, with conflicting results secondary to the differences and/or inconsistencies in methodologies used throughout the studies . column51: Alcohol is among the leading causes of preventable death worldwide, with 3 million deaths per year attributable to alcohol, this represents 5.3% of all deaths (WHO-Global status report on alcohol and health 2018). The morbidity and mortality associated with alcohol are largely due to the high rates of alcohol use disorder in the population. Alcohol use disorder is defined in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders, 5th edition (DSM-5) as a pattern of alcohol consumption, leading to problems associated with 2 or more of 11 potential symptoms of alcohol use disorder. The public health impacts of alcohol use extend far beyond those individuals who drink alcohol, engage in heavy alcohol use, and/or meet criteria for an alcohol use disorder. Alcohol use disorder is characterized by loss of control over alcohol drinking that is accompanied by changes in brain regions related to the execution of motivated behaviours and to the control of stress and emotionality (e.g., the midbrain, the limbic system, the prefrontal cortex, and the amygdala). Mechanisms of positive and negative reinforcement both play important roles with individual drinking behaviour being maintained by positive reinforcement (rewarding and desirable effects of alcohol) and/or negative reinforcement mechanisms (negative affective and physiological states that are relieved by alcohol consumption). Recent advances in neuromodulation techniques hold promise for the development of novel treatments for alcohol use disorder. Deep brain stimulation, transcranial magnetic stimulation, transcranial electrical stimulation (including transcranial direct current stimulation and transcranial alternating current stimulation), and real-time neurofeedback have recently been tested as potential treatments for addiction, although evidence in favour of these treatments is currently uncertain and focused mostly on intermediate targets (e.g., alcohol craving). The effect of transcranial stimulation would reduce feelings of craving by enhancing cognitive control and modulating striatal functions. In this context, alternative or adjunctive therapies such as tDCS and rTMS, two non-invasive brain stimulation techniques, may play a prominent role because of their ability to modulate focally the neuronal excitability of superficial brain regions and even deeper structures due to brain connectivity (Sauvaget A et al., 2015). | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Pressure injuries are common cause of morbidity, mortality and extended hospital stay among patients with spinal cord injuries. At present there are wide variety of methods to manage pressure injury but the quest for an inexpensive, safe and effective topical agent to treat pressure injury continues. Phenytoin is an effective anti-epileptic medication. The possibility of using phenytoin for wound healing was first recognised in 1939 when it was observed that patients receiving oral phenytoin had a side-effect of gingival hyperplasia. It has been reported that phenytoin may promote ulcer healing by stimulating the following processes: fibroblast proliferation, collagen deposition , vessel ingrowth , glucocorticoid antagonism and antibacterial activity as well as enhancing the number of macrophages in the wound. Therefore, this study intends to find if topical phenytoin could be used a safe, inexpensive , effective and non-invasive topical agent for healing pressure injuries. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: The assisted reproductive technology (ART) method of frozen embryo transfer (FET) is now often used to produce healthy babies. Adjunctive medications to enhance endometrial receptivity are being investigated, nevertheless, because implantation failure continues to be a major obstacle. Endometrial perfusion and responsiveness may be modulated by platelet-rich plasma (PRP), which is abundant in growth factors and cytokines. In order to assess the impact of PRP endometrial perfusion on the success of frozen embryo transfer, this abstract undertakes a meta-analysis of the literature. Research examining the effect of PRP on FET outcomes was included in the eligible papers, which also included prospective cohort studies and retrospective analyses. When comparing the clinical pregnancy rates of women undergoing FET with endometrial perfusion of PRP to controls, a pooled analysis of data from specific studies shows a substantial improvement (p < 0.05). Moreover, a dose-response relationship is suggested by the positive association shown by meta-regression analysis between the concentration of platelets in PRP and pregnancy outcomes. Subgroup studies that take into account the patient’s demographics, the cause of their infertility, and the methods used to prepare PRP offer valuable information on possible causes of heterogeneity and variances in treatment outcomes. Notably, there is no discernible rise in adverse events recorded across studies, suggesting that PRP treatment has a positive safety profile. Although the results indicate that PRP may be useful in improving endometrial receptivity and FET success, there are a number of limitations that should be taken into consideration when interpreting the results. These include limited sample sizes, heterogeneity in study designs, and variability in PRP preparation techniques. Larger sample sizes and more carefully planned RCTs are required in the future to confirm these results and clarify the best PRP delivery schedule for enhancing FET outcomes. column51: Haemorrhage contributes to a majority of trauma-related deaths globally (more than half of the annual 4.4 million trauma deaths worldwide) [1], while coagulopathy presents a serious challenge, affecting a significant proportion of trauma patients upon arrival at the emergency room (ER). Coagulopathy being present in approximately 25 to 35% of all trauma patients upon ER admission, represents a serious problem for major trauma patients and accounts for 40% of all trauma-related deaths which necessitates a strategy of early and rapid haemostatic treatment to prevent exsanguination. [2]. Currently one of the mainstay managements of such patients includes damage control resuscitation which advocates early blood transfusion along with judicial intravenous fluid administration and patients with higher class of shock may also warrant massive blood transfusion under Massive Haemorrhagic Protocol (MHP) [3]. Massive Blood Transfusion Protocol (MTP) refers to the rapid administration of large amounts of blood products (at least 6 units of pRBC) in fixed ratios (usually 1:1:1) for the management of haemorrhagic shock. It is a treatment for massive haemorrhage and can keep patients alive through volume and oxygen transport replacement while other methods of bleeding source control such as damage control surgery, abdominal packing, or any organ transplant is being carried out. MHP is a clinical pathway that brings together the right patient, right team, and right interventions at the right time points. It has been shown to improve patient outcomes and must incorporate the best available evidence and practices. The components of this protocol are best summarized in terms of 7 Ts: trigger, team, tranexamic acid, testing, transfusion, temperature, and termination. Both protocols are designed to expedite the provision of blood components based on best practices for the management of massively bleeding patients [3]. They are typically initiated based on clinical judgement, considering factors such as the rapidity of bleeding, the severity of haemorrhage or amount of blood lost, and the clinical stability of the patient [4]. The severe form of haemorrhagic shock can be defined as a critical medical emergency resulting from significant blood loss, that is, when the body loses a substantial amount of blood and the heart struggles to maintain circulation leading to the failure of vital systems. This condition can begin when approximately 20% of the total blood volume is lost [5]. The combination of severe haemorrhage, hypotension, hypothermia, and acidosis is also accompanied with acute and persistent loss of key coagulation factors such as fibrinogen which also contribute to dysregulation of haemostasis leading to acute traumatic coagulopathy and this understanding underscores the importance of prompt and precise intervention in managing such cases. Early recognition, and intervention with prompt and effective haemostatic treatment is crucial in managing these conditions while playing a vital role to prevent life-threatening blood loss and improving the chances of survival for severely injured individuals [6]. It is noted that low fibrinogen levels on admission are common in trauma patients, often falling below replacement thresholds recommended in major bleeding treatment guidelines. Major haemorrhage protocols (MHPs) play a crucial role in guiding the administration of blood components during resuscitation, aiming for a balanced transfusion of red blood cells, plasma, and platelet components to mimic whole blood concentrations but in trauma patients fibrinogen levels also need to be raised towards normal range to support coagulation in bleeding patients and concentrated fibrinogen products are essential for effective management [Davenport R et.al. 1], as fibrinogen plays a critical role in restoring haemostasis during haemorrhage, the evidence supporting its supplementation in bleeding patients is biologically plausible [7]. Three therapeutic options for fibrinogen supplementation include donor plasma, fibrinogen concentrate (FC), and cryoprecipitate (CRYO). Cryoprecipitate, containing approximately 32% of plasma fibrinogen, has a higher fibrinogen concentration compared to fresh frozen plasma (FFP) due to its small plasma volume. While cryoprecipitate was previously used in haemophilia-A treatment, its primary use today is to replenish fibrinogen in acquired bleeding and coagulopathy cases. However, a quantifiable serologic analysis based evidence depicting its impact is still lacking [8]. Coagulation profiles play a crucial role in managing trauma patients, especially those with severe injuries. The significance and applications range from early identification of coagulopathy and balanced transfusion strategy to monitoring coagulation status, with a goal to grasp coagulation status quickly for effective therapeutic strategies [9]. Thromboelastography (TEG) and Rotational Thromboelastometry (ROTEM) are viscoelastic assays (VEAs) that provide a comprehensive view of clot formation, strength, and lysis in whole blood and compared to traditional coagulation tests like PT (Prothrombin Time) and aPTT (Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time), provide a more holistic assessment of coagulation [10,11]. ROTEM based EXTEM Reagent contains tissue factor activator and this assay assesses the tissue factorâ€“initiated pathway of coagulation and provides information similar to the prothrombin time (PT) [11]. The integration of Rotational Thromboelastometry (ROTEM) into the definition of Acute Traumatic Coagulopathy (ATC) could enhance the detection of patients requiring Massive Transfusion (MT) and ROTEM has been used to diagnose coagulopathy and guide haemostatic therapy in trauma [12]. In Rotational Thromboelastometry (ROTEM), the K time (clotting time) is a crucial parameter that provides insights into the speed of clot formation, which can be indicative of coagulopathy [11]. In the context of trauma-induced coagulopathy, a prolonged K time could suggest a deficiency of fibrinogen or dysfunction of clotting factors, which can delay the initiation of clot formation. This delay can be critical in trauma patients, where rapid clot formation is necessary to prevent excessive bleeding [13]. Thus, in recent years, viscoelastic methods that assess the speed of clotting and quality of the clot, such as thromboelastometry devices such as the TEGÂ® and RoTemÂ® can provide information about fibrin formation, platelet activation, and clot retraction, hence successfully guiding haemostatic therapy [6]. column51: Aims and Objectives: We hypothesize that the insights on simulated short-term microgravity exposure will induce changes in cardiorespiratory and neuro-cognitive functions and will have broader applications, including potential benefits for sports performance and recovery. Therefore this study aims to investigate the impact of 6Â° HDBR, simulating microgravity, on cardiorespiratory and neuro-cognitive functions in healthy young adults. Methodology: Participants: Around 60 healthy adults, comprising 30 male and 30 female athletes and sedentary individuals, aged between 18 and 30 years will be selected through a convenient sampling method. The inclusion criteria of the participants will be healthy volunteers who are non-smokers, non-alcoholics and have no known diseases. Exclusion criteria included individuals who had Subjects undergoing any medication or suffered from cardiovascular, respiratory, and metabolic diseases, neurological disorders, recent history of surgery, or any other illness that could affect the functioning of the nervous or cardiovascular systems. The subjects will be informed about the methodology and a written informed consent will be obtained. Study Design & Protocol: This study employed a pre-test/post-test experimental design to investigate the impact of 6Â° head-down tilt bed rest (HDBR) simulating microgravity on cardiorespiratory and neuro-cognitive functions and its implications for sports performance and recovery. Acute and immediate effect of 6Â° HDBR on cardiorespiratory parameters, cardiac autonomic function will be assessed using breath-by-breath metabolic gas analyzer and heart rate belt. Neuro-cognitive functions will be assessed using a battery of standardized cognitive tests, including tests for memory, attention, executive function, and processing speed. Statistical Analysis: Statistical analyses will be performed using SPSS software. Paired t-tests will be used to compare pre- and post-HDBR measurements for both cardiorespiratory and neuro-cognitive parameters. column51: Dentinal hypersensitivity, caused by exposed dentinal tubules due to enamel or cementum wear, significantly affects patientsâ€™ daily lives by causing pain that disrupts sleep, work, and dietary habits. While self-applied desensitizing toothpastes like Colgate Sensitive Pro-relief, which contains 8% arginine, are commonly used, their primary disadvantage is the time needed for symptom relief. Irimedadi Oil, an Ayurvedic preparation with astringent, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory properties, is effective against various oral conditions, including dentinal hypersensitivity. A study reported that 26% of patients experienced relief after 10 days of using Irimedadi Oil, increasing to 76% after 21 days. If found effective, Irimedadi oil would be a natural, organic, herbal alternative for hypersensitivity patients. A Randomized controlled trial will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of Irimedadi Oil against Colgate Sensitive Pro-relief in patients with dental hypersensitivity. Patients from a dental outpatient department will be selected based on specific inclusion and exclusion criteria. A pilot study with 25 patients in both groups will be conducted for 10 days. This will help determine the sample size for a 21-day trial. In the study, 50 subjects will be randomly divided into two groups using by block randomization method, with one group receiving Irimedadi Oil and the other Colgate Sensitive Pro-relief. column51: The study, "Effectiveness of MTA, Biodentine, and Calcium Hydroxide in Open Apex Closure of Nonvital Immature Teeth," aims to assess the comparative effectiveness of three dental materialsâ€”mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA), Biodentine, and bioceramic repair materialsâ€”in facilitating apex closure in non-vital, immature teeth. Conducted as a triple-blinded, randomized controlled trial, the study involves 45 patients between 9 and 14 years old, each meeting specific inclusion criteria. Participants are randomly divided into three groups, each treated with one of the materials. The methodology includes a rigorous protocol, beginning with clinical and radiographic evaluation of non-vital immature teeth, followed by standardized endodontic procedures. Local anesthesia and isolation of the tooth are performed, after which each material is applied according to manufacturer guidelines. Throughout the study, apical closure is tracked through scheduled follow-ups at intervals of 1, 3, and 6 months. Radiographic assessments and clinical examinations are used to evaluate the degree of root development and apical closure, with additional analyses on treatment outcomes, including root canal wall thickening and apical barrier formation. The studyâ€™s design and randomization ensure robust data collection to facilitate comparison among the three materials. Ethical guidelines, including informed consent, are strictly followed to maintain participant safety and compliance, with clinical and radiographic assessments forming the primary outcome measures. column51: Wilson disease in children has a varied presentation. Wilson disease with acute liver failure is associated with very high mortality and morbidity. The standard therapy i.e chelation (with either D- penicillamine or trientene can be used as a temporizing agent to treat the enormous release of copper into the blood stream; however, substantial removal is not achieved for at least 1 to 3 months. Plasma exchange provides a means of rapid means of removal of copper. As per American Society for Apheresis, TPE in wilson disease with acute liver failure can rapidly remove an average of 20 mg of copper per TPE treatment. Decreased serum copper may decrease hemolysis, prevent progression of kidney failure and provide clinical stabilization. TPE can also remove large molecular weight toxins (aromatic amino acids, ammonia, endotoxins) and other factors, which may be responsible for hepatic coma. The frequency of said TPE is not defined as most evidence is based on case reports and case series. Copper is highly protein bound and the volume of distribution for copper is large. Under normal conditions, 90-95% of serum copper is ceruloplasmin-bound with the remaining 5-10% being nonceruloplasmin-bound. TPE efficiently removes both ceruloplasmin- and albumin-bound copper. FFP used for exchange can be helpful in treating the associated coagulopathy. TPE has been used as a bridge to liver transplantation as well as seen to improve survival with native liver, the optimum protocol for same remains uncertain. Study population: Children aged 3 to 18 years with Wilson disease (diagnosed as per Leipzig score >=4) with fulminant presentation (as defined by New Wilson Index>= 11 and INR >= 2.5 ). column51: Brief Summary of the Study Chronic wounds, such as diabetic foot ulcers, venous ulcers, and pressure ulcers, present significant healthcare challenges due to their resistance to standard treatments and associated complications like infections, necrosis, and amputations. Current management strategies often focus on symptom control rather than addressing underlying biological deficiencies. Amnion, derived from the innermost layer of the placenta, has gained attention as a potential therapeutic agent for enhancing wound healing. Rich in growth factors, extracellular matrix components, and cytokines, amnion exhibits anti-inflammatory, pro-regenerative, and immunomodulatory properties. Its use has shown promising results in preliminary studies, but there remains a need for robust evidence to establish its efficacy and safety in chronic wound management. This single-center prospective interventional study aims to evaluate the healing effects of processed human amnion applied as a dressing in patients with chronic non-healing wounds. Conducted at MS Ramaiah Hospitals, Bengaluru, the study will recruit 64 participants who meet specific inclusion criteria, such as chronic wounds persisting for at least four weeks despite standard care. Participants will receive amnion dressings, and outcomes will be assessed over a specified follow-up period. Primary outcomes include wound closure rates, while secondary outcomes focus on pain reduction, improvements in quality of life, and cost-effectiveness. Data will be analyzed using paired t-tests to assess the efficacy of amnion therapy. The studyâ€™s findings aim to provide valuable insights into the role of amnion in wound healing, contributing to the advancement of wound care practices and scientific understanding of tissue regeneration. This research could potentially establish amnion-based therapies as a standard of care for managing chronic wounds, improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare burdens. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Pregnancy is characterized by significant physiological adaptations, and maladaptive changes can increase the risk of gestational hypertensive conditions like pre-eclampsia (PE) and gestational hypertension (GHTN), which are leading causes of maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality globally. While exercise during pregnancy is generally recommended and has shown benefits for weight management and reduced risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), there’s a need for more research on its specific effects on blood pressure in at-risk populations and the optimal exercise parameters. The study aims to address the underutilization of preventive measures and effective management strategies for pre-eclampsia in India, where it contributes to approximately 15-20% of maternal deaths. The proposed non-pharmacological intervention, prenatal aerobic exercise, titled “A study to evaluate the effectiveness of prenatal aerobic exercise program on knowledge, attitude, exercise practices and blood pressure control among pregnant women at risk of pre-eclampsia attending outpatient department of Obstetrics & Gynecology in a tertiary care hospital” can be effective in controlling blood pressure. This study will employ a quantitative research approach with an quasi-experimental design involving an experimental and a control group. The target population is pregnant women at risk of pre-eclampsia, with a sample size of 58 antenatal women (29 in each group) to be recruited from the outpatient department of Obstetrics & Gynecology at AIIMS Mangalagiri. Participants will be selected based on inclusion criteria such as gestational age between 20 to 28 weeks and Gestosis score 3 or more than 3. The intervention group will receive a systematically designed prenatal aerobic exercise program, including educational sessions for 35 minutes and demonstration of selected aerobic exercises like side bends, hip circles, hamstring curls, tap and punch, and shoulder press jerk for 25 minutes followed by providing information leaflet for further study. The control group will receive routine care and same information containing leaflet given to the interventional group.
