column51: This study is a phase I-II, multicenter, prospective, openlabel, singlearm clinical study to evaluate the PK, efficacy, and safety of human plasma derived fibrinogen concentrate FIB Grifols in adult and pediatric subjects with congenital afibrinogenemia. Approximately 10 adult subjects (â‰¥18 years) with congenitalafibrinogenemia will be administered a single dose of study drug at 70 mg/kg body weight and will be followed for PK, efficacy, and safety assessments. After the safety of fibrinogen concentrate FIB Grifols is assessed in at least 10 adult subjects and no safety issues are raised by the sponsor, the study will start to enroll approximately 10 pediatric subjects (<18 years) who will be dosed with study drug and followed for PK, efficacy, and safety assessments. All enrolled subjects (both adult and pediatric) will have documented congenital fibrinogen deficiency manifested as afibrinogenemia but will not have received any fibrinogen-containing product therapy within the preceding 21 days before the infusion of study drug. All subjects (both adult and pediatric) will be infused with the investigational product at 70 mg/kg body weight. PK parameters that will be calculated from plasma fibrinogen levels measured at different time points include: in vivo recovery (IVR), area under the curve (AUC) calculated as AUC from zero to 14 days (AUC0-14days) and AUC from zero to infinity (AUC0-âˆž), maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), time to the observed maximum plasma concentration (tmax), half-life (t1/2), mean residence time (MRT), volume of distribution (Vd), and clearance (Cl). Hemostatic efficacy of the investigational product will be assessed by means of rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) measure of maximum clot firmness (MCF) at baseline and 1-hour post-infusion. Other thromboelastographic measures as well as standard coagulation tests will be also determined pre- and post-infusion. Clinical safety, viral safety, and immunogenicity will be assessed in this clinical trial. Safety variables include adverse events (AEs), vital signs, physical assessments, laboratory tests, viral markers, and antibodies against human fibrinogen. Allergic/hypersensitivity reactions and thrombotic events will be monitored during the study. Stopping criteria have been established for immunogenic and thrombogenic events. Briefly, if a confirmed, single case of any of these events is reported after a subject has been dosed with study drug, any further enrollment and dosing of subjects in the study will be suspended until the event can be adequately assessed by the sponsor. column28: The application of Investigator prepared Human Amniotic Membrane has already been used as a dressing material for burns wounds. Amnion will be obtained from Elective LSCS placentas and will be prepared in a sterile manner followed by storage in a solution of Crystalline Penicillin and Gentamycin at 4degrees C for a maximum of one week. After cleaning the wound with normal saline, a strip of amnion will be applied to one half of the burns wound and kept for as long as it takes for wound healing to occur (ie, approximately 2 weeks). Ideally the dressing material should come off on its own once the wound heals, as marked by wrinkling of the dressing and lifting off. Hence each will be compared with the other with respect to time to wound healing and scarring. | The application Collagen will be similar to that of Amnion. It also has already been in use as standard treatment in burn wounds. There are separate studies that have established that either of these can be used in burn wounds. In this study, the two are used side by side, each as an active control of the other. After cleaning the wound, the commercially prepared collagen (Available as a 10x15cm pre packaged sterile sheet) will be applied alongside the amnion, preferably each on opposite sides of the midline. Hence each will be compared with the other with respect to time to wound healing and scarring.

column51: After extraction, severe hard and soft tissue alteration takes place within the affected site of alveolar ridge.1 The three dimensional resorption process at extraction sites results in narrower ridges and reduced vertical height and lingual/palatal shifting of their long axis. Most of the dimensional alterations take place in the first 3 months following tooth removal.2 In the first 12 months after extraction, the height of alveolar ridge can diminish upto 50% because the alveolar bone resorbs especially on the buccal aspect.3 This change may lead to esthetic and functional disadvantages that compromise future implant placement particularly if the dental implant placement needs to be delayed for 6 months or longer. Hence it is crucial to preserve the dimensions and contour of the alveolar ridge after tooth extraction to achieve a predictable esthetic and functional prosthetic restoration. Preservation of the residual alveolar socket at the time of tooth extraction has been evaluated in many studies. Clinical, histologic and radiographic studies documented positive socket healing responses with autogenous bone, alloplasts and xenografts, whereas others reported poor results with bovine bone, decalcified freeze dried bone & autogenous bone.1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 Since they are associated with varying amounts of vital bone socket fill, comparison studies are useful to determine the amount of socket preservation that occurs with each material. A new class of alloplast materials, namely, calcium phosphate cements (CPC) raised certain hopes in periodontal repair in the early 1990s. These are aqueous based cements that get converted to hydroxyapatite upon setting. The combination of biocompatibility, osteoconductivity and restorability makes it a unique material for grafting bony defects.9 Platelet rich fibrin (PRF) is an autologous preparation of concentrated platelets created by centrifugation of a patientâ€™s blood. The use of PRF during surgical procedure is a current treatment concept used to accelerate wound healing and tissue maturation. It can be used directly as a clot or after compression as a strong membrane. 10 Based on these positive findings of calcium phosphate cement and platelet rich fibrin, the purpose of this study is to compare clinical and radiographic [Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT)] outcomes following grafting for post extraction ridge preservation in sites treated with platelet rich fibrin with or without calcium phosphate cement. Aim: To compare the use of platelet rich fibrin (PRF) with and without calcium phosphate cement in fresh extraction sockets by clinical and radiographic analyses. Objectives: 1. To evaluate horizontal and vertical ridge changes associated with PRF used with and without CPC at baseline and after 6 months using clinical and radiographic methods. 2. To compare horizontal and vertical ridge changes associated with PRF used with and without CPC using clinical and radiographic methods. 3. column51: Trastuzumab is a recombinant humanised IgG1 monoclonal antibody against the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). Intas Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Biopharma Division, Ahmedabad, India intends to develop a biosimilar version of Trastuzumab, marketed by Roche. column51: Romiplostim is a novel thrombopoiesis-stimulating protein that has been developed as a treatment for adults with thrombocytopenia associated with ITP. column51: Evaluation of antibacterial potential of a herbal mouth-rinse containing curry leaves extract on periodontal health AIM: To evaluate the anti-bacterial efficacy of a herbal mouthrinse containing 2.5% curry leaves extract on periodontal health MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 45 systemically healthy patients diagnosed with Chronic Periodontitis were included in the study. Group B: Commercially available 0.2% Chlorhexidine gluconate mouthrinse Group C: Mouthrinse containing 2.5% curry leaves extract The supra-gingival plaque samples of all subjects were collected by a single trained operator from two different sites in sterile ependoff tubes following standardized collection. Baseline scores for Colony Forming Units (CFU), Oral Hygiene Index- Simplified (OHI-S) and Modified Gingival Index (MGI) were recorded for each sample. Each subject underwent full mouth scaling by the same operator. They were provided the respective mouthrinse by a second operator to avoid bias. All subjects were instructed to rinse with 5ml of undiluted mouthrinse twice daily for two weeks. Plaque samples were taken from each subject from the same site on the 7th and 15th days and CFUâ€™s , OHI-S and MGI scores were re- recorded. RESULTS: 1. There was significant reduction in the OHI-S scores of the test group 2. The test group showed significant reduction of CFUâ€™s in the plaque samples from baseline to 15 days thus exhibiting potential antibacterial activity. column51: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) is common problem in preterm babies. Recently there have been various studies for and against an association between thrombocytopenia and PDA. A meta-analysis published in 2015 showed a marginally significant positive association between PDA and thrombocytopenia but these were all observational studies and there are no randomized controlled trials (RCT) on it. We decided to conduct an RCT to determine whether liberal platelet transfusion criteria achieve earlier PDA closure rates than standard restrictive platelet transfusion criteria among thrombocytopenic preterm neonates (<35 weeksâ€™ gestation) with hemodynamically significant PDA presenting within the first 14 days of life. Our primary objective is to determine whether liberal platelet transfusion criteria achieve earlier PDA closure rates within 120 hours compared to standard restrictive platelet transfusion criteria among thrombocytopenic preterm neonates (<35 weeksâ€™ gestation) with hemodynamically significant PDA presenting within the first 14 days of life. We will stratify the study population based on platelet count, i.e < 50000 and 50000-100000 per microlitre, and will randomly allocate participants into control and intervention group. Babies in intervention group will receive platelet transfusion to maintain platelet count above 100,000 per microloitre. Babies in control group will receive platelets only when clinically indicated and as per current standard indications. We will perform an echocardiogram at baseline to document a hemodynamically significant PDA (hsPDA) and then serially to look for closure of PDA. Medical management of PDA will be as per unit policy. column51: Research question 1. 1. Is there a beneficial effect of autologous platelet-rich plasma on hair growth in alopecia areata? 2. 2. Does autologous platelet-rich plasma alter the immune dysregulation in the lesional skin in alopecia areata? Aims and objectives Primary objective 1. 1. To evaluate the clinical efficacy of autologous platelet-rich plasma on hair growth in alopecia areata 2. 2. To evaluate the change in the mRNA expression profile of Th-1 (IFN-gamma, IL-2), Th2 (IL-4, IL-13), Th17 (IL-17, IL-22) and T-regulatory cells (Foxp-3) specific-markers in the lesional skin of alopecia areata after treatment with autologous platelet-rich plasma by real-time polymerase chain reaction Secondary objective 1. 1. To quantitatively evaluate the change in the Th-1 (IFN-gamma, IL-2), Th2 (IL-4, IL-13) and Th17 (IL-17, IL-22) cytokines and T-regulatory (Foxp-3) cell markers in the lesional skin of alopecia areata after treatment with autologous platelet-rich plasma by immunohistochemistry in a subset of patients Study design Randomized, investigator-blinded, placebo-controlled, half-head superiority trial Setting The study will be conducted in the department of dermatology and venereology, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, India. The study will be conducted after obtaining clearance from the institute ethics committee. Inclusion criteria 1. 1. Adult (age > 18 years) patients with alopecia areata of the scalp with at-least 25% scalp hair loss (SALT score 25%) of duration atleast 6 months with symmetrically distributed patches of hair loss on either side of the scalp Exclusion criteria 1. 1. Patients with alopecia areata with asymmetrically distributed patches of hair loss on scalp 2. 2. Patients with a SALT score less than 25% 3. 3. Patients using topical corticosteroids for 2 weeks or systemic immunosuppressants like systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, azathioprine or cyclosporine for 4 weeks 4. 4. Patients with a co-existent scalp or hair disorder 5. 5. Patients with thrombocytopenia (<1 lac/mm3) on baseline haematological evaluation 6. 6. Patients with underlying systemic illness, including autoimmune disorders 7. 7. Pregnant or lactating female patients 8. 8. Patients not consenting to participate in the study Methodology At the screening visit (visit 0), patients fulfilling the inclusion criteria will undergo a detailed history and examination, the particulars will be filled in a pre-structured proforma and a 3ml venous blood sample will be collected for complete blood count. At visit 1, clinical photographs will be taken for all the patients (four views: right side, left side, top and back) and severity of alopecia will be evaluated using the Severity of alopecia tool (SALT) by two independent observers based on the clinical photographs. A dermoscopic photomicrograph (using the HEINE Delta20T hand-held dermatoscope) will also be taken at visit 1 of a representative patch which will be evaluated by two independent observers for the number of dystrophic hair (exclamation mark hair, black dots, yellow dots and broken hair) in the patch. Randomization The side of the scalp receiving the active agent (platelet-rich plasma) or placebo will be randomized by block randomization method, treating each patient with 2 sides as a block. Numbers will be prepared by computer generated random tables. Envelopes will be opaque and sealed with each containing details of which preparation will be applied to alopecic patches on which side of the scalp. These envelopes will be made by a person not directly or indirectly involved in the study. One envelope will be taken per patient and opened by the dermatologist who will inject the platelet-rich plasma and normal saline (placebo) to the randomly assigned sides of the scalp. Only the dermatologist. injecting the platelet-rich plasma and placebo will be aware of the contents of the envelope and will not be blinded, as the color and consistency of the two injections are different. However, the two independent observers who will evaluate the treatment outcome will be blinded to the treatment arms. Preparation of autologous platelet-rich plasma After obtaining 40ml of whole blood by venipuncture method in acid citrate dextrose tubes, centrifugation of the blood using a soft spin (160 G for 10 minutes) will be done. The supernatant plasma containing platelets will be transferred into another sterile tube and then it will be centrifuged at a higher speed (400 G for 10 minutes) to obtain a platelet concentrate. The lower 1/3rd is platelet-rich plasma and the upper 2/3rd is platelet poor plasma. At the bottom of tube platelet pellets are formed. After this platelet-poor plasma is removed and platelet pellets are suspended in minimum quantity of plasma by gently shaking the tube to prepare the final platelet-rich plasma. Platelet-rich plasma will be prepared using the above described method at each of the three visits (visit 1, 2 and 3) when it is to be injected to alopecic patches on the scalp (side as determined by block randomization). The PRP will be activated with calcium gluconate in 1:9 ratio before injection. Starting from visit 1, patients will be treated with about 4ml of autologous platelet-rich plasma injected intra-dermally on one side of the scalp and equal amount of normal saline (placebo) on the other side (as per the randomized allocation table) at one-monthly interval for a total of 3 months (visits 1, 2 and 3) and will be asked to follow-up one monthly for 3 months after the 3rd injection of platelet-rich plasma. Clinical photographs and dermoscopic photomicrographs, identical to the manner as visit 1, will be taken at every subsequent visit will be subjected to independent evaluation by two observers blinded to treatment arms. column51: Despite advances in neonatal medicine, preterm and very low birth weight(VLBW) infants have substantial mortality and morbidity, often resulting from late-onset neonatal sepsis (LONS) and necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). This is attributed to a large extent to the immature immune system in these infants which predisposes them to increased risk of infection associated morbidity and mortality. Preterm infants are functionally immunodeficient , have immature intestinal mucosal barrier, require multiple invasive lines and procedures as part of their care. In addition to these, long term exposure to pathogens in neonatal intensive care unit(NICU) , overuse of antibiotics, delayed initiation of enteral feeds, presence of gastric tubes and multiple intravenous lines are factors that predispose VLBW infants to increased risks of sepsis and other co-morbidities like NEC, intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) etc. During breastfeeding or oral feeding of breast milk, the lymphoid cells in the oral mucosa get stimulated which leads to development of oral mucosa associated lymphoid tissue. The development of acquired immunity via breastfeeding and oral feeding has proven role in prevention of infection associated morbidity like LONS and NEC. Colostrum is the milk produced during the first few days after birth. It contains various substances that provide immunity in high concentration, to newborn babies. Even small volume of colostrums contains increased concentrations of secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA), growth factors, lactoferrin, anti-inflammatory cytokines, pro inflammatory cytokines, and other protective components, compared with mature breast milk. Motherâ€™s milk contains many biofactors which are immunomodulatory in nature. Lactoferrin, one of many biofactors contained in motherâ€™s milk, can protect against LONS and NEC via various mechanisms. Clinical instability and immaturity precludes enteral feeds for extremely premature infants in the first days of life. Even when started, in infants with gestation less than 31weeks, enteral feeds have to be given via a gastric tube because of undeveloped or poorly developed coordination of swallowing, breathing and sucking. This bypasses the infantâ€™s oropharynx and therefore, the infantâ€™s oropharynx is not exposed to protective (immune and trophic) milk biofactors until oral feeds are introduced several days later. To overcome this handicap of the immature infant, oral application of colostrum and mother’s own milk has been tried in very low birth weight infants and shown to be safe and feasible. It has been shown to improve the concentrations of several immune substances in the urine, saliva and tracheal secretions as well as decrease the levels of inflammatory substances like Interleukin-10. Oral application of colostrum has also shown benefits in achieving full feeds earlier and decreasing the duration of parenteral nutrition. we plan to conduct a randomized controlled trial of oral application of colostrum and placebo to study the effects on above listed clinical outcomes in preterm infants of 26 to 30 weeks gestation. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Systemic sclerosis is a multisystem disorder characterized by fibrosis of skin and interstitial tissues in various organs, leading to progressive loss of function in various organs, including the lung. Cyclophosphamide (Cyc), the mainstay of therapy1 is associated with significant side effects. Its effects seem to taper off at the end of 24 months as well2. Rituximab has been an alternative therapy for scleroderma and interstitial lung disease (ILD), shown to improve forced vital capacity.3 Vital capacity appears to be preserved in the long term as well4. Animal models point to B cells as important effectors in the pathogenesis of scleroderma. B-cells from tight skin mice, an animal model of scleroderma, display a "hyperresponsive" phenotype. In humans, B-cell infiltration is also present in most lung biopsies obtained from patients with scleroderma and interstitial lung disease5. Rituximab has been shown to improve, in open label studies, both dermatological manifestations and lung function in patients with scleroderma.4,6 In this study, we compare the efficacy and safety of rituximab (RTX) compared to cyclophosphamide in the treatment of systemic sclerosis. Background Justification and relevance of the proposed work Scleroderma or diffuse systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare multisystem autoimmune disease characterized by immune abnormalities, fibrosis of the skin and internal organs, and obliterative vasculopathy predominantly affecting the microvascular circulation. Estimated prevalence in the United States is 240 per million. Mean survival is approximately 12 years from diagnosis7. Prevalence in India is not precisely known. The mean age of onset, from a study in Northern India, is 32.7 years, with a male: female ratio of 1.5:2. Lung involvement was common; abnormalities found on the chest X-ray were ground glass appearance in 32 (45.7%), reticular shadows in 28 (40%), honeycombing in seven (10%), nodular opacity and paratracheal lymph nodes in three (4.2%)8. Cyclophosphamide has been the mainstay of therapy in scleroderma, with improvements shown in pulmonary function tests. With oral cyclophosphamide, the mean absolute difference in adjusted 12-month FVC percent predicted between the cyclophosphamide and placebo groups was 2.53 percent (95 percent confidence interval, 0.28 to 4.79 percent), favoring cyclophosphamide (P<0.03)1. IV pulse cyclophosphamide was also shown to have effects similar to oral cyclophosphamide9. However, effects of cyclophosphamide taper off at about a year after therapy2. In addition, cyclophosphamide has been associated with increase in the number of infections, is difficult to use be used in patients who want pregnancy and carries a risk of malignancy10. Rituximab, in uncontrolled studies, has been shown to be useful in the treatment of scleroderma, with significant improvements in total lung capacity and forced vital capacity4,3. Histologically, B cell infiltration has been demonstrated in both skin and lung biopsies in animal models as well as in the human disease phenotype. In the Tight Skin (TSK) murine model and Bleomycin (BLM) murine model, which approximate human disease, increased signaling of CD 19 tyrosine phosphorylation5. In a study of six patients with refractory scleroderma, significant reduction of anti-PDGF receptor autoantibodies was observed in the serum of all patients 3 months after treatment. Fibroblasts showed a significant downregulation of type I collagen gene expression and the intracellular signalling triggered by anti-PDGFR autoantibodies11. There has been no head to head clinical trial of cyclophosphamide vs. rituximab in the therapy of scleroderma. Hence, there is an urgent need for a randomized controlled trial to compare the therapies in scleroderma. Review of literature Tashkin et al first compared the effects of oral cyclophosphamide vs. placebo, and found that cyclophosphamide had a significant but modest beneficial effect on lung function, dyspnea, thickening of the skin, and the health-related quality of life1. Several researchers treated scleroderma with IV pulse cyclophosphamide, and achieved equivalent results12,9,13. Other modalities used to treat scleroderma included mycophenolate mofetil14, combination of cyclophosphamide and imatinib15 and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation16. Wolhem et al first described the presence of CD 20 positive B cells in scleroderma and suggested that rituximab may be beneficial in scleroderma17.Use of rituximab first appeared as case reports, in patients with myositis18, and refractory scleroderma19. In a pilot study by Lafyatis et al, rituximab was administered to 15 patients of scleroderma, but was seen to have little effect in the skin20. Daoussis et al treated 14 patients with rituximab, and found improvement in FVC compared to standard treatment3.Smith et al treated 8 patients with rituximab and demonstrated improvement of dermatological parameters including histology21. Research question/Hypothesis Our study aims to determine the efficacy and safety of rituximab compared to cyclophosphamide in the treatment of systemic sclerosis, with specific reference to lung and skin manifestations. The study is designed with a non- inferiority principle, the null hypothesis being that rituximab is not inferior to cyclophosphamide in the treatment of systemic sclerosis. Objectives To compare the safety and efficacy of rituximab compared to cyclophosphamide in the treatment of systemic sclerosis with reference to lung and skin manifestations. Materials and Methods This study is an open label, randomized, parallel group trial with a 1:1 allocation of patients in the cyclophosphamide and rituximab groups. Participants Patients will be recruited from the Rheumatology OPD and inpatient of IPGMER, Kolkata. Period of study: From January 2016 to June 2017 (18 months) Eligibility criteria: 1. Inclusion criteria a. Patients of diffuse systemic sclerosis, fulfilling the ACR classification criteria for diagnosis22, will be enrolled in the study. b. Patients will be positive for antiScl-70 c. Patients have ILD by HRCT criteria, or pulmonary function testing, or both. d. Age of patients will be from 18-60 years and of either sex. e. Female patients will be willing to adopt barrier contraception during this period. 2. Exclusion criteria a. Patients who have received cyclophosphamide or rituximab in the last year b. Patients with pregnancy or breast-feeding c. Patients with active systemic infections. d. Patients with hepatitis B and C, HIV infections, tuberculosis and overlap syndromes e. Patients with severe pulmonary hypertension (NYHA class IV) Methods 1. All patients will undergo a detailed history and physical examination at baseline, 2. Blood investigations: complete hemogram, electrolytes, urea, creatinine, liver function tests, viral serology 3. ANA profile 4. ECG, 5. Urinalysis and 6. Chest x-ray, 7. Mantoux test 8. Echodoppler study 9. HRCT chest, 10.Pulmonary function testing and a six-minute walk test will be done. 11.A modified Rodnan skin score will be done in all patients. 12.A skin biopsy will be taken from lesional skin (5mm) and examined with hematoxylin and eosin, and Massonâ€™s trichrome stain. A blinded histopathologist for assessment of skin fibrosis will examine these. 13.Mahler Baseline dyspnea Index and Transition Dyspnea Index23 (BDI/MDI) All these parameters (except the Mantoux test) will be repeated at 24 weeks to monitor outcomes. Intervention Patients will be randomized to the Cyc or RTX groups on the basis of a computer generated random number table in a 1:1 allocation ratio. Patients in the Cyc group will receive 500 mg/m2 of cyclophosphamide pulses IV every four weeks. Patients in the RTX group will receive two Rituximab pulses of 1000 mg at 0 and 15 days. Both groups will receive prednisolone 10 mg per day throughout the course. After six months, all patients will receive usual care including azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil for maintenance. Outcome Primary outcomes will be the 1. Change in forced vital capacity (FVC) at six months, and 2. Modified Rodnan skin scores at 6 months. Secondary outcome measures will be 1. Histologic appearance of fibrosis, 2. Six-minute walk test results, 3. Presence of pulmonary hypertension by echocardiographic criteria, 4. Change in BDI/TDI scores 5. Assessment of HRCT. Statistical methods Previous studies have demonstrated that, with cyclophosphamide, the drop in FVC is 1% with a standard deviation of 0.91. Assuming a non- inferiority trial design, and assuming an effect size of 0.8, we calculate the total number of patients to be recruited in both groups to be 16, with 8 in each. Appropriate statistical methods including non-parametric methods such as the Wilcoxon Mann Whitney test will be utilized for analysis for continuous variables, and Fischerâ€™s exact test for categorical variables. column51: In this study we hope to assess the efficacy a non pharmacological approachâ€”Yoga, as an add-on treatment modality in patients with moderate to severe depressive illness. Currently, cryopreserved homografts are considered to be the â€œGold standardâ€ for RVOT reconstruction followed by the use of Bovine Jugular Vein (BJV) xenografts with varying degrees of success and longevity. Early conduit failure and conduit regurgitation, accelerated graft degeneration due to immunological reaction are the areas that still need to be addressed. column51: The data from India on the clinical use of Rituximab in RA is sparse. We intend to explore this in a prospective manner in a routine clinical rheumatology setting and further explore the effectiveness of an additional dose of Rituximab (Ristova TM) in patients with inadequate clinical response to Methotrexate and other DMARDs. This is a non-commercial, investigator initiated pragmatic study. This study aims to assess the effectiveness of Rituximab and its Biosimilar, a standard of care B cell depleting biological DMARD in the management of patients of RA with active disease despite supervised standard of rheumatological care that includes methotrexate as a pivotal DMARD. Patients will continue on their stable background arthritis therapy which can include non steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID), low dose prednisolone (less than 10 mg daily) and selected DMARD (Methotrexate, HCQS and sulphasalazine). The primary efficacy endpoint will be proportion of patients achieving ACR 50 response at 24 weeks.Patients not responding adequately to the conventional two infusion regimen of 500 mg each of Rituximab by 6-8 weeks of initial treatment will be randomized to two groups. One group will be prescribed an additional 500 mg infusion of Rituximab plus 120 mg Methyl prednisolone. The other group will be prescribed only 120mg of Methylprednisolone. At month 3 all non responders will be given 120mg of Methylprednisolone. At month 6, responders will be continued with standard of care treatment, non responders will be randomized to two groups. One group will continue with standard of care and 1 additional dose of Methylprednisolone, the other group will be given Biosimilar Rituximab. At month 9 and 12, non responders will be randomized to two groups. One group will receive Biosimilar Rituximab plus 120 mg Methylprednisolone and other group will receive only 120mg Methyl prednisolone. Data from several published studies show that an initial standard infusion regimen (two infusions with a fortnight interval) can lead to a good disease control in RA lasting for several months. However, a proportion (almost 30-40%) of patients do not achieve a satisfactory response with conventional standard regimen of Rituximab and this is considered to be due to inadequate B cell depletion which is central to its mechanism of action. The adequacy of initial clinical response to Rituximab will be assessed using the standard American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 50% improvement index response. Patients will be assessed for effectiveness and safety using standard measures at regular intervals till completion of study at week 48-54. column51: Prandial insulin with faster-onset and/or faster-offset characteristics might reduce glycemic excursions and decrease the incidence of delayed postprandial hypoglycemia compared to currently available rapid-acting insulin analogs. The insulin analog, insulin lispro (HumalogÂ®), has been shown to be absorbed more quickly than regular human insulin (Humalog package insert, 2015). In healthy volunteers given subcutaneous (SC) doses of insulin lispro ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 U/kg, peak serum levels were seen 30 to 90 minutes after dosing. Rapid-acting insulins have been shown to have a more rapid onset of action compared to human insulin; however, the general consensus is that they are not rapid enough to match carbohydrate absorption and many patients are unable to achieve optimal glycemic control. An ultra-rapidacting prandial insulin with pharmacokinetic (PK) and glucodynamic (GD) profiles that demonstrate faster absorption and onset of action, may better match carbohydrate absorption and lead to improved postprandial control. The time action profile of a rapid-acting insulin could be enhanced through the addition of excipients to an existing formulation to increase capillary blood flow and/or enhance vascular permeability. An ultra-rapid insulin (URI) would be useful in the treatment of type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) when delivered by multiple daily injections (MDI), by continuous SC insulin infusion (CSII), and in the development of closed loop insulin delivery systems. column51: Background: The immediate placement of dental implant into the extraction socket avoids the undesirable resorption of alveolar bone volume and thus renders favourable implant placement. This technique offers advantages such as minimizes the number of surgical procedures by combining extraction, implant placement and bone grafting in a single session. Often immediate implants are deferred or avoided at a site (periodontal or endodontic) where infection is present because of the fear of failure possibly due to bacterial contamination of implant surface at the initial stages. Recent literature have concluded that similar success rates have been reported for immediate implants placed in infected sites compared to non-infected sites provided control of infections with thorough alveolar curettage and irrigation and use of antibiotics.1-5 The use of platelet rich in growth factors are considered as safe, effective and predictable treatment option for the rehabilitation with success rate up to 98.4% after one year.6 Histologically, it is observed that numerous newly proliferative vascular endothelial cells and regenerative molecules are present at the site of inflammation. Autologous platelet rich in growth factors (PRGFs) has been proposed as an aid to enhance regeneration of osseous tissues in oral surgery.7 Several in vitro studies, animal experiments, and clinical studies have shown that platelet-derived growth factors can effectively trigger stimulation of osseous and soft tissue regeneration, as well as reduce inflammation, pain, and unwanted side effects.1 The elimination of apical infections through mechanical debridement with systemic medication and incorporation of growth factors in the healing socket with immediate implant placement is actually beneficial in clinical conditions is still unknown. Till date there are no studies regarding the adjunctive role of second generation growth factors i.e. PRF to decalcified freeze dried allograft in immediate implant placement in chronic periapical infection sites. Hence, this study was aimed to assess the survival of immediate implant placement in an extraction site exhibiting chronic periapical lesions and PRF as an adjunct to decalcified freeze dried allograft. Aims: To assess the outcome of immeditely placed implants at the tooth extraction sites with the presence of periapical infection.. Objectives: To assess and compare the bone levels on proximal and facial aspect after immedite implant placement in periapical infected sites and 12 months after final restoration with platelet-rich-fibrin and decalcified freezed dried bone allograft. To assess and compare the interdental palliae levels after immedite implant placement in periapical infected sites, 6- and 12-months after final restoration with platelet-rich-fibrin and decalcified freezed dried bone allograft. To assess survival of immediate implant placement in fresh extraction with periapical infection assoicated with platelet-rich-fibrin and decalcified freezed dried bone allograft. column51: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding remains one of the most common surgical emergencies with high mortality rates even in developed countries. Bleeding may be due to variceal causes or non variceal causes for which blood and blood component products have to be transfused depending on the amount of blood loss. Marik PE and Corwin HL, in 2008, concluded that RBC transfusions are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. 8 A study by Lacroix J et al done in 2007 in a paediatric ICU setting has shown that in stable, critically ill children, a haemoglobin threshold of 7g/dl for packed cell transfusion has not increased the adverse outcomes and decreased the use of blood supplies. 6 Carson JL et al in 2011 studied restrictive or liberal transfusion in high risk patients after hip surgery concluded that liberal transfusion did not reduce the morbidity or mortality when compared to a restrictive transfusion strategy. Hebert PC and Carson JL in their review of literature have concluded that restrictive transfusion with a transfusion threshold of 7g/dl should be the recommended cut off for transfusion in all critically ill patients. However, they also stated that a higher threshold for transfusion (9-10g/dl) is recommended for patients with acute coronary syndromes due to increased myocardial oxygen demand. In a study done by Villanueva et al, an absolute reduction of 4% mortality was documented with restrictive transfusion guidelines when compared to liberal transfusion therapy in patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Few studies are available evaluating the potential benefit of restrictive Vs. liberal transfusions. Inconsistencies exist among the available results and well conducted randomized controlled trials are required to ascertain the role of haemoglobin threshold to decide the blood transfusion in upper gastro intestinal bleeding. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Spondyloarthritis (SpA) is an HLA B27 associated heterogeneous group of chronic inter-related inflammatory arthropathies affecting predominantly the spine but also peripheral joints, entheses and certain extra-articular sites. Axial SpA including Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) is the most prevalent subtype of the spectrum having grave prognosis. Classical clinical features of AS are onset in younger group of population with Persisting and progressive inflammatory back pain causing significant stiffness and limitation of activities. It may be associated with peripheral arthritis and extraarticular manifestations. If not intervened early, leads to progressive spinal deformity, ultimately ankylosis of axial joints i. e. column51: The present study was conducted to evaluate the role of Aloe vera as an adjuvant to lycopene in the treatment of OSMF. The patients were randomly divided into two groups, Group A (lycopene) and group B (lycopene and Aloe vera). Group A was administered 4mg lycopene twice daily and group B was administered lycopene 4 mg and 10ml Aloe vera twice daily. 17 patients in group A and 12 patients in group B completed the trial for 2 months. The patients were evaluated for reduction in burning sensation, improvement in mouth opening, tongue protrusion and cheek flexibility.The percentage of reduction in burning sensation was calculated. Comparison within and between the groups using ANOVA and Post hoc Tukeys test was done. Complete reduction of burning sensation was reported in 52.9% in group A and 58.9% in group B. The percentage of reduction in burning sensation in group A and B was 78.87 %, 81.96%. The percentage of improvement in mouth opening in group A and B was 0.645%, 3.896%. The improvement in tongue protrusion in group A and B was 0.433% and 0.747%. The improvement in cheek flexibility was 0.333% and 0.335%. A significant improvement was found between both group A and B from baseline and completion of treatment. However no significance was found when comparison was done between the groups. There was no significant improvement in mouth opening, tongue protrusion and cheek flexibility in either of the groups. The results of the study suggest that there was no significant benefit of adding Aloe vera to lycopene in managing the symptoms of OSMF. column51: Focal segmental glomeruloselerosis (FSGS) and minimal change disease (MCD) are two most important cause of adult onset nephrotic syndrome. They can progress to ESRD. More the proteinuria more chance to progress to ESRD. In adult the remission rate is low than children and relapse rate is high. Nephrotic syndrome due to underlying minimal change disease (MCD) or focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) remains a therapeutic challenge for the treating physician. A high proportion of initial steroid responsive patients develop a steroid-dependent or steroid-resistant disease course necessitating the use of a high cumulative dose of steroids. As steroids per se exhibit an unfavourable spectrum of side effects, second or third-line immunosuppressive treatment options such as calcineurin inhibitors, mycophenolate mofetil, alkylating agents are often required in these patients to spare and reduce the side effects of steroid. There are, however, limitations to these alternative agents due to toxicity attributable to their use. In steroid resistant MCD and FSGS the first line treatment is calcineurin inhibitor. Among them tacrolimus is a well-known entity. Tacrolimus is a macrolide immunosuppressant and calcineurin inhibitor that has immunosuppressant properties similar to cyclosporine and has a relatively selective inhibitory action on CD4 T-helper lymphocyte activation and proliferation. Tacrolimus has also antiproteinuric effect. As the alternative medication has their own toxic effect researcher are finding other novel agent with good efficacy and better side effect profile. In the search some drug found which shows benefit in FSGS and MCD. column51: Introduction: Proximal hypospadias repair has many postoperative complications such as urethrocutaneous fistulae, wound dehiscence, and urethral stricture. The beneficial effect of estrogen to promote wound healing has been known. We designed a study to determine whether preoperative stimulation of tissue with estrogen can reduce the postoperative complications associated with wound healing in patients undergoing hypospadias repair. Methods: Patients with proximal hypospadias requiring two-stage repairs (chordee correction followed by urethral tubularization) were randomized to estrogen and control groups before the second stage of surgery. In the former, topical estrogen cream (0.5 mg of estriol) was applied to the ventral penis for a month, whereas normal saline gel was applied to the latter; the urethroplasty was carried out thereafter. Patients were followed up for complications. Results: There were 29 patients in the estrogen group and 31 in the placebo group after the exclusion criteria were met. There was no significant difference in the overall postoperative complications between the estrogen group (44.8%) and the placebo group (51.6%). The occurrence of urethrocutaneous fistula (37.9% vs. 51.6%) and dehiscence (41.4% vs. 45.2%) was not significantly different between the estrogen and placebo groups. Neourethral stricture occurred in four patients in the estrogen group, while none of the patients in the placebo group developed stricture. Conclusions: The preoperative application of topical estrogen cream to the ventral penis failed to demonstrate any significant effect on wound healing and complications. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Rationale: Several methods have been devised to accelerate the rate of tooth movement during orthodontic treatment which include local administration of cytokines, physical methods and surgical methods. Recently, it has been found that Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) increases the rate of orthodontic tooth movement. PRP is an autologous concentration of platelets in a small volume of plasma. It has a high concentration of growth factors which include platelet derived growth factors, fibroblast growth factor, vascular endothelial growth factor, epithelial growth factor and few others. These growth factors enhance mitogenesis, angiogenesis, chemotaxis, cell differentiation and bone remodelling. Aims and Objectives: To evaluate the effect of PRP on rate of tooth movement in canine retraction. Objectives of this study is to evaluate the amount of extraction space closure during canine retraction in experimental and control side and to compare the same. Setting: Department of Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopaedics, PGIDS, Rohtak. Study Design: Prospective, single blind, split-mouth, randomized clinical study Time frame: 12 months Population/participant: Inclusion criteria:- Patients with age between 15-25 years, requiring bilateral extraction of maxillary 1st premolars, with platelet count above 1,00,000 per ml and good oral hygiene. Exclusion Criteria:- Patients with thrombocytopenia (platelet count less than 1,00,000 per ml), clotting or bleeding disorders, systemic diseases, presence of any signs and symptoms of gingival and periodontal diseases, long-term drug history, evidence of bone loss, smoking habit, any untreated carious lesions. Sample size: a sample size of 12 patients Method of study: Patients who met the inclusion criteria will be selected for the study. Treatment will be initiated by bonding 0.022â€ slot MBT straight wire appliance. Space closure will be carried out with 0.017â€x 0.025â€ SS wires using closed coil NiTi springs and Transpalatal Arch- 20gauge(0.9mm) as anchorage unit. 10ml of venous blood sample from each patient will be collected in a sterile test tube. 1ml of 10% Sodium Citrate will be used as anticoagulant. One ml of the whole blood will be sent to the laboratory for the calculation of platelet count. The remaining 9ml of blood will be used for the preparation of PRP. PRP will be prepared by the method of double spin centrifugation. 1ml of PRP will be obtained from which 0.2 ml will be sent to the laboratory for analysis of platelet count and 0.8 ml will be injected submucosally into the buccal vestibular mucosa distal to the canine tooth on the experimental side. Outcome Measures: The outcome variables will be the rate of canine retraction measured in millimeters. Statistical Analysis: Data will be checked for normality. If normally distributed then paired t test will be applied. If not normally distributed then wilcoxon signed rank test will be applied. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a life long disease and need prolonged medication and specialized care. Biological agents are extremely effective but limited by side effects and cost. Is it possible to induce a prolonged remission or a low disease activity after an intensive course of a biological agent and follow patients with a lesser intense medication plan? The follow up management may include symptomatic drugs and or standard oral conventional DMARD. This hypothesis has been tested by the current investigator several years ago with innovator anti-TNF agents etanercept and infliximab. This kind of strategy was not easy to accept for scientific scrutiny and evaluation because of various reasons, more to do with economics than science. However, recently, some initiatives have been taken in the World to study a drug free control of disease after an intensive period of using biologic agents. Overall, this short term treatment strategy has an important socioeconomic appeal in the Indian setting. It is against this perspective, that the current study is designed. In the current pragmatic drug trial study, Exemptiaâ„¢ is being evaluated to treat symptomatic AS. The protocol is designed to define its role as an induction therapy wherein a short course may lead to an extended drug free asymptomatic or low disease activity state. This is a non-commercial, investigator initiated pragmatic study. 50 patients will be enrolled in a 12 month study and evaluated at regular intervals for effectiveness and safety at 4, 8,12, 24, 36 and 48 weeks. Injection Adalimumab as a biological DMARD will be administered during the initial 12 weeks. Patients showing inadequate response at 12 weeks end point will be randomized to either receive a further 2 doses of Adalimumab or continue symptomatic treatment. Inadequate response to Adalimumab will be assessed using ASAS 20. All patients will receive a standard of care treatment including pain relieving medication and non steroidal anti inflammatory drug as per the discretion of the study rheumatologist. column51: Type of Study: Experimental ; clinical; single center study Aims & objectives : To apply photo acoustic and fluorescence techniques to differentially diagnose lumps in the breast a. To record photo acoustic and fluorescence spectra of normal, benign and malignant breast tissue b. To apply photo acoustic and fluorescence techniques to discriminate lumps in the breast - benign, malignant and others by core needle biopsy and fine needle aspiration cytology. Hypothesis Techniques other than histopathology exist to make a diagnosis (usually subcellular markers) and it is feasible, using laser to optically document spectra and differentiate normal from malignant tissue (based on subcellular markers) . Justification for study : Breast cancer is one of the most commonly diagnosed cancers among women in the world and also it is one of the leading causes of deaths from cancer in the female population. However, when detected in early stage, it is one of the most treatable forms of cancer. Therefore, fluorescence technologies and photoacoustics could be highly beneficial in early detection and timely treatment of cancer, as it well reduce reporting time and potentially be objective and machine read rather than subjective and depending on the expertise of a pathologist. Study period: 2 years Sample size : 60 Materials and methods: Sample collection - Tissue : FNAC specimens and core needle biopsy specimen are obtained in ex-vivo surgical tissue of normal, benign and malignant areas at the time of surgery Transport and storage : Samples in PBS (due precaution is taken for accurate labeling) are personally taken (to avoid delay) to the laboratory. The samples are processed (washed in saline to remove blood/clots, diced, placed in labeled plastic centrifuge tubes) The sample can then be frozen using liquid nitrogen and stored in a deep freezer at - 85 0 , if required. The sample is thawed to room temperature before analysis. a) Inclusion criteria: Patients diagnosed with benign or malignant breast lumps b) Information that will be accessed: Pathology reports and medical records c) Statistical methods/ scales being used to implicate causality Detailed description of procedure / processes: Patients coming to the Department of general Surgery, KMC Hospital, Manipal with clinical features suggestive of breast lump will be seen by consultant surgeon. Once a clinical diagnosis is made by consultant surgeon and a surgical intervention is confirmed by the particular consultant surgeon, PI will take informed consent from the patient. If the patient is willing, she will be enrolled into the study. During the surgery, after the specimen is removed by the consultant surgeon as part of standard of care, the samples will be harvested by the PI (from the excised specimen â€“ ex vivo). For FNAC- a needle will be passed into the lump 5 times and the cells that are obtained is placed into a test tube with PBS. For core needle, 3 approximately 0.2x 0.5cm linear strips of tissue is obtained by using a dedicated needle. Adjacent normal tissue and lymph nodes will be harvested similarly. No distortion of the specimen will occur that may jeopardize any future routine HPE analysis The harvested samples will be sent to the biophysics laboratory for analysis using photoacoustic and fluorescence spectrometry. Outcome measures: Based on the results i.e sensitivity , specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value of photo acoustics and fluorescence spectrometry to benign, malignant and normal respectively will be determined. Potential risks and benefits : Risks â€“ This is a prospective interventional study and carries only minimal risk as the sample is obtained from the tissue removed for standard of care provided. Benefits â€“ There is no direct benefit to the patient but the results may help future patients with a similar complaints. Ethical considerations and methods to address issues: This is an experimental study. The data from standard of care investigations will be obtained from the patientâ€™s record through the hospital information system and medical records. column51: Successful tissue regeneration requires that the reparative cells should posses the potential to differentiate between the phenotypes needed to restore the damaged site and also a micro-environment that can support the proliferation and differentiation of those cells. column51: This clinical study of the efficacy and safety of BCD-057 and HumiraÂ® in patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis is a multicenter double-blind randomized parallel-group study with an active comparator (Phase III). column51: This is an open-labeled, prospective, non-comparative, interventional postmarketing study in patients indicated and treated with marketing formulation of Hetero-Rituximab. The present study will gather the data of at least 200 patients. The primary objective is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of Rituximab under post marketing phase. The secondary objectives are to evaluate the immunogenicity and efficacy of Rituximab under post marketing phase. All patients will be monitored for significant clinical signs and symptoms and laboratory abnormalities during treatment. column51: Presently immunotherapy in the form of Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) and Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE) is considered as the first line treatment for Guillain Barre Syndrome (GBS) along with supportive management and has been supported by many randomized clinical trials done so far. A rise in medical expenses has a direct bearing on national as well patientâ€™s household budget. Hence healthcare policies are now being framed by taking consideration the cost-effectiveness along with clinical benefits and cost economically if both treatment option showing equal health outcomes for a particular treatment modality. Therapeutic Plasma Exchange and Intravenous Immunoglobulin both are first-line treatments for Guillain Barre Syndrome; however, there is a significant difference in cost. We undertook this study to assess the cost minimization for treating Guillain Barre Syndrome patients. Although both the treatment options (TPE and IVIG) are in use in different parts of the world, however, treatment cost differs due to differences in health care policies, infrastructure, and settings. Hence it is considered worthwhile to do a prospective randomized comparative cost-effective analysis of the outcomes of these two treatment modalities in our settings with an objective to assess the incremental cost-effectiveness of treating GBS patient with IVIG as compared to TPE. Results: Among the 40 patients enrolled in the study, 27(67.4%) were male and 13 (32.5%) were female (p=.305). Mean age of patients in IVIG group was 33.42 Â± 14.72 years and in TPE group was 34.81 Â± 20.54 years (p= 0.80) with an overall mean of 33.98 Â± 17.05 years. Mean weight of patients in IVIG group was 62.62 Â± 13.22 kg and in TPE group was 54.88 Â± 10.96 kg (p= 0.60). Mean duration of illness before starting of treatment was 5.71 Â± 3.8 in IVIG group and 5.88Â± 3.03 in TPE group with an overall mean of 5.77 Â± 3.49 days. No significant difference was observed in baseline demographic profile of both the study groups. Treatment was done with mean IVIG dose of 124.17 Â± 27.65 grams per patient and the mean number of TPE procedure done per patient was 4.75 Â± 0.58 exchanging one plasma volume in each procedure. Mean duration of hospital stay was 15.33 Â± 13.89 days in IVIG group and 17.88 Â± 10.13 days in TPE group with an overall mean of 16.35 Â± 12.44 days (although this increased the health system related cost in TPE group due to nature of treatment i.e. alternate day TPE) and was not statistically significant (p= 0.063). Mean GBS Disability score in IVIG group was 4.17 Â± 0.38 and in TPE group was 4.25 Â± 0.45 implying statistically similar pattern and grades of illness at the onset of treatment (p=0.53). Overall 12 patients (30%) required mechanical ventilation before starting the treatment out of which 7 were in IVIG group and 5 were in TPE group. Till the end of two weeks, there was no statistically significant neuromuscular and functional recovery as revealed by the difference in GBS Disability Score observed in TPE groups from baseline, but this was statistically significant in IVIG group (p=0.036). Both treatment options were found to be equally efficacious in terms of neurological improvement during the course of treatment as revealed by statistical analysis by comparing GBS Disability scores. Overall INR 86,685 ($1,700) i.e. 53% higher cost was observed in IVIG group without any concomitant health outcome benefit. column51: This is a double-blind, randomized, single-dose, placebo-controlled study of ASN100 for the prevention of S. aureus pneumonia in mechanically ventilated subjects who are heavily colonized with S. aureus. This will be a global study conducted at approximately 70 sites. Subjects will be screened for eligibility; once an Informed Consent Form (ICF) is signed and all entry criteria are met, a subject is considered to be enrolled in the study. All enrolled subjects will undergo an observational stage evaluating endotracheal colonization. Subjects who are randomized will undergo a treatment, monitoring, and follow-up period. Approximately 2250 eligible subjects who meet all of the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria will be screened daily (while mechanically ventilated) for up to 8 days to identify those subjects who are heavily colonized with S. aureus. Upon determination of eligibility, approximately 354 subjects will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to 1 of 2 treatment groups i.e ASN 100 or placebo. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of a single dose of ASN100 (administered as ASN-1 and ASN-2 components) versus placebo for the prevention of S. aureus pneumonia in mechanically ventilated subjects who are heavily colonized with S. aureus. The secondary objectives of this study are to compare the duration of mechanical ventilation, length of stay in the intensive care unit (ICU), determine the serum pharmacokinetics (PK), compare 28-day all-cause mortality post-treatment in subjects treated with ASN100 versus placebo. column51: Background of the study Newborn deserves the best Nutrition, Improved Survival, Optimum Development and healthy life. Breast milk can do this miracle The benefits of breastmilk have encouraged the establishment of healthy people breastfeeding goals. Although rates of initiation have increased however breast feeding at time points after initiation are well below the target. This is more commonly seen in motherâ€™s with preterm infants who have poor infant suck and latching on the breast. Breast milk expression has proven to be helpful in establishing and continuing the breast feeding. Women can express milk by hand using specific hand movements to stimulate the flow of milk in their breasts. No equipment is needed, other than something to collect the milk in. Most women will need a bit of time and practice to get used to it. Expression of breast milk using breast pumps create suction pressure on the outside of the nipple, which pulls or sucks milk out of the breast. A bit of practice is often needed to get used to these too. Electric pumps of various sizes are also available. Some are battery operated. It is usually possible to regulate the pumpâ€™s suction strength. Many electric pumps can be used on both breasts at the same time. Though the breast milk can be expressed either by pump or manually, the method of milk expression has an impact on the quantity and macronutrient composition of breast milk is unknown. There are not many studies related to the effect of type of milk expression on the quantity and composition of the breast milk. The fat content of the expressed breast milk can be found out using a creamatocrit technique which represents the lipid concentration of breast milk. As a result creamatocrit technique could be applied in the nutrition plan for premature infants who are exclusively fed by breast milk. A study done by H Yu Lin and et al (2010) revealed efficacy of creamatocrit technique in evaluation of fat content and calories in expressed breast milk for premature infants. A study done to evaluate the effect of type of milk expression on the quantity and fat content of the expressed breast milk will help to realize the effect in a scientific way and help to formulate the policies. Need for the study A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step Breast Milk Natureâ€™s Protection for the Baby One million infant lives can be saved by just breast feeding in the 1st Hour following the birth of the child. If mothers and families comprehend the benefits of breast feeding for six months, it can save the life of 2,50,000 babies annually. Breast milk is a large pool of various carbohydrates, fats, proteins, minerals, immunoglobulins etc. Infants who are premature and not latching and sucking well are at early risk of deprivation of benefits of breast milk. So expression of breast milk is done by either hand expression or electric breast pump method. Though some studies have shown that breast pumping removes more milk than hand expression, some have observed that hand expression may result in larger milk volumes immediately after birth. An experimental study be manual Mangel L and et al (2015) on 21 mothers of 21 new born babies 48-72 hours post delivery have concluded that manually expressed human milk had higher fat content than milk expressed by electric breast pump. The difference is due to the presence of hind milk in manually expressed milk because the technique of massaging the breast during manual expression is more likely than the pump to eject the hind milk. Though this study is done the difference between the effect of breast pumping and the effect of early hand expression on the quantity and fat content is unknown. Expression of breast milk is an important aspect in care of babies in NICU. It requires a lot of motivation and encouragement of the mother. Manual expression is an age old method being practiced by mothers. Use of electric breast pump is a technological advancement which has been found equally effective. In this motherâ€™s effort is less. Either of the way the method should be beneficial for the mother. Based on the above research studies and personal experiences in the NICU and post natal wards the investigator felt a need to evaluate the effect of manual expression and expression by electric breast pump on the quantity and fat content of the expressed breast milk. Mother is the most important person caring for the baby. The researcher felt that the result of this study will help the mother in practicing the appropriate method where it will be most effective and less effort involved. Also the investigator felt that the study will help to realize the effect in a scientific way and help to formulate policies or standard operating procedures regarding manual or electrical expression or combination of both for the maximum benefit of the new born. It will also help us to improve nursing practice by evidence based practices. It is proven that composition of term milk is different than that of preterm milk. Though, expression of breast milk by manual as well as breast pump are both acceptable and regularly practiced in NICU and nursery, there are not many studies done in India and abroad to find out which method is better in terms of quantity and composition of milk. There are many nursing procedures which are being practiced in the hospitals for many years whose benefit is not questioned / proven. Through this study, in its unique way, the nurse researcher desires to strengthen the knowledge base regarding a simple, regularly practiced procedure of expression of breast milk by two techniques with evidences. Research Problem A comparative study to assess the quantity and fat content of expressed breast milk by Manual expression Versus electric breast pump in motherâ€™s with new born babies admitted in a selected tertiary care hospital. Primary objective of the study To assess the quantity and fat content of motherâ€™s expressed breast milk by manual expression Versus electric breast pump. Objectives To assess the quantity and fat content of expressed breast milk of mothers by manual method. To assess the quantity and fat content of expressed breast milk of mothers by .electric breast pump. To compare the quantity and fat content of expressed breast milk by both the methods. Operational Definitions Assess: It refers to an activity to evaluate how to express breast milk. Expressed breast milk: It refers to the milk which the mother expels from her breast.(c) Manual Expression: Something which is done with the hands. In this study it means expressing breast milk with the hands. Electric Breast Pump: It refers to a mechanical device powered by batteries or electricity from the grid that extracts milk from the breasts of a lactating woman. Quantity: It refers to the measurable amount of breast milk expressed by a mother. (f) Newborn babies: It refers to babies between 0-28 days of birth. Hypothesis H0 There will be no difference in quantity and fat content of expressed breast milk using manual expression Versus electric breast pump method in motherâ€™s with new born babies admitted in selected tertiary care hospital. H1 There will be difference in quantity and fat content of expressed breast milk using manual expression Versus electric breast pump method in motherâ€™s with new born babies admitted in selected tertiary care hospital. Use of electric breast pump is a technological advancement and has been found equally effective where motherâ€™s effort is less or when they are having physical inhibition such as sore nipples, retracted nipples, engorgement etc. Â· The study of comparing the two will help to realize the effect in a scientific way and help to formulate policies or Standard operating procedures regarding manual / electrical expression. Review of Literature The review of literature in a research report is a summary of current knowledge about a particular problem and includes what is known and not known about the problem. The literature is reviewed to broaden the understanding and gain insight into the problem under the study. 1. An experimental study(2015) was conducted to evaluate the effect of milk expression method (manual expression versus electric pump)on the composition of breast milk. The study was done on 21 mothers of 21 new born babies 48-72 hours post delivery. The women were randomly assigned to express breast milk manually followed by pump or in reverse order. The researcher concluded that manually expressed human milk had higher fat content than milk expressed by electric pump. The difference is due to the presence of hind milk in manually expressed milk because the technique of massaging the breast during manual expression is more likely than the pump to eject hind milk, which has been shown to have higher fat content than foremilk. 2. A randomized controlled trial study(2011) was done to compare hand expression with breast pump for mothers of term newborns feeding poorly at 12-36 hrs after birth.68 mothers of 12-36h newborns were randomly assigned 15 minutes of electric breast pumping and 15 minutes of hand expression. The median volume of expressed milk (range) was 0.5 (0â€“5) ml for hand expressing mothers and 1 (0â€“40) ml for pumping mothers (p=0.07). Maternal pain, breastfeeding confidence and Breast milk expression experience did not differ by intervention. At 2 months, mothers assigned to hand expression were more likely to be breastfeeding (96.1%) than mothers assigned to breast pumping (72.7%) (p=0.02). Hand expression in the early postpartum period appears to improve eventual breastfeeding rates at 2 months after birth compared with breast pumping, but further research is needed to confirm this. However, in circumstances where either pumping or hand expression would be appropriate for healthy term infants 12â€“36 h old feeding poorly, providers should consider recommending hand expression. 3. ,. A study done by Morton J(2011) comparing hand techniques with electric pumping increases milk production in mothers of preterm infants. A total of 67 mothers of infants less than 31 weeks gestation were enrolled and instructed on production of hand expression of colostrums and hands-on pumping of mature milk. 78%of the mothers completed the study. Mean daily volumes rose to 820ml per day by week 8 and 955ml per day in mothers who had hand expressed more than 5 per day in the first 3 days. Week 2 and or week 8 Mean daily volume related to hand expression, maternal age, gestational age, pumping frequency duration, longest interval between pumping and Hands-On- Pumping . column51: Background: The left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) seems to exert a bilateral control of pain. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, (rTMS) known to modulate brain excitability. Lack of short term habituation (Sensory gating) in migraine might result in part from a pericortical dysfunction Objectives: This study was designed to assess the efficacy of adjunctive intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS) to the left DLPFC, as treatment in migraine patients. To assess the sensory gating in migraine patients and change in sensory gating in migraine patients, after adjunctive iTBS. Method: The study was a randomised double blind, sham controlled experiment. Subjects with migraine were randomized to active (n=20) or sham (n=21) rTMS. The patients received 10 sessions of iTBS over the left DLPFC each comprised of 600 pulses. Patients were rated at base line and at 2 weeks, 4weeks, 6weeks and 12weeks after receiving the treatment from the headache diary and by applying Migraine Disability Assessment Scale (MIDAS). 15 age sex and handedness matched healthy controls selected for comparing sensory gating. 40 channel ERP recording was done on patient groups and normal controls. On patient groups, 1st ERP recording was done before 1st session of rTMS and second ERP recording was done after the 10th session of rTMS. In all healthy controls ERP recording was done once. Results: There was significant decrease in frequency; duration and severity of headache in active group than the sham group over the study period and effect was more pronounced during the initial 2 weeks. The MIDAS score reduced significantly in active group than that of sham group at 12 weeks. There were no significant adverse effects observed. There was significant reduced/weak sensory gating of auditory responses in migraine patients between attacks in comparison to healthy controls. iTBS had no effect in altering the P50 sensory gating in migraine patients . Conclusion: Compared to sham stimulation adjunctive active iTBS over the left DLPFC was safe and effective in reducing the frequency, duration and severity of migraine headache and in reducing migraine disability. Platelet rich fibrin (PRF) is considered as second generation platelet concentrate, consisting of viable platelets, releasing various growth factors. Hence, this study aims to investigate the clinical and radiological (bone fill) effectiveness of autologous PRF and synthetic Hydroxyapatite granules in the treatment of periapical defect bony defects. Aim and Objective: Comparison of the efficacy of PRF and HA bone grafts in periradicular surgery by clinical and radiographic evaluation. Study Design/Methodology: A randomised clinical trial was conducted in patients who were assigned for periradicular surgery. 20 patients were included in this study and were divided into 2 groups. The patients were randomly assigned for the surgery, received synthetic HA graft and PRF obtained from the patient in the respective assigned groups. A clinical and radiographic evaluation was performed postoperatively at the period of 1 month, 3 months and 6 months. column51: Obsessive-compulsive disorder(OCD) is a common and debilitating neuropsychiatric disorder. The proposed research aims to examine the effect of anodal right pre-supplementary motor area(pre-SMA) high definition transcranial direct current stimulation(HD-tDCS) on neurocognitive functions, and respective physiological correlates in patients with OCD who have persistent symptoms despite being on adequate treatment with medications. Task-related physiological alterations is proposed to be examined through comprehensive assessment of neurohemodynamic and electrophysiological changes pertaining to the key neurocognitive functions coupled with the assessment of neurochemical alterations(glutamate and N-acetyl aspartate) in pre-SMA before and after 10 days of HD-tDCS sessions (conducted 2 sessions per day) using a randomised sham controlled design. Following the RCT phase those patients who have only <25% improvement will be offered an open label extension phase for addition 10 days. The translational implication is to evaluate novel treatment options for OCD patients who do not respond to conventional treatment options and to understand the mechanistic basis for the brain stimulation method. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU.
