column51: Physeal bars in children are common following trauma and infection in our country eventually leading to deformities, and shortening. This contributes to the burden of disability and children require multiple corrective surgeries and time consuming lengthening procedures during their growth period. While in smaller (<30%) physeal bars of favorable types the bar excision and replacement with cranioplasts or fat [1,2] acts as a nonunion allowing the surrounding physis to grow, this option is not available for larger defects. In addition this option gives a transient recovery with recurrence of growth arrest and migration of the filler material leading to pathological fractures. Based on the available literature and our own previous work funded by DBT and Indo Danish Grant from DBT we carried out studies in large animals (goat) to prove the concept that autologous culture expanded iliac apophyseal chondrocytes in matrix enhanced monolayer could restore and replace the damaged growth plate with a tissue engineered construct and restore growth capability. This was clinically tested and established safety in a CTRI (CTRI/2012/05/002638) registered and IRB/ethical committee approved pilot study in 5 children where we were able to show restoration of growth and its continuation at a mean 30 months in five out of eight transplanted physis with more than 30% physeal bars using ACT, the three failures occurring in near total loss of physes and a hemiepihyseal loss (T1468, ISSCR, Sweden, June 2015). The sizes of bars selected in this study were larger than those suitable for repair using interposition material thus demonstrating the usefulness of the technique even in difficult unrepairable situations. Based on our results, we propose a human clinical trial for the autologous physeal chondrocytes to assess its efficacy as well as safety. The proposed study will use autologous culture expanded chondrocytes for repair of the physeal defect in twenty children for defect sizes varying from 10 to 60% and excluding hemiphyseal loss. Objectives: 1) To isolate and culture human physeal chondrocytes as monolayer in GMP condition 2) To assess the quality of chondrocytes by assessing the viability, characterization using chondrocyte specific markers (COL 2 and COL 1) and perform release criteria for mycoplasma, endotoxin and microbiology 3) Surgical transplantation of monolayer cultured cells in the physeal defect after excision of the bone bridge 4) Follow up of 15 children with radiographs and pre and post MRI for a minimum of one year and preferably till skeletal maturity Expected outcome: Primary Outcome: Resumption of growth at the physeal arrest site (change in length) Secondary Outcome/s: Integration of the transplant with the existing growth plate verified using radiograph and MRI. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Metastasis to the bone is a frequent complication of visceral cancers, most commonly in patients with advanced breast, prostate, or lung cancer. More than 50% of patients with advanced breast or prostate cancer have identifiable bone metastasis, and 30% to 40% of patients with nonâ€“small-cell lung cancer ultimately develop metastases to bone. Most tumours preferentially metastasize to the axial skeleton, targeting the vertebrae, pelvis, proximal ends of long bones, and skull. Skeletal-related events (SREs) as a result of these metastasis remain a main source of morbidity and shorter life expectancies. Denosumab is a fully human, monoclonal, synthetic, IgG2 antibody that binds to Receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-Î’ ligand (RANKL), with high affinity and specificity, and inhibits formation, function, and survival of activated osteoclasts, bone destruction, and tumour growth. Denosumab is recommended to be administered at a dose of 120 mg as a single subcutaneous (SC) injection once every 4 weeks along with supplemental calcium and vitamin D. This is an assessor-blind, stratified randomized, parallel-arm, multicentre clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of Intas Denosumab with reference product. Patients will be screened for up to 14 days. Eligible patients will be randomized post stratification, to receive either Intas Denosumab 120 mg/1.7 mL or Xgeva in equal ratio. All randomized patients will be part of the study for a period of 24 weeks. Efficacy, pharmacokinetic, immunogenicity, and safety of the drug will be evaluated. column51: 1. Title of the project: Effect of Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) on Coronary Sinus Blood Gas Analysis 2. Type of Study: Prospective and single center 3. Aims & objectives (hypotheses if applicable) : In coronary artery disease patient blood flow of heart muscle is compromised. Post coronary artery bypass grafting blood flow to the heart will increase and that will lead to increase in oxygen supply to the Heart. Hypothetically we assume that as Oxygen delivery to heart will increase post CABG, mixed venous saturation of coronary sinus blood will increase. To know the effect of CABG on oxygen supply demand ratio of heart muscle. To know the benefit of CABG in view of improvement of oxygen supply to the heart 4. Justification for study: Arterial ABG we are taking from peripheral line only. As we assume that arterial blood is same in coronary artery and periphery. But to know the oxygen consumption or oxygen delivery of body we need to take venous blood from Right atrium ( as it is final drainage of venous blood), similarly to know oxygen delivery of heart, we need to take blood from coronary sinus as it is final drainage of heart blood before it mix with Right atrium. 5. Departments involved: Cardiac Anesthesia & Cardiac Surgery 6. Study period: 1 year 7. Sample size : 50 8. Materials and methods: a) Inclusion and exclusion criteria: Inclusion: Â· patient posted for elective off pump CABG only Â· ages 20-70 years Â· Signed informed consent. Exclusion: Â· EF < 40% Â· CABG with other procedure Â· Post PTCA Â· Chronic Kidney Disease Â· Critical LMCA stenosis Â· PAH Â· moderate to severe MR Â· Recent MI Â· Ongoing chest pain Â· History of allergy to any drug Â· Pregnant patient Â· Patient with heart block Â· Baseline pulse rate < 50/min Â· History of epilepsy or seizure Â· Prolongd PT & APTT b) Biological materials required: Blood â€“ 5 ml c) Statistical methods: Paired T test 9. Detailed description of procedure / processes: After getting Ethical committee clearance we will enroll patient for this study. We will select patients undergoing elective off pump CABG. Written and informed consent will be taken from patient. Patients will be induced with routine anesthetic agents. Sternotomy will be done after routine painting and draping. Then surgeon will take 2 ml blood sample in heparinized syringe from coronary sinus. We will take routine ABG sample from arterial line at the same time. Both samples will be send for blood gas analysis. Then surgery will be proceed as routine. After completion of distal and proximal grafting, surgeon will again take 2 ml blood in heparinized syringe from coronary sinus. A sample from arterial will also be taken at the same time. We will send both the sample for arterial blood gas analysis. Further course of patient will be routine. 10. Outcome measures: After completion of study in 50 patients, we will measure and compare PaO2, PCO2 and SaO2 in Pre CABG and Post CABG coronary sinus blood sample. We will also see if there is any major change in arterial blood gas analysis. 11. Potential risks and benefits : Risk- Minor Risk over minimal as blood will be taken from Coronary Sinus , Benefit- Effectiveness and benefit of CABG with immediate result 12. Ethical considerations and methods to address issues : Informed consent will be taken. Indirect identifiers will be used to ensure confidentiality. 13. Budget (give details) and proposed funding source: 10000 14. Review of literature (within 1000 words): The adequacy of tissue oxygenation depends on the rate of oxygen delivered to the tissues (oxygen delivery (DO2) and the rate of oxygen consumed by the tissues (oxygen consumption or oxygen uptake (VO2). Oxygen delivery (DO2) is the volume of oxygen delivered to the systemic vascular bed per minute and is the product of cardiac output (CO) and arterial oxygen concentration (CaO2): DO2 = CO x CaO2. Oxygen uptake is the amount of oxygen that diffuses from capillaries to mitochondria. Tissue oxygenation is adequate when tissues receive sufficient oxygen to meet their metabolic needs. When tissues do not receive sufficient oxygen, cellular injury could potentially occur. Oxygen deprivation may cause tissue damage directly if energy supplied to meet the tissue demands is insufficient1. In addition, Oxygen deprivation may cause tissue damage indirectly during the reperfusion of the tissue 2. Oxygen delivery may be calculated as follows: DO2 = CO x CaO2 x 10. Where CO is the cardiac output and CaO2 is arterial O2 content. Calculation of CaO2 may be performed using the following formula: CaO2 = (Hb x 1.39 x SaO2) + (PaO2 x 0.003). Where Hb represents the hemoglobin level, SaO2 the arterial saturation, PaO2 the arterial tension, and 0.003 is the solubility coefficient of oxygen in human plasma. CvO2 = (Hb x 1.39 x SvO2) + (PvO2 x 0.003). Where SvO2 is the venous saturation and PvO2 the venous tension. The fraction of DO2 that diffuses from capillares into tissues, expressed as the percent of total, is termed O2 extraction ratio (O2ER). The O2 extraction ratio is defined as: O2ER = [(CaO2 - CvO2)/CaO2] = VO2/DO2. In CABG we are increasing coronary blood flow by giving additional blood supply to heart from vessel conduit. So oxygen extraction ratio should either decrease or remain same. We have reviewed literature for the increase in coronary sinus blood flow post CABG and post PTCA3, 4. All literature conclude that there is increase in blood flow to the coronary artery with indirect measurement of increase in blood flow to coronary sinus. But weather that increase in coronary blood flow improve oxygen consumption of heart muscle or not that is not shown. So we are doing this study to prove our hypothesis. 15. References: 1. Jones DP. column51: This is a multicentre, single arm, open label phase IV study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of bevacizumab(KRABEVAÂ® / AbevmyÂ® )intravenous infusion administered as per the prescribing information. The study will consist of a 21-day screening period, study drug treatment cycles every 2 weeks or 3 weeks, lasting for a period of up to 6 months. Approximately 225 patients will be enrolled. The study population will comprise of the patients with solid tumors who have passed screening assessments, have provided written informed consent and considered eligible to receive bevacizumab treatment as per the prescribing information of bevacizumab as per the investigator. Rationale for ART-123 in Sepsis and Coagulopathy i. Coagulopathy is associated with increased mortality in sepsis (Corrigan et al, NEJM 1968). ii. Coagulation and inflammatory pathways are intricately linked and Thrombomodulin appears to play a key role both as a scavenger and modulator of thrombin activity, and its role as an endothelial cell surface protein (Esmon C et al, Nature medicine, 2005) iii. Modulation of coagulation is a likely method to impact the prognosis of patients with sepsis and coagulopathy. iv. The post-hoc analysis of the global phase 2b study suggested that ART-123 was beneficial to sepsis patients with coagulopathy (INR > 1.4), and elevated inflammation (at least one organ dysfunction). column51: AIM of study is to 1. To evaluate healing rate and post obturation pain in single visit root canal treatment using Bioceramic sealer (Bioroot RCS Septodont) as a root canal sealer. 2. To evaluate healing rate and post obturation pain in single visit root canal treatment using Calcium hydroxide based sealer (Sealapex Kerr Sybronendo) as a root canal sealer 3. To evaluate healing rate and post obturation pain in single visit root canal treatment using Resin based sealer (AH plus Dentsply DeTrey) as a root canal sealer. 4. To compare healing rate and post obturation pain in single visit root canal treatment with Bioceramic sealer (Bioroot RCS), Calcium hydroxide based sealer (sealapex) and Resin based sealer (AH plus) as a root canal sealer. Scope: In endodontic practice, the success of root canal therapy mainly depend on achieving a compact fluid tight seal of the apical end of the root canal, so as to prevent the ingress and accumulation of irritants causing biological breakdown of attachment apparatus leading to failure. Root canal sealers along with solid core material play a major role in achieving the fluid tight seal. Several types of root canal sealers are used in endodontic practice with each one having own merits and demerits. Sealers are basically selected based on their sealing ability, adhesive properties, biocompatibility & antimicrobial efficacy. Therefore ,with advent of new techniques and knowledge it becomes imperative that the use of advanced materials be used to increase the success rate of root canal treatment in single visit whenever possible. This study might help us to devise an advanced treatment modality directed at enhancing the success rate of root canal treatment and increasing tooth longevity. Method:1 The case will be allocated into three different groups of 20 in each based on sealer used. Initially access cavity will be made under rubber dam isolation using a high speed air motor with water coolant. After shaping and cleaning of canal using 5.25% sodium hypochlorite, 17% EDTA and 2% chlorhexidine as root canal irrigants, each group will be sonic activated and then the canal will be obturated with gutta-percha cones using sealer: in Group 1 bioroot RCS used as a sealer ,in group 2 sealapex used as a sealer and in group 3 AH plus used as sealer by Cold lateral condensation technique followed by GIC restoration . Teeth will then be reviewed clinically and radiographically at 1months,3 months,6 months and 12 months. column51: The vast majority of children with idiopathic nephrotic syndrome respond well to corticosteroid treatment. However, as many as 70% experience at least one relapse, and 30% develop a more complicated course with frequent relapses (FRNS) with or without steroid dependency (SDNS). Extended steroid exposure in these children often results in long-term complications. The management of patients with SDNS is challenging and expensive. Relapses may lead to serious complications, e.g. related to anasarca, hypertension, life threatening infections (peritonitis, pneumonia, meningitis), thrombosis and malnutrition. Repeated courses or even continuous steroid treatment lead to considerable medication related toxicity and morbidity. The goal of treatment is to reduce the rate of relapses, the cumulative dose of corticosteroids, and the incidence of serious complications. Various prospective studies suggest that Rituximab, a B cell depleting monoclonal antibody, could be a safe and effective alternative to steroid or immunosuppressants to achieve and maintain remission in this population. Single rituximab infusion have been shown to be efficacious for 6 to 12 months and the side effect profile observed to date is very benign but after 6-8 months there was relapse due to regeneration of B-lymphocytes, hence for maintenance of remission MMF has been considered. In spite of good initial response, rituximab responders always remain prone to further relapse with regeneration of B lymphocytes, necessitating either repeat course of rituximab or addition of another steroid-sparing immunosuppressant. Reports suggest efficacy of rituximab may vary depending on disease pathology, clinical course, and simultaneous use of other immunosuppressants. column51: Osteoarthritis (OA) Knee is a common debilitating condition, for which there is no cure. Although OA is not a life-threatening condition, the severity of this disease lies in the continuous pain and functional impairment. It is evident from the literature, that cartilage loss is not only a pathologic process that triggers OA. Subchondral bone is identified as the starting place for pathologic changes, and cartilage is the victim of this process. In OA, the sub-chondral bone undergoes changes which include microcrack, structural defects and progressive replacement of the subchondral marrow with fibro neurovascular mesenchymal tissue. Hence, lesions in this subchondral tissue lead inevitably to the onset of OA, if they are not treated properly. The popular biologic therapy, autologous platelet rich plasma (PRP), prepared from patients own blood, contains a pool of growth factors for cartilage repair. Biological analysis of PRP has also demonstrated an anti-inflammatory effect on the intra-articular environment. The use of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) for the treatment of osteoarthritis (OA) has demonstrated mixed clinical outcomes in randomized controlled trials. As it is yet to establish which of the joint tissues, among synovial membranes, synovial fluid, articular cartilage or sub-chondral bones, is the primary driver of OA Knee, it is not clear whether we should target one or multiple tissues or structures during interventions. We can assume that targeting several joint tissues or structures at a time, can provide a better result. column51: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic progressive inflammatory disease characterized by swelling and pain in multiple joints. The primary lesion of RA is considered to be in synovial membranes. Synovial cell proliferation gradually affects surrounding cartilage and bone, frequently leading to the disruption or deformation of joints. Physical symptoms other than those of joints include subcutaneous nodules or vascular inflammation, skin ulcers, and pulmonary fibrosis. RA is therefore considered not a joint disease but a systemic disease. Immune abnormalities underlie the pathology of RA, and the correction of these abnormalities is currently considered optimal therapy for RA. The outlook for patients with rheumatoid arthritis has improved significantly over the last three decades with the use of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. column28: Neurofeedback is using the brain EEG signals as a feedback to assist, enhance or modify cognitive or sensory-motor functions of the concerned person. It is a type of non-invasive operant-conditioning technique. It consists of the following steps: 1. Data-recording- the EEG of the subject is measured through scalp electrodes in real-time. 2. Data-processing- the EEG is filtered of any artifacts and specific pattern of EEG is located which correlates with the specific cognitive state. 3. Generation of a feedback signal- the processed data is converted into a sensory stimulus which can be understood by the subject (e.g., changing colours, sound intensity or speed of vehicle in a video game, etc.). The subject by modulating his/her cognitive state changes the EEG pattern and thereby the presented stimulus. It is a non-invasive, harmless intervention technique to modify and modulate ones own cognitive and emotional state (e.g., craving for drugs). | EEG would be recorded in the subjects recruited in this arm. column51: INTRODUCTION AND REVIEW OF LITERATURE Acute lymphoblastic leukemia(ALL) accounts for 80 % of leukemia in children less than 15 years of age.1 Among the various types of childhood malignancy incidence of leukemia is very high.2 Asparagine is needed for protein synthesis, DNA, RNA synthesis and cell growth.3 De novo synthesis of asparagine from aspartic acid requires asparagine synthetase. Leukemic cells are devoid of asparagine synthetase and they depend on circulating asparagine for cell growth. L-asparaginase hydrolyzes asparagine, thereby decreasing the asparagine levels and inhibiting protein synthesis of leukemic cells causing leukemic cell death.4 The use of L-asparaginase in combination chemotherapy of acute lymphoblastic leukemia has drastically improved the survival rate in children.5-8 Available formulations of asparaginase are Escherichia coli asparaginase, PEG asparaginase (polyethylene glycol) and Erwinia asparaginase. The area of concerns of native E.coli asparaginase form is the shorter half-life of about 1.28 days, more frequent administration of the drug and the higher frequency of anti-asparaginase antibody formation. The half-life of PEG-asparaginase is about 5-7 days, with lesser dosing frequency and lower anti-asparaginase antibody formation.4, 9 Adverse reactions of L-asparaginase include hypersensitivity reactions, silent inactivation of enzyme asparaginase due to the production of asparaginase antibody, thromboembolic events, hyperglycemia, pancreatitis, hepatic toxicity, encephalopathy, myelosuppression and hypertriglyceridemia.10 Asparaginase efficacy can be assessed by serum asparagine levels and the clearance of blast cells.11-14 Based on HPLC assay detection the level of serum asparagine less than 0.1-0.2 Î¼M is taken as complete depletion of asparagine.11, 15 The innovator PEG-asparaginase is Oncaspar and the Indian biosimilar is Hamsyl. As Hamsyl is a biosimilar, elaborate studies have to be conducted against the E.coli asparaginase to replace the use of native forms with the pegylated form. Moreover, there are no studies comparing the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the native form against pegylated biosimilar from India when given intramuscularly in lower doses. So, the present study has been planned to address the above-mentioned issues. The variability in asparaginase activity with E.coli asparaginase warrants that the therapeutic drug monitoring of asparaginase could be an essential factor in the management of ALL.16 When the population pharmacokinetic profiling of the pegylated form was analyzed, the variability was low.17 Such a population data is not available in the published literature for the biosimilar pegylated form from India. This study will help us in taking a decision regarding the deployment of therapeutic drug monitoring for the pegylated forms when used in the management of ALL. In this study, we hypothesize that the variability in the pharmacokinetic parameters for the pegylated forms will be less than the native forms and the variability of the asparagine levels against the asparaginase activity will be lesser than the native form. Sample size calculations and data analysis: Fourteen participants are required in each group to detect a difference in the mean asparagine levels of 20 ng/ml with the standard deviation of 18 (Alpha error â€“ 5%, Beta error â€“ 20%). Population analysis will be performed by non-linear mixed effect (NLME) modeling. The pharmacokinetic parameters included in the modelling will be clearance, volume of distribution and Cmax. The pharmacodynamic parameters included will be asparagine levels and blast cells status at the end of induction period. The covariates for modeling will be demographic parameters, biochemical parameters and the disease severity. R 3.5 will be used statistical analysis. Study procedure, tools & evaluation: a. Consent from parents and assent from children will be obtained. The study will be conducted after obtaining permission from institutional ethics committee. b. Post-screening a total of 28 patients of either sex will be randomized to receive native E. coli asparaginase, 10000 IU/ mÂ² intramuscularly on day 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, and 30 of induction therapy or PEG-asparaginase 1000 IU/ mÂ² intramuscularly on day 9 and 23 of induction therapy. In case of patients receiving E. coli asparaginase, blood samples will be collected at baseline, 20 minutes, 1hour, 4 hours, 24 hours and at 72 hours post the administration of the drug. One sample will be taken at three days after the last dose of E.coli asparaginase injection in the induction phase. In case of patients receiving PEG asparaginase, blood samples will be collected baseline, 24 hours, 48 hours, 168 hours, 336 hours post administration of the drug. One blood sample will be taken 10 days after the last dose of pegylated asparaginase injection. c. Then measurement of L-asparagine plasma levels and plasma asparaginase activity will be done using High Performance Liquid Chromatography.18 d. Both the groups will be followed up to the end of the induction phase which is usually 35 days from the start of the chemotherapy regimen. Biochemical tests will be done to determine the treatment-emergent adverse events. e. Post induction, remission status of the patients will be assessed by morphological examination of the bone marrow. f. column51: This is a randomized, open-label, controlled, multi-center, global Phase III study to determine the efficacy and safety of combining durvalumab Â± tremelimumab with 6 cycles of standard of care (SoC) chemotherapy (cisplatin + gemcitabine or carboplatin + gemcitabine doublet) followed by durvalumab monotherapy versus SoC alone as first-line chemotherapy in patients with histologically or cytologically documented transitional cell carcinoma (transitional cell and mixed transitional/non-transitional cell histologies) of the urothelium (including renal pelvis, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra), unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic (ie, T4b, any N; or any T, N2-N3; or M1).The study will plan to enrol approximately 1265 patients globally in order to randomize (1:1:1) approximately 885 patients to durvalumab + SoC, durvalumab + tremelimumab + SoC combination therapy, or SoC (cisplatin + gemcitabine or carboplatin + gemcitabine). Therefore, approximately 295 patients will be randomized to each of the treatment arms.The primary aim of this study is to assess the efficacy of durvalumab + SoC combination therapy compared with SoC in terms of OS and PFS in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic UC.Antitumor activity will be assessed according to RECIST 1.1 guidelines. The co-primary analysis of PFS will be based on programmatically derived PFS calculated from the tumor assessments according to RECIST 1.1 by BICR. In addition, PFS by RECIST 1.1 modified for confirmation of progression and Immune-related Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors, version 1.1, using BICR assessments will also be performed for exploratory purposes.Other secondary efficacy endpoints of proportion of patients alive and progression-free at 12 months from randomization (APF12), overall survival at 24 months after randomization (OS24), duration of response (DoR), disease control rate (DCR), and time from randomization to second progression (PFS2) will be examined to further evaluate the antitumor effect and survival benefit of durvalumab + SoC compared with SoC, and durvalumab + tremelimumab + SoC compared with SoC. column51: Gingival recession is a apical migration of gingival margin beyond the cementoenamel junction (CEJ).1 Connective tissue graft (CTG) technique is most commonly used free soft tissue graft and is considered to be the gold standard though it has its own limitation which include a second surgical site and technique sensitive procedure.1It has predictability of 100% in achieving complete root coverage.1 Chorion membrane a foetal membrane is a biomaterial that can be easily obtained, processed and transported. It has gained importance because of its ability to reduce scarring and inï¬‚ammation; enhance wound healing; and serve as a scaffold for cell proliferation and differentiation as a result of its antimicrobial properties.2 The matrix of chorion contains abundant growth factors such as keratinocyte growth factors , basic fibroblast growth factors, transforming growth factor- Î² that promote periodontal regeneration.3 The ability of autograft to self-adhere eliminates the need of suturing.3 Modified vestibular incision supraperiosteal tunnel access technique (modified VISTA) is a minimally invasive technique known to treat multiple gingival recession compared to other techniques4.Till date, there are no clinical studies on modified VISTA for root coverage procedures around natural teeth using chorion membrane. The scope and further applications of the chorion membrane in root coverage needs to be studied. column51: A randomized pilot study to evaluate the efficacy of amniotic membrane as an alternative wound dressing in patients with large posttraumatic raw area at level 1 Trauma Center. This is an open label , pilot study to assess the efficacy of amniotic membrane as a wound dressing. It will be tested in patients with large post traumatic raw area requiring coverage with skin grafts or flaps, which needs an appropriate wound dressing till the wound bed is ready for grafting or flap cover. Patients will be randomized in two groups using sealed envelope method. In group I (control group) patients will be treated with the conventional wound dressing. In the Group II amniotic membrane (AM) dressing will be used. The wound will be observed for healing and any signs of infection. In both the group patients the post traumatic raw area will be assessed by Bates Jensen Wound assessment tool and the photo documentation will be done. The time frame will initial baseline ie one day one then on 7th, 14th and 28th day of the treatment period. During this treatment period assessment of pain will also be done with Visual analog scale. Primary and secondary outcome measures will be noted and analyzed. Placenta will be obtained from the patient undergoing an elective caesarian section and willing for a repeat serological test after 3month.The donor blood serological test will be performed and the placenta will be used only if the serological test will be negative for HIV, Hepatitis B and C and VDRL at baseline. Placenta will be collected in a sterile storage container containing transport media and it will be transported to Stem Cell Facility (DBT Center of Excellence for Stem Cell Research), CTC, AIIMS. At this facility, amniotic membrane will be processed and be stored at â€“80Â° c in deep freezer for further use as per the requirement. For transfer to the patient, the amniotic membrane will be applied on large post traumatic raw in patient admitted in trauma surgery unit, to prepare the wound bed for early grafting or flap cover. column51: Blood transfusion plays an important role in the management of trauma patients. Transfusion of blood components leads to introduction of immune components such as white blood cells, antibodies and cytokines responsible for Immune alterations in the recipients. In severely injured patients a dysregulated immune response due to the trauma itself along with large requirement of blood transfusion over shorter time periods making them more susceptible to the immunomodulatory effects of blood transfusion. Often resulting in complications like increased risk of infections, length of stay, pulmonary morbidity, postinjury MOF (multiple organ failure) and mortality in these group of patient. Leukoreduction of the blood components before transfusion has been advocated to decrease the effect of immunomodulation by eliminating direct actions of the leukocytes as well as the accumulation of leukocyte-derived inflammatory mediators. In this study we will compare the incidence of hospital acquired infections in severely injured trauma patients transfused with leukoreduced (LR) vs non-leukoreduced (NLR) blood components. column51: Gingival recession is a apical migration of gingival margin beyond the cementoenamel junction (CEJ). Connective tissue graft (CTG) technique is most commonly used free soft tissue graft and is considered to be the gold standard though it has its own limitation which include a second surgical site and technique sensitive procedure.1It has predictability of 100% in achieving complete root coverage. Chorion membrane a foetal membrane is a biomaterial that can be easily obtained, processed and transported. It has gained importance because of its ability to reduce scarring and inï¬‚ammation; enhance wound healing; and serve as a scaffold for cell proliferation and differentiation as a result of its antimicrobial properties.The matrix of chorion contains abundant growth factors such as keratinocyte growth factors , basic fibroblast growth factors, transforming growth factor- Î² that promote periodontal regeneration. The ability of autograft to self-adhere eliminates the need of suturing. VISTA is a careful subperiosteal dissection that reduces the tension of the gingival margin during coronal advancement while at the same time maintaining the anatomical integrity of the interdental papillae by avoiding papillary reflection. Treatment of millers class I and II using VISTA technique offers improved esthetic outcomes as well as shows complete root coverage over long follow up periods. Modified vestibular incision supraperiosteal tunnel access technique (modified VISTA) is a minimally invasive technique known to treat multiple gingival recession compared to other techniques.Till date, there are no clinical studies on modified VISTA for root coverage procedures around natural teeth using chorion membrane. The scope and further applications of the chorion membrane in root coverage needs to be studied. Hence, this study is undertaken to evaluate short term treatment effects of root coverage using chorionic membrane in multiple Millerâ€™s Class I and/or II gingival recession with VISTA compared to modified VISTA. column51: Cirrhosis is characterized by progressive deterioration in liver functions. Liver’s synthetic functions are inferred by serum albumin and INR estimation. Lower albumin level is a marker of severe liver disease and probability of worsening ascites, hepatorenal syndrome with increased risk for infections. Of the three recent RCTs on utility of long-term administration of albumin, two showed improvement in survival. The studies had included different patient populations (diuretic refractory ascites, high dose diuretics and patients on liver transplant waiting list) with different albumin infusion protocols and different end-points. These studies were done in advanced cases of cirrhosis. There is limited data on the utility of regular albumin infusions in early hepatic decompensation (albumin levels-<2.8g/dl with ascites) and the effect of maintaining a targeted albumin level on survival or liver related side effects. column28: PREPARATION OF PRF: Using all aseptic precautions, 10-20 ml of venous blood will be withdrawn using a 18 G needle from an appropriate vein in the undraped upper limb. It will be quickly transferred to a plain centrifuge vial within a minute or two and placed in a centrifuge machine kept in the operation theatre. The PRF will be prepared In the Group PRF cases where PRF will be added the following method will be used: â€¢ IC fractures undergoing CRIF: After satisfactory anatomical closed reduction of the fracture, 3 guide wires will be passed under image intensifier in the standard inverted triangle configuration, After using a cannulated drill bit and if required a cannulated tap over the inferior most guide wire, an appropriate sized cannulated cancellous screw will be used to fix and stabilize the fracture site. The other two screw holes will be prepared in tandem by drilling and tapping in a similar way and the cannulated cancellous screws will be advanced under the image intensifier till the tip of the screw reaches the fracture site. The guide wire would now be removed and replaced temporarily by an infant feeding tube of appropriate size inside the cannulate screw. The injectable PRF (i PRF)will be injected through this tube for the liquid PRF to fill up the fracture site, The infant feeding tube will be removed, guide wire replaced and the screw would be advanced for the final compression at the fracture site. â€¢ IC fractures undergoing ORIF: If closed reduction fails, after ORIF with cancellous screws or a PRF clot shall be placed over the fracture site. â€¢ IC fractures undergoing valgus osteotomy : IC fractures treated by valgus osteotomy, the iPRF will be injected through the cannulated barrel of the lag screw used for fixation of the fracture. â€¢ IT fractures undergoing CRIF: Similar to the CRIF and iPRF method of intracapsular fractures, the iPRF will be injected through the cannulated lag screw of DHS or the proximal locking screws of the PFN. â€¢ IT fractures undergoing ORIF: After open reduction and stable fixation by DHS /PFN, iPRF or PRF clot / membrane will be placed over the fracture site. In all Group B cases the wound will be closed in layers without a suction drain. If required tranexamic acid will be injected after withdrawal of sample for PRF. | Group S (Standard Treatment): â€¢ IC Fracture : IC fractures will undergo CRIF or ORIF with CCS or valgus osteotomy with double angle barrel plate. â€¢ IT fracture : IT fractures will undergo CR/OR with stable fixation using proximal femoral nail (PFN) or dynamic hip screw (DHS). column51: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is obtained by centrifuging a fresh sample of uncoagulated venous blood. It is an immune and platelet concentrate collected on a single fibrin membrane which is favorable to healing and immunity.1-2 PRF has a dense fibrin network with leukocytes, cytokines, structural glycoproteins3 and growth factors (transforming growth factor b1, platelet-derived growth factor, vascular endothelial growth factor).4 Compared to platelet rich plasma (PRP) the fibrin matrix of PRF supports the platelets, cytokines and the growth factors, It is considered the determining element responsible for the real therapeutic potential of PRF.Fibrin is a recognized support matrix of bone morphogenic protein and has angiotrophic, hemostatic, and osseous conductive properties. PRF enhances wound healing and regeneration and several studies show rapid and accelerated wound healing.PRF is superior to PRP because it does not need addition of bovine thrombin and calcium chloride and has shown better results in union of fractures.5,6 Experimental studies of PRF in rabbits for fracture union has shown positive results.7 Dental surgeons have been extensively using PRF mixed bone grafts for filling alveolar defects.8 We propose to evaluate the role of PRF in hip fractures.This pilot study, will be useful to find a practical and biological adjunct to aid union of fractures. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: The root coverage procedures are performed for the correction of gingival recession, which is necessary for aesthetic demands, root hypersensitivity, root carious lesions, and cervical abrasions. One of the treatment modalities performed for the gingival recession is free gingival graft(FGG). The keratinized gingiva of the hard palate is one of the common sites for obtaining a free soft tissue graft for periodontal plastic surgical procedure. They yield excellent clinical results and are considered superior. The disadvantages of free gingival grafts are requirement of second surgical site, tissue necrosis, hemorrhage, discomfort and pain. the donor site healing occurs by secondary intention and it takes about 2-4 weeks for the healing to be complete. There is very minimal literature evidence to overcome the disadvantages of the free gingival graft procedure. Choukroun’s platelet rich fibrin is a second generation platelet concentrate that is used in wound healing of skin wounds and recent evidences suggest application of PRF for various modalities in the periodontal therapy. The PRF has stimulatory effect on wound healing due to the presence of various growth factors and also acts as an excellent scaffold for angiogenesis and epithelialisation. This study is time bound (18 Months) randomized controlled clinical trial, patients fulfilling the inclusion and exclusion criteria during the study period will be recruited for the study. column51: Osteoarthritis (OA) is best defined as a chronic and degenerative disorder of multiple etiologies and is characterized by articular cartilage destruction, bony hypertrophy at the margins, sub-chondral sclerosis, and a range of biochemical and morphological alterations of the synovial membrane as well as of the joint capsule. Osteoarthritis occurs when there is disequilibrium between the breakdown and repair of joint tissues and it becomes unbalanced, especially when the mechanical loads applied exceed the limit of tolerance by the joint tissues. Osteoarthritis is the second most common rheumatologic problem and it is the most frequent joint disease with a prevalence rate of 22 to 39% in India. It is more common in women than men, but the prevalence increases dramatically with age. Approximately , 45% women over the age of 65 years presented with symptoms while radiological abnormalities were found in 70% of those over 65 years. OA of the knee is a major cause of locomotor disability, particularly among the female population.Earlier it was postulated that joint overloading and mechanical stress were the main factors leading to osteoarthritis. However with the growing knowledge of biochemical changes, during the past years increased emphasis has been placed on biochemical factors responsible for maintaining the health of articular cartilage and overall joint health. Recent postulates emphasize and put stress upon biochemical factors that are thought to be responsible for overall joint health. At present treatment modalities for Osteoarthritis are limited in their scope of providing only symptomatic relief for a short period of time. No disease modifying therapies are currently available which makes the patients of osteoarthritis resorting to more surgically invasive procedures like joint replacement for finding relief from their symptoms like pain.Platelet rich plasma (PRP) has emerged over the past decade in the treatment of early osteoarthritic knee joints. It probably has the potential to modify the disease progression and help in healing the ailing joint and symptomatic relief which has been shown in many perspective studies.PRP has been shown to be an innovative, novel and promising procedure to stimulate the repair or replace damaged cartilage. It is also a promising solution for tendino-pathies, non union and arthritis(3).Platelet rich plasma (PRP) is defined as a volume of the plasma fraction, of autologous blood and having a platelet concentration above the baseline. It has been suggested that PRP should achieve three to five times increase in platelet concentration over baseline.The work at PGIMER began with the use of PRP for OA knee back in 2009 and were the first to establish the superiority of PRP over placebo (normal saline) in the treatment of OA knee.Various experimental studies on guinea pig model have also been conducted at PGIMER to study the role of PRP as well as the influence of doses for treatment of OA knee.In the past, there have been many prospective studies highlighting the role of Platelet Rich Plasma in Osteoarthritis knee and have established the anti-inflammatory and chondro-protective effects of Platelet Rich Plasma. Anti-inflammatory effect seems to be the most important action of PRP which best explains the symptomatic relief experienced by patients.With the hype, comes the confusion and there are a lot of unanswered question with regard to PRP use. These questions pertain to type of PRP (leukocyte rich vs. leukocyte poor), the number of injections (single vs. multiple), the need of activator and the dose of PRP. One basic difference in the PRP studies in literature is the dose of PRP. There are various studies which have used different doses of PRP like 3ml, 4ml, 6ml, 8ml. At PGI 8ml PRP has been used for knee OA as knee is a big joint and can easily accommodate 8ml which have labelled as â€œSuperdose PRPâ€. column51: Ulcerative colitis is a form of inflammatory bowel disease characterized by chronic relapsing and remitting inflammation of the colon and rectum. There remains a high unmet need for novel treatments that achieve a higher rate of efficacy in resolving disease symptoms, and inducing and maintaining mucosal healing to achieve long-term corticosteroid-free remission. T cells are integral to the pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis, and clinical experience with anti-integrin monoclonal antibodies has established the principle of T cell-targeted therapies in the disease. GSK2831781 causes targeted depletion of Lymphocyte activation gene-3 (LAG3+) T cells, and has shown preliminary evidence of clinical efficacy in plaque psoriasis. It is therefore hypothesized that GSK2831781 will selectively deplete activated mucosal T cells in ulcerative colitis, but with relative sparing of resting T cells. This study will investigate the safety, tolerability, efficacy and dose-response of GSK2831781 in subjects with moderate to severe active ulcerative colitis. The study consists of a 5-week screening window, 10-week Induction Phase, 20-week Extended Treatment Phase, and a 12-week Follow-Up Phase. Non-Responders allocated to open label treatment who subsequently respond to treatment may spend up to 54 weeks in total on study. column51: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a major cause of non-relapse mortality in post hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients. Mortality is high in patients with grade III-IV GVHD. Treatment with immunosuppressants also adds to the morbidity and mortality due to prolonged immunosuppression and infection. The current modality of treatment available for GVHD include steroids and other second-line immunosuppressants. column51: For this study patients with negative symptoms of schizophrenia will be included. Duration of study would be 1.5 years, with 1 year for enrollment, intervention, assessment and data collection, and final half-year for data analysis and thesis writing. This would be a prospective double blind (Participant and Assessor) follow-up study. Consultants and Senior Residents in the Psychiatry OPD or IPD, AIIMS, New Delhi shall be requested to refer all the patients with schizophrenia. Patients with negative symptoms of schizophrenia presenting to department of psychiatry OPD or IPD at AIIMS will be screened by the thesis candidate and those who meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria will be enrolled into the study after taking written informed consent by a purposive method for participation in the study. Investigator and participant will be blind to group allocation. After enrolling the participant into the study, alphanumeric coding will be used to label the participant by the investigator (for blinding the investigator to group allotment) and will be referred to TMS facility. The participants with the alphanumeric codes will be randomized into two groups as Group 1 and Group 2 using random block design by the guide. The guide will provide sealed envelopes regarding group allocation for each participant to the TMS technician prior to the recruitment initiation. Participants in Group 1 will receive active iTBS to left DLPFC and participants in Group 2 will receive Sham iTBS. TMS technician will include the participant in one of the 2 groups of intervention based on a pre-defined chart (X/Y) available with the technician prepared by the guide mentioning group allocation. Participants would keep receiving the medications which they received earlier for stabilization and a record of it would be made. All the baseline assessments {Sociodemographic and Clinical data (Semi-structured datasheet), SAPS, SANS, CGI, CDSS, TMT, MoCA, ESRS, rSEC and fNIRS) will be conducted within 1 week prior to the first iTBS session. The patients will continue receiving the medications in the same pattern and dosage as previously prescribed without any change during the course of iTBS intervention. All participants will receive 15 sessions of sham or active iTBS over left DLPFC depending on their allocated groups for 15 sessions over a period of 3 weeks (Monday to Friday). The final study sample will comprise of total 30 participants initiating intervention and completing at least 5 sessions. All baseline assessments will be repeated within 24 hours at end of 5th session and last session. Any subject leaving the study prior to receiving complete intervention sessions, will be assessed on the leaving day if possible. column51: Currently, no effective treatments are available for the COVID-19 pandemic, which is related to more than 70,000 deaths all over the world. Scientists and Researchers are working on many aspects of treatment options for the development of vaccination and medication to combat this life-threatening problem. Convalescent plasma from recovered COVID-19 patients contains antibodies against COVID-19 which may be beneficial to severely sick COVID019 infected patients. We have planned a randomized controlled trial to assess the efficacy of this therapy in COVID-19 infected sick patients. We will collect up to 500 ml Convalescent Plasma from the COVID-19 infected recovered patient after 14 days of clinical and radiological recovery with two consecutive COVID-19 negative tests by PCR. We will further test the sample from the collected plasma for COVID-19 specific antibodies and their titer. This plasma will be frozen and sent to the treating center (MAMC). 200-600 ml of convalescent plasma will be transfused to patients who fit the eligibility criteria and are randomized to the convalescent plasma group. This will be done in severely sick patients. Data will be collected for the benefit and adverse events related to convalescent plasma transfusion. For Donors: Microtiter plates will be coated overnight at 4Â°C with 4 Î¼g/mL recombinant SARS-CoV-2 RBD (receptor binding domain) proteins (50 Î¼L per well). The plates will be washed 3 times with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) containing 0.1% vol/vol Tween-20(PBST) and blocked with blocking solution (PBS containing 2% wt/vol nonfat dry milk) for 2 hours at 37 Â°C. The plates will be then washed with PBST. The serum samples will be diluted to 200-fold into PBS as initial concentration, and serial 3-fold dilutions of serum will be added to the wells and incubated at 37 Â°C for 60 minutes. After 3 washes, 100 Î¼L of horseradish peroxidase-conjugated goat anti-human IgG (for IgG antibody titer detection)and IgM (for IgM antibody titer detection) antibodies solution will be added to each plate, respectively, and incubated at 37 Â°C for 60 minutes. After 5 washes, 100 Î¼L of tetramethylbenzidine substrate will be added at room temperature in the dark. After 15 minutes, the reaction will be stopped with a2MH2SO4 solution (sulfuric acid). The absorbance will be measured at 450nm. All samples will be run in triplicate. The IgG titers will be determined by endpoint dilution. Serum Neutralization Assay Vero cells (104) will be seeded 24 hours before the infection in a 96-well plate. On the day of infection, the cells will be washed twice. Serum samples from patients will be incubated at 56 Â°C for 30 minutes and then diluted 2-fold in cell culture medium (modified eagle medium). Aliquots (40 Î¼L) of diluted serum samples (from2-fold to 2056-fold) will be added to 50 Î¼L of cell culture medium containing 50 times the tissue culture infective dose (TCID50) of the virus strain on a 96-well plate and incubated at 37 Â°C for 2 hours in CO2 5% vol/vol. Virus antibody mix will be added to cells in 96-well plates and plates will be incubated at 37 Â°C with a microscopic examination for cytopathic effect after 5-day incubation. The highest dilution of serum that showed inhibition activity of SARS-CoV-2 will be recorded as the neutralizing antibody titer. Assays will be performed in triplicate with negative control samples from healthy volunteers. For recipients: The serum of each recipient will be obtained and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and neutralizing antibody titers will be tested one day prior to the convalescent plasma transfusion. Changes of Receptor Binding Domain-Specific IgG titre and neutralizing antibody titers before and after convalescent plasma transfusion in patients will be obtained on day 0, day 1, day 3 and day 7. if possible. Although not completely understood, multiple pathophysiological mechanisms have been hypothesized for the cause of mortality in COVID-19. Currently, there are no approved treatments for COVID-19. In a small case series, five critically ill COVID-19 patients with ARDS were treated with convalescent plasma containing neutralizing antibodies. The RES system evaluated five variables: the level of the gingival margin, marginal tissue contour, soft tissue texture, Mucogingival junction alignment and gingival color. As the complete root coverage (CRC) was the main treatment goal whereas other variables were secondary endpoints, 60% of the RES value was attributed to the level of gingival margin (primary variable), and 40% was attributed to the other four variables (secondary variables). Gingival margin level (GM): score 0 was given when the gingival margin was apical or almost equal to the baseline recession level which indicates failure of root coverage. Score 3 was given for the partial root coverage and Score 3 was given for complete root coverage. Gingival color: Score 0 was given when gingival color of tissue contrasts the gingival color of adjacent tissue and Score 1 was given when the gingival color matches with the adjacent soft tissue. Marginal Tissue Contour (MTC): Score 0 was given when irregular gingival margin which does not follow CEJ was seen and Score 1 was given when proper marginal contour/scalloped gingival margin following CEJ was seen. Soft tissue texture (STT): Score 0 was given due to the presence of scar formation and/or keloid-like appearance and Score 1 was given in the absence of scar or keloid formation 4) Muco-gingival junction (MGJ): Score 0 was given when mucogingival junction (MGJ) not aligned with MGJ on adjacent teeth and Score 1 was given when MGJ aligned with MGJ on adjacent teeth; A total esthetic score was 10 for the complete root coverage which was esthetically pleasing. column51: Cancer, one of the most deadly challenges spreading drastically in 21st century, has now officially become the most dangerous killer in the world according to the World Health Organization. The fact of cancer disease is related to adversary of modernization and advanced pattern of irregular and stressed life dominated by altered culture, environment and dietetic life style. Scientists are making their best efforts to fight this disease, however the sure-shot cure is still awaited. The complementary and alternative medicine is another hope along with modern medical science; therefore our scientists are keener to researches on complementary and alternative medicine for the management of cancer. Carcinoma of the lung or lung cancer is considered as one of the most common types of cancer in present scenario due to enhancement of certain aetiologies. In case of lung cancer, the symptoms are not clearly visible at an early stage. Most lung cancers start in the lining of the bronchi, frequently in the periphery of the lungs and after that precancerous changes developed in the lungs. Initially these changes do not form a mass or tumour, or cannot be seen or x-ray, and do not cause any symptoms. Ayurvedic Concept of Lung Cancer - Ayurveda, the oldest Indian indigenous medicine system of plant drugs is known from very early times for preventing or suppressing various tumours using these natural drugs. The word Arbuda is used in Ayurveda to define cancer and it is one of the most Asadhya Vyadhi (Incurable disease). Further, In Ayurvedic concept, according to â€˜Charakaâ€™ and â€˜Sushruta Samhitasâ€™ cancer is described as inflammatory or non-inflammatory swelling and mentioned either as â€˜Granthiâ€™ (minor neoplasm) or â€˜Arbudaâ€˜ (major neoplasm). The principles of Vata, Pitta and Kapha are three basics of Ayurveda and very important for normal body function . In the pathogenesis of Arbuda (Cancer) the involvement of Mamsa Dhatu and Rakta Dhatu is occurred due to vitiation of Tridosha i.e. Vata, Pitta and Kapha. Arbudas are gradually increasing mass of big size, globular in shape, fixed with deeper structure, usually do not suppurate, giving occasional pain. In malignant tumours all tridosha i.e. Vata, Pitta and Kapha get out of control and lose mutual coordination that causes tissue damage, resulting critical condition. Tridoshas cause excessive metabolic crisis resulting in proliferation. column51: PROJECT OVERVIEW: BACKGROUND Labour involves a series of changes in the female genital organs associated with painful uterine contractions with effacement & dilation of the cervix. Even after decades of clinical research work, the complex process of labour could not be understood completely as it varies widely from woman to woman. Various theories were put forward to divide the labour process into stages, phases with time limit allotted to each one of them. In 2014, WHO defined active phase initiating at 4 cm of cervical os dilatation and considering the rate of dilatation of <1cm/hour to be abnormal. However, due to the increased need for obstetrical intervention, this remained a matter of conflict. Recently in 2018, WHO modified the guidelines and redefined the active phase to be from 5cm of cervical dilatation and considering the rate of dilatation <1cm/hour to be normal. AIM OF THE STUDY Minimal intervention in the process of labour continuing at its natural pace on its own with watchful expectancy without adversely compromising the feto-maternal outcome. METHODOLOGY In this randomized control trial, 136 non-high-risk nulliparous women at term with spontaneous onset of labour pains will be randomly allocated in two groups. In group 1, the active phase will be from 4cm of cervical dilatation, considering <1cm/hour rate of dilation as abnormal, intervening when indicated as per WHO 2014 labour protocol. In group 2 the active phase will be from 5cm of cervical dilatation, considering <1cm/hour rate of cervical dilatation as normal (WHO 2018 guidelines) and the whole idea for redefining the existing labour protocol will be carefully observed, compared and analysed. column51: Platelet Rich Plasma is a newer treatment modality with abundant Growth factors, bacteriostatic nature, anti-apoptotic and anti-collagenase property. It is seen to be very effective in treating dry eye not amenable to treatment by other means. It can be autologous or heterologous. Autologous PRP has added benefits of preventing occurrence of allergy, or immunological reactions which could occur in cases of heterologous donation. column51: Shoulder pain is the 3rd leading cause of musculoskeletal pain after backpain and neck pain. Peri arthritis (PA), adhesive capsulitis, Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy (RCT), Acromioclavicular joint arthritis, Glenohumeral Osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthritis are some of the common causes of shoulder pain. Periarthritis shoulder/Frozen shoulder is a common condition resulting in insidious onset pain and global restriction of motion at the shoulder joint. Peak incidence between 46 and 64 years of age, with females more often affected.There is inflammation, thickening and contracture of the joint capsule as well as soft tissue fibrosis and inflammation of the rotator interval, capsule and ligaments. Painful stiffness of the shoulder can adversely affect activities of daily living and consequently impair quality of life.The typical natural history is of gradual resolution of symptoms over 1 to 3 year period and between 20% to 50% of patients may go on to develop long-lasting symptoms. A plethora of treatment options have been recommended which include benign neglect, oral corticosteroids, intra articular injection of corticosteroids, hyalouronic acid and platelet rich plasma(PRP), physical therapy exercises, deep heat modalities, manipulation under anaesthesia, hydro dilation, arthroscopic release. column28: At IIT-Bombay, a novel and indigenous HCAR19 cell product has been designed and developed. The gene therapy product (GTP) has been tested for the ex vivo and in vivo functionality and the results are quite promising. Autologous T-cells will be transduced using a lentiviral vector that will contain a gene coding for a single chain variable fragment (scFv) directed against the surface CD19 antigen. The cells will also express an intracellular signalling domain made of 4-1BB and TCRÎ¶ signalling modules. Clinical grade viral vector used for this process will be manufactured at IIT-Bombay. The humanized scFv is designed from FMC63 scFv (murine anti-human CD19 antibody). The signalling domains will be from the native human sequence. Patients will receive the CAR-T cell product as a split-regimen at 10%, 30% and 60% dose on Days 0, 1 and 2 respectively. The minimum dose to be administered is 1x10 raise to power 7 CAR-T cells to a maximum of 5x10 raise to power 9 CAR- T cells. The product will be infused in a single room at Tata Memorial centre, using precautions for immunocompromised patients. The product will be infused at 10-20 ml/min via an 18-G latex free Y- type blood set with a 3-way stopcock. | Not Applicable

column51: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) accounts for 30% of all the cases of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL). Two-thirds of patients respond to frontline chemoimmunotherapy. Only 5 per cent of relapsed/refractory DLBCL responds to salvage chemotherapy and could undergo stem cell transplant. There is a large unmet need to be addressed in the relapsed/refractory setting. The CAR-T cell therapy directed against CD19 shown significant clinical benefit. Two CAR-T cell therapy products are granted FDA approval, namely Axicabtagene ciloleucel (Yescarta) and Tisagenlecleucel (Kymriah). The cost of therapy is exorbitant. Therefore, we need to develop an indigenous product with less production costs and make it accessible to our patients. Our hypothesis is that HCAR19 cell product is safe with manageable toxicities. The primary objective of the study is to assess the safety and tolerability of a clinical-grade HCAR19 cells product in relapsed/refractory DLBCL subjects by recording the frequency and severity of adverse events reporting, including but not limited to, estimating the frequency of cytokine release syndrome ( CRS) and Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS). column51: Maintaining the integrity of the dental arch in the primary and mixed dentition is important for establishing proper occlusion and function in the permanent dentition. The objective behind pulp therapy is to maintain the vitality of the pulp of a tooth affected by caries or traumatic injury and one such widely used pulp therapy method is pulpotomy. Despite the recent advances in synthetically based biomaterials, researchers still reported mild to moderate cytotoxicity on pulp. Hence, it is essential to propose new biologically based therapeutics to preserve pulp vitality, form biological tissue, and neutralizing used side effects of previously used synthetically based biomaterials. Hydroxyapatite is a natural substance with the chemical formula Ca10 (PO4)6 (OH) 4. It has extensive applications in medicine and dentistry due to its favorable properties similar to the mineral phase of the human hard tissues, biocompatibility and low solubility in humid environments. Eggshell is considered a rich source of calcium carbonates and oxides that qualify them as an excellent source of hydroxyapatite. It provides a cost-effective, renewable as well as a sustainable source of biological hydroxyapatite. Recently, biologically based novel materials have been developed from the placenta or other gestational tissues like the umbilical cord, which are highly rich in stem cell reservoirs. Amniotic Membrane (AM) is a fetal membranous sac forming the innermost layer of the placenta. The matrix of the Amniotic membrane contains plenteous growth factors (GFs) including basic-Fibroblast Growth Factor (b-FGF), Nidogen Growth Factor (NGF), Keratinocyte Growth Factor (KGF), Epidermal Derived Growth Factor (EDGF), and Transforming Growth Factor -beta (TGF-Î²) which promote tissue regeneration. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. The ultimate goal of periodontal therapy is the regeneration of periodontal tissues that have been destroyed due to periodontal disease. Periodontal regeneration is the reconstruction of the lost tissues as evidenced histologically in the formation of new cementum, new alveolar bone, and functionally oriented periodontal ligament.2 Loss of alveolar bone support is one of the characteristic signs of destructive periodontal disease and is generally considered to represent the anatomical sequelae to the apical spread of periodontitis. Treatment of bony defects is intended to meet two objectives. Elimination of microbial plaque from exposed surfaces of the root and establishing the anatomy of effected surfaces that facilitates proper self-performed plaque control. column51: SUMMARY Percutaneous computed tomography (CT)-guided lung biopsy is an effective, highly accurate and safe method of obtaining tissue for the diagnosis of pulmonary lesions. Pneumothorax is the most common complication of CT guided percutaneous lung biopsy. Many methods and techniques, such as cessation of respiration during the puncture; avoiding transgression of fissures; puncture in a lateral decubitus position; and sealing the biopsy tract during needle retraction with products such as fibrin glue, gelfoam, hydrogel, 0.9% NaCl and intraparenchymal pulmonary blood patch have been advocated to reduce the frequency of pneumothorax but have met with variable success. Plugging the biopsy track with autologous blood clot seal (ABCS) appears to significantly reduce the occurrence of pneumothorax, particularly large pneumothoraxes, thereby reducing the need for treatment and hospitalization. Aims and Objectives To assess the role of autologous blood clot seal (ABCS) in reducing the frequency of pneumothorax after CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy and to determine whether ABCS reduces the need for chest tube placement for pneumothorax complicating CT-guided lung biopsy. Why this Study? The relatively high frequency of pneumothorax complicating CT-guided Lung Biopsy scan can convert an outpatient procedure to one requiring hospitalization. Because many patients referred for biopsy lack pulmonary reserve they are unable to tolerate even minimal pneumothorax. ABCS appears to reduce the frequency of post-biopsy pneumothorax thereby reducing the need for treatment, hospitalization and attendant cost. Methodology Study Design: Prospective Randomised Controlled Trial. The patients will be randomly assigned to undergo biopsy either with or without the use of an Autologous Blood Clot Seal (ABCS). Sample Size: Literature was reviewed for expected rate of pneumothorax in CT- guided lung biopsy without the use of ABCS which was found out to be 36% and rate of pneumothorax with the use of ABCS which was found out to be 10% [18]. Sample size was calculated from â€œPower calculator for binary outcome superiority trial by Sealed Envelope Ltd.â€ [22] which calculated that 100 patients are required to have a 90% chance of detecting, as significant at the 5% level, a decrease in the primary outcome measure from 36% in the control group (rate of pneumothorax without the use of ABCS) to 10% in the experimental group (rate of pneumothorax with the use of ABCS). Inclusion Criteria: All the patients referred to the Department of Radiodiagnosis and Imaging, Soura, Srinagar for CT-guided lung biopsy. Exclusion Criteria: ï¬ patients with age <12years, ï¬ pregnant women, ï¬ uncooperative patients, ï¬ patients with pulmonary hypertension, ï¬ highly vascular lesions, ï¬ severe anemia, ï¬ patients with uncorrected coagulopathy, ï¬ hydatid Cyst, ï¬ contralateral pneumonectomy, ï¬ And hemodynamically unstable patients Procedure: The ABCS will be prepared beforehand by removing 4.0-8.0 mL of blood from an antecubital vein and allowing the blood to clot in the syringe. In group A patients, 0.5-3.0 ml clot and 0.5-1.5 mL of supernatant will be injected at the level of biopsied nodule, filling the entire track to the visceral pleura while the coaxial sheath is being withdrawn after completion of biopsy. The supernatant will be primarily deployed at the level of biopsied nodule, the solid clot elements in the peripheral track and at the point of exit from visceral pleura. In Group B patients, the coaxial sheath will be withdrawn in one swift motion without injection of ABCS. In the follow-up assessments after the procedure, CT images of the area will be obtained while the patient is still on the table to look for presence of pneumothorax. A posteroanterior radiograph of chest will be obtained at 0 hour i.e. immediately after biopsy and the patient will then remain in a short stay unit for 4 hours in the recumbent position or with sampled side dependent. column51: The medial collateral ligament (MCL) is the most frequently injured ligament in the knee. It may result in a significant loss of time to sports and participation. Early return to sports is the goal of both amateur and professional athletes. Partial MCL injuries can be successfully treated conservatively with an appropriate functional rehabilitation program. Chronic valgus instability from failed healing of MCL tears can result in degenerative arthritis and is therefore treated operatively with MCL reconstruction. Failure of non-surgical treatment can result in debilitating, persistent medial instability, secondary dysfunction of the anterior cruciate ligament, weakness, and osteoarthritis. An alternative to conservative and surgical treatment is a biological stimulus of ligament healing to accelerate the rehabilitation process and allow a faster return to sports and avoid the complications of surgical interventions. Despite being the most commonly injured ligament in sports, there are very less studies to explore other effective treatment options. At present, there is a dearth of literature regarding ultrasound-guided Platelet Rich Plasma injection for the treatment of MCL injuries. A prospective, randomized, controlled study was done in the Department of Sports Medicine, Regional Institute of Medical Sciences, Imphal with the aim to compare the effectiveness of ultrasound-guided platelet-rich plasma injection in comparison with pulsed ultrasound therapy on improving pain and function in athletes with medial collateral ligament injury of the knee. A sample size of 32 patients who were willing to participate in the study was taken from patients with partial MCL tears attending Sports Medicine OPD, RIMS. Sixteen patients underwent ultrasound-guided Platelet Rich Plasma injection (study group) while another sixteen underwent pulsed ultrasound therapy (control group). Pain outcome was measured using the VAS score and functional outcome was assessed by using the Lysholm score at two, six and twelve weeks after the intervention. The collected data was analysed using SPSS 21 version. For descriptive statistics, mean and standard deviation were used. Characteristics of the study participants for the continuous and categorical variables were analysed by independent t-test, Chi-square test and repeated measure ANOVA was used for within the group comparison whereas paired t-test was used for between the group comparison and p-value <0.05 was taken as significant. On comparing the VAS mean score of the study with the control group, a maximum improvement from baseline was found in both groups at 12 weeks (8.73Â±.54 to 2.81Â±.69 vs 8.70Â±.56 to 3.32Â±.47). However, the effect of platelet-rich plasma injection surpassed pulsed ultrasound therapy in terms of pain relief (2.81Â±.69 vs 3.32Â±.47) at the end of 12 weeks. The Lysholm score also had significant improvement in both groups separately (p<0.05). The mean Lysholm score improved from 33.44Â±5.17 at baseline to 88.38Â±2.06 at 12 weeks of follow-up in the study group and from 32.31Â±5.14 to 81.50Â±3.07 in the control group. Improvement was more in the study group in comparison to the control group. It can thus be concluded that both interventions were effective in relieving pain and function during all follow-ups. However, at short-term follow-up, the improvement in pain and function in the PRP group was more than that in pulsed ultrasound therapy. It contains several growth factors like VEGF,FGF,EGF,PDGF,TGF and other cytokines that stimulate proliferation and growth. Activated platelets release granules by exocytosis which contain more than sixty different biologically active substances that are involved in process of tissue regeneration, angiogenesis and epithelization. column51: The rationale for the study: Depression is a leading cause of global disability and about one-third of the individuals with depression who receive treatment fail to respond adequately. Treatment guidelines recommend in-depth clinical research to arrive at evidence-based treatment options for such individuals and non-invasive brain stimulation or neuromodulatory therapies are one such treatment avenue. Among the available newer neuromodulatory therapies, intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS), a form of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) has been shown to be equally effective to conventional high-frequency TMS in the treatment of resistant depression. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) on the other hand, is effective in treating depression patients but is not as effective as medications. Conventional neuromodulation therapy like electroconvulsive therapy is however considered a gold-standard treatment option for resistant depression. TMS and tDCS show variable treatment responses with some patients improving and others not improving. Methods to enhance treatment response are therefore being actively investigated, especially in resistant individuals. In a first-of-its-kind study, we plan to specifically examine the incremental clinical efficacy of cathodal transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (c-tDCS) primed intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS) delivered to the left Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex (DLPFC) in Patients with Treatment-Resistant Depression. As a second part extension, non-responders to the first part-1 treatment will be given open-label electroconvulsive therapy. In addition, we also aim to use neurobiological investigations to understand the mechanisms of such neuromodulatory therapies and use these biomarkers to predict treatment response Aims and hypothesis: Primary To examine the incremental clinical efficacy of cathodal transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (c-tDCS) primed intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS) delivered to the left Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex (DLPFC) in Patients with Treatment-Resistant Depression Hypothesis: True c-tDCS primed iTBS will demonstrate a greater clinical efficacy (change in HAMD scores) compared to sham c-tDCS primed iTBS Secondary To compare the neurobiological profile of patients with Treatment-Resistant Depression with matched healthy controls using multi-modal data (brain imaging, EEG, TMS-tDCS perturbation study metrics, HRV and neuroplastic gene polymorphisms) To examine the clinical utility of the proposed sequential treatment algorithm for treatment-resistant depression. To evaluate the predictive utility of multi-modal data (brain imaging, EEG, TMS-tDCS perturbation study metrics, HRV, and neuroplastic gene polymorphisms) in identifying clinical response to the proposed sequential treatment algorithm for treatment-resistant depression To examine the differential effect of True c-tDCS primed iTBS versus Sham c-tDCS primed iTBS and ECT on the neurobiological profile of Patients with Treatment-Resistant Depression using multi-modal data (brain imaging, EEG, TMS-tDCS perturbation study metrics, HRV) and potential interactions with neuroplasticity gene polymorphisms Study Procedure Participants meeting the selection criteria will be enrolled in a sequential neuromodulation treatment study. All treatments will be added to ongoing pharmacotherapy. In part-1 (randomized controlled trial), participants will be randomized to receive iTBS (sham tDCS-primed or true c-tDCS primed) for 20 days. Participants with an improvement in HAMD-17 score of more than 30% from baseline, but those who do not achieve remission (HAMD-17 score <8), will receive two more weeks of treatment. The primary outcome at the end of 4 or 6 weeks of treatment would be treatment response, defined as a HAMD-17 score reduction of â‰¥50% from baseline and a post-treatment HAMD-17 score of <13. In part-2, non-responders will be offered ECT (open-label); treatment response will be assessed at the end of the ECT treatment.
