column51: The rationale for the study: Clozapine-resistant schizophrenia is a major challenge in the practice of psychiatry. There are almost no evidence-based treatment modalities for this condition. Most people with this condition, the majority of whom are very young, lead their lives with substantial subjective distress and disability. ECT is commonly prescribed in this condition. Unlike in major depressive disorder, the quality of evidence to support the efficacy of ECT in schizophrenia is limited. Part-1: Consenting participants will be randomized (using standard allocation concealment techniques) to true/sham ECT administered thrice-weekly for 9 sessions. Fitness for ECT will be ascertained as per standard guidelines. Pharmacotherapy will remain stable during the ECT course. An investigator blind to group assignment will assess the change over time using the Scale to Assess Positive Symptoms (SAPS). Participants with a <40% change in SAPS scores will be considered non-responders. Part-2: Non-responders due to lack of response from sham treatment will be given the option to receive true ECT, at the same frequency, unless a decision is taken to reduce the frequency of sessions to two per week because of cognitive adverse effects. ECT course would be terminated if there is no change in the clinical status from the previous session on three consecutive sessions as measured by CGI-21 after the 9th session. Irrespective of the number of ECTs received, ECT would be terminated in any of the following situations: (1) Complete remission of symptoms; (2) significant cognitive impairment (as decided clinically) despite reducing the frequency to twice weekly; (3) medical conditions precluding continuation of ECT; (4) on request from the patient. The patients would be free to withdraw from the study at any point in time â€“ the reason for withdrawal would be documented; (5)if patients develop suicidality (though this may happen very rarely) amounting to HAM-D suicide item > 2, then they would be terminated from the study and their treatment would be discussed with the treating team. If patients in the sham arm withdraw due to lack of response, then they would be offered true ECT from that time onward. If they accept it, then they would receive true ECT in an open-label fashion. Aims and hypotheses: Primary To compare the efficacy of true-vs-sham ECT in patients with clozapine-resistant schizophrenia Hypothesis: True-ECT will demonstrate a greater clinical response than sham-ECT To evaluate the predictors of response to ECT in patients with clozapine-resistant schizophrenia Hypothesis: A differential pre-treatment resting brain functional connectivity signal will identify responders to ECT Secondary To compare the neurobiological profile of clozapine-resistant schizophrenia patients with matched healthy controls using multi-modal data (brain imaging, EEG, TMS-tDCS perturbation study metrics, HRV and neuroplastic gene polymorphisms). column51: The rationale for the study: Schizophrenia is a complex neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by delusions, hallucinations, disorganized behavior, and progressive cognitive deficits. This disorder is ranked among the top ten disabling medical disorders by the World Health Organization. Despite the best of the available treatments, about 25 â€“ 35% of patients with schizophrenia show partial or no clinical improvement and they persist to have symptoms that contribute to a critical component of the disability burden. In addition, most of the existing antipsychotic medications are associated with intolerable side effects as well. Contextually, alterative paradigms that involve neuromodulatory techniques have been gaining increasing significance in treating schizophrenia patients. Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation [tDCS] has been reported to be useful in treating hallucinations resistant to antipsychotic treatment in schizophrenia patients. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a non-invasive neuromodulatory technique that delivers low intensity, direct current to cortical areas through the surface application of electrodes on the scalp facilitating or inhibiting spontaneous neuronal activity. Continuous theta-burst stimulation is a safe and well-tolerated treatment option in auditory hallucinations when applied unilaterally, as well as, bilaterally. At present, there is no research study that informs whether a schizophrenia patient may differentially respond to one of these two treatments; such information can be very vital in expediting appropriate neuromodulation treatment choice. This research project addresses this compelling research question. Aims and hypothesis: Primary The primary aim of this study is to identify resting brain functional connectivity markers of response to continuous Theta Burst Stimulation (cTBS) and cathodal transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (c-tDCS) in schizophrenia patients with persistent auditory hallucinations. We hypothesize that a differential pre-treatment resting brain functional connectivity signal will identify responders to cTBS and c-tDCS Secondary To compare the neurobiological profile of schizophrenia patients with persistent auditory hallucinations with matched healthy controls using multi-modal data (brain imaging, Electroencephalography (EEG), TMS-tDCS perturbation study metrics, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), and neuroplastic gene polymorphisms) To examine the differential effect of cTBS versus c-tDCS on the neurobiological profile of schizophrenia patients with persistent auditory hallucinations using multi-modal data (brain imaging, EEG, TMS-tDCS perturbation study metrics, HRV) and potential interactions with neuroplasticity gene polymorphisms To evaluate the predictive utility of multi-modal data (brain imaging, EEG, TMS-tDCS perturbation study metrics, HRV, and neuroplastic gene polymorphisms) in identifying clinical response to cTBS or c-tDCS in schizophrenia patients with persistent auditory hallucinations Study Design Participants meeting selection criteria will be enrolled in a sequential neuromodulation treatment study. All treatments will be added to ongoing pharmacotherapy. In part-1 (randomized controlled trial), participants will be randomized to receive (a) true cTBS (with sham tDCS) and (b) true c-tDCS (with sham cTBS) to the left TPJ for 15 days. Participants will be blind to the true-sham status of their treatment. An investigator blind to group assignment will assess the change over time in the severity of auditory hallucinations using the Auditory Hallucination Rating Scale (AHRS). Participants with a <30% change in AHRS scores will be considered to be non-responders. In part-2, non-responders to either of the treatments will receive a crossover of the alternative treatment (blinded to the participant and the raters); initiated after a 2-4-week washout period. Treatment response will be reassessed at the end of the cross-over treatment. column51: Patients with cirrhosis were long thought to be auto-anticoagulated and at risk of bleeding primarily due to the deranged prothrombin time (PT) / International Normalised Ratio (INR) and frequent episodes of both variceal and non-variceal bleeds.1 However, conventional coagulation tests like PT/INR and platelet count do not reflect in-vivo hemostasis. Patients with cirrhosis are rather at increased venous thromboembolism-both portal venous thrombosis (PVT) and deep venous thrombosis (DVT). Patients with cirrhosis have a delicate but precariously balanced state between procoagulants and anticoagulants. Thrombocytopenia due to hypersplenism and decreased thrombopoietin is balanced by an increase in von Willebrand factor (vWF) levels and low metalloprotease levels which cleaves vWF (ADAMTS13). Similarly, low levels of coagulation factors which are produced by liver, such as clotting factors I, II, V, VII, X, IX are balanced by increased levels of endothelium produced factor VIII and low levels of anticoagulant protein C, protein S and anti-thrombin III.2 This balance can be easily tipped by renal failure due to the inhibitory effect of guanidinosuccinic acid on platelets and infections due to endogenous heparinoids on the coagulation cascade.3,4 The balanced in vivo hemostasis has been demonstrated by Tripodi, who reported that cirrhosis patients have normal thrombin generation by thrombin generation assays after addition of thrombomodulin.5 Therefore, conventional tests of coagulation may not represent the true state of balance (between pro- and anti-coagulants) which exists in vivo. We and others have previously shown that transfusion strategies guided by viscoelastic tests of coagulation like thromboelastography (TEG) in patients with cirrhosis and coagulopathy with variceal bleeding, non-variceal bleeding and those undergoing invasive procedures is able to decrease transfusion requirements along with its antecedent risks.6â€“9 Although these viscoelastic tests of coagulation have been shown to be useful as compared to the INR and platelet guided transfusion but even the results of these tests correlate poorly with the bleeding risk and they underestimate the coagulation capacity. Hence, the most recent guidelines issued by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) recommend that INR should not be used to gauge the risk of bleeding prior to invasive procedures in patients with cirrhosis and prophylactic transfusion aimed at correcting the INR is not advised. Similarly prophylactic platelet transfusion or use of thrombopoietin agonists to increase platelet counts is not recommended by these guidelines. column28: Alb-PRF will be prepared according to the following protocol:For PRF preparation 5 ml blood will be collected from subjects and transferred to vacutainer tubes without anticoagulant and is centrifuged at 2700 rpms for 12 mins at room temperature. The PRF clot will be present in the middle of the tube,just between a jelly like red blood cell layer at bottom and a supernatant serum at the top which is removed with sterile tweezer. The PRF clot and the upper layer (platelet-poor plasma layer) will be collected in 5 ml sterile glasstubes and heated at 75Â°C for 10 minutes using a water bath to create denatured albumin gel(Alb). Following heating, the albumin gel will be allowed to cool to room temperature for 10 minutes. Then the remaining cells containing growth factors found within the buffy coat layer will be thereafter coated with the cooled albumin gel to form Alb-PRFwhich will be placed into the apical part of the socket. This combination combines lower-resorption properties of the albumin gel with the higher cell content and growth factorcontent of the PRF. The socket will be filled with Alb- PRF Biofiller up to 4-5 mm from the most coronal extension of the bone crest which acts as a scaffold. DFDBA graftis placed on top of the biofiller to fill the coronal part of the socket (graft layer). Socket sealing will be performed by placing gelatin sponge over the exposed portion of the graft, and the socket is then sutured using hidden x suturing technique with 4-0 silk suture.No effort will be made to approximate the wound margins by approximating the flaps. | The same DFDBA as used above will be hydrated with sterile saline and added in the sockets with light compression up to the bony crest. column51: Negative symptoms are important when it comes to prognosis and outcomes of schizophrenia. Both typical and atypical antipsychotics have shown limited effectiveness in modifying the psychopathology of negative symptoms. Hypo-activation of the ACC are found in neuroimaging studies of schizophrenia. column51: In this prospective randomized controlled trial we aim to evaluate the impact of early initiation of CRRT on outcomes in patients with acute liver failure with cerebral edema and hyperammonemia in improving cerebral edema and clinical outcomes. We also aim to evaluate the effects of early initiation of CRRT on systemic hemodynamics (cardiac output and systemic vascular resistive index, extravascular lung water and lung permeability index), endothelial function and coagulation, microcirculation (as assessed by lactate clearance and central venous oxygen saturation), mitochondrial function. Patients with ALF who meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Group 1: CRRT initiation within the first 12 hours Group 2: CRRT would be initiated i) In patients with worsening hyperammonemia despite two sessions of plasma-exchange ii) Patients meeting renal indications (hyperkalemia, volume overload, oliguria or metabolic acidosis etc) Hypothesis: We hypothesize that preemptive administration of continuous renal replacement therapy would be synergistic to plasma-exchange in ameliorating the cytokine storm, cerebral edema and improve outcomes in patients with non-acetaminophen ALF with cerebral edema compared to late initiation. Aim and Objective - AIM: Primary 1) 21-day transplant free survival with Prometheus Secondary To compare the improvement effect in cerebral edema and hepatic encephalopathy in both groups To study the safety of therapy (incidence of intradialytic hypotension, impairment of coagulation, hypothermia) Duration of mechanical ventilation and ICU stay in both groups Impact on arterial lactate Improvement in SIRS Effect on systemic hemodynamics and pulmonary function Effect on endotoxin, DAMPS, pro-inflammatory cytokines, endothelial functions and coagulation Methodology Study Protocol All patients will be evaluated as follows: Clinical history and examination Etiology of acute event Severity assessment indices Complications if any Investigations Arterial blood gas analysis Hematology CBC, Prothrombin time and INR Peripheral smear, Retics Thromboelastogram(ROTEM) S.Fibrinogen level Biochemistry Liver function testing Kidney function test Arterial ammonia levels Serum lactate CRP and procalcitonin S.Ferritin and LDH Etiology of acute event: Infectious etiology: IgM anti HAV, IgM anti HEV, IgM anti HBc ( If HBsAg +ve), IgM anti HDV ( If HBsAg +ve) , total antiHBc, anti HCV Non Infectious etiology: Alcohol binging in last 4 weeks, hepatotoxic drugs, ANA (>1: 80), IgG Non infectious etiology: Autoimmune markers, copper studies, iron studies, HOMA IR, FBS Imaging USG abdomen with Doppler for spleno-portal axis NCCT abdomen and brain Assessment of cerebral edema Optic nerve sheath diameter Transcranial doppler Electroechocardiogram Study Population: 60 patients with ALF will be randomized to two groups in 1:1 ratio. Study Design: A randomized controlled study. The study will be conducted on patients admitted to Department of Hepatology from May 2021 to March 2023 at ILBS, New Delhi Study group will comprise of patients with acute liver failure (ALF) with documented cerebral edema on CT-scan and arterial ammonia >150 ug/dl Study Period: May 2021 to March 2023 Sample Size calculation: Currently there are lack of studies investigating the timing of CRRT in patients with ALF therefore a minimum of 60 patients 30 in each group would be included in the current study. The detailed cytokine profile, endotoxin assay, markers of endothelial dysfunction and bioenergetics would be performed in a subset of 10 patients in each group. Intervention: Continuous renal replacement therapy Monitoring and Assessment: Hourly till the patient is in the intensive care unit then every 7 days for 1 month Statistical analysis All variables shall be expressed in median (range). Variables will be compared by Mann- Whitney U test. For Categorical variables we will use Chi-Square or Fisherâ€™s test. Survival analysis will be done using cox-proportional regression analysis. Actuarial probability of survival shall be calculated by Kaplan- Meier graph and compared by log- rank test. Standard medical treatment: All patients will undergo plain CT-scan of the brain to screen for the presence and severity of cerebral edema in the emergency before being shifted to the L-ICU. In the L- ICU, patients will be managed by a multidisciplinary team. Intubation and ventilation will be undertaken for standard indications in addition to the development of grade 3 encephalopathy or evidence of cerebral edema on CT-scan. Ventilation will be managed by fentanyl and propofol along with the use of atracurium for paralysis wherever required. All patients will be monitored constantly for macro-hemodynamics, global tissue perfusion, and microcirculation. The macro-hemodynamic parameters included continuous monitoring of mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate and urine output per hour. The real-time monitoring of systemic vascular resistance (SVR), stroke volume variation (SVV), cardiac index (CI) and cardiac output (CO) will be done by a hemodynamic monitor (FloTracâ„¢ system 4.0, Edwards Lifesciences, California, US) wherever feasible. Global tissue perfusion adequacy and indirect assessment of microcirculation will be done by measurement of arterial lactate. Fluid management will be done with crystalloids, with the use of colloids (5% albumin) in patients with severe hypoalbuminemia (serum albumin less than 2.5gm/dl). Norepinephrine will be the primary vasopressor used to target a mean arterial pressure of 65-70 mm of Hg. with adjunctive use of intravenous low dose hydrocortisone and vasopressin in patients not responsive to initial therapy. Cerebral edema: The monitoring of cerebral edema will be performed measuring the optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) in both the eyes using a 7.5 MHz probe every 6-8 hours. Apart from this, routine monitoring of pupillary size and reactions, extensor posturing and plantar reflexes will be performed every 6-8 hrs. Transcranial doppler would be done every 6-8 hours. Patients will receive 3% hypertonic saline as a continuous infusion, initially started at 25ml /hr and titrated 6 hourly to between 5 and 20 mL per hour (maximum 100 ml/hour) to achieve serum sodium levels between 145-150 mmol/L. Intravenous 20% mannitol (1 g/kg IV bolus) over 20 to 30 minutes will be administered to those without renal failure. All patients will in addition receive intravenous N-acetylcysteine for 5 day.Routine electroencephalogram (EEG) will be done for all patients daily to screen for non-convulsive seizures which will be managed by intravenous levetiracetam. Assessment of coagulation will be performed by ROTEM at baseline and subsequently as required. Protocol for standard-volume plasma-exchange Standard-Volume Plasma Exchange: SVPE procedures will be performed using either Spectra Optia (SPO, Terumo BCT, Lakewood, CO, USA) continuous-flow centrifugal apheresis system or Haemonetics MCS+ (Braintree, MA, USA) intermittent flow centrifugal apheresis system via a double-lumen central venous dialysis catheter. All patients will receive plasma-exchange within first 6 hours of admission to the L-ICU along with a target volume of 1.5 to 2.0 plasma volumes per session. column51: Gingival Recession is a condition in which the location of the gingival margin is apical to the cemento-enamel junction. It is one of the most common clinical finding of periodontal disease. As a result of recessions there will be loss of support and exposure of root surface which will be resulting in compromised esthetics and other associated problem like plaque retention, gingival bleeding, abrasion and pain due to cervical dentin hypersensitivity, root caries and fear of tooth loss. These consequences led to the emergence of several new methods aiming at periodontal regeneration, most coveted goal of periodontal therapy. Isolated gingival recessions have been treated by several techniques. The main goal of these periodontal plastic surgical procedures is to obtain root coverage and an optimal esthetic appearance together with the blending of mucosa and/or gingiva. These root-coverage procedures are usually based on the coronally advanced flap (CAF), and the outcome, when combined with a connective tissue graft (CTG) is considered the gold standard. However, there are some disadvantages with connective tissue graft. It is time consuming, increases morbidity, requires second surgery, leads to post-operative pain and bleeding and the supply of donor tissue is limited. So, many materials have been proposed to improve clinical outcomes in root coverage. The most recent advances in root coverage were focused on the adjunctive agents of platelet concentrates (PCs) to provide key cells and growth factors to advance healing and to promote regeneration. Five major growth factors (GFs) were released from the local application of PCs, which may enable better tissue regeneration and healing. These GFs are mainly located in the blood plasma and platelets. So, platelets have been widely used to accelerate tissue re-generation and repair in dental and medical fields. As first generation of PC, platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is identified as one mediator that has many GFs. Recently, investigators introduced platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) and concentrated growth factors (CGF). CGF was first developed by Sacco and is produced by the centrifugation of venous blood and platelets are concentrated in a gel layer containing fibrin matrix same as PRF. However, a different centrifugation speed permits the isolation of much larger, denser and richer GFs in fibrin matrix from CGF. This fibrin clot has a high cohesion because of the agglutination of fibrinogen, factor XIII and thrombin. Factor XIII a, which is activated by thrombin, causes fibrin to clot. This provides protection from plasmin degradation, resulting in higher fibrin tensile strength and stability. So, this clinical trial aims to evaluate CGFâ€™s placement together with CAF may enhance the root coverage and the healing of the soft tissue in the treatment of isolated Millerâ€™s class I or II gingival recessions. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Data from Phase 2 studies with interferon (IFN)Î±-blocking agents and a plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) antagonist have demonstrated improvement in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or cutaneous lupus disease activity, supporting the rationale for blocking the IFN pathways and pDCs in patients with SLE. Given the lack of highly efficacious and safe treatments for active SLE and the significant impact of this disease on health-related quality of life, there is currently a significant unmet need for new targeted therapies. Based on its mechanism of action (binding to immunoglobulin-like transcript 7 on the surface of pDCs, thus inducing apoptosis and reduction in the number of pDCs), VIB7734 has the potential to decrease SLE disease activity. In addition, based on data currently available, VIB7734 presents an acceptable safety profile, and hence it is justified to evaluate its potential efficacy in patients with active SLE. In this study, approximately 195 participants will be randomized in a ratio of 1:1:1 (65 participants per group) to receive VIB7734 200 mg Q4W SC, VIB7734 200 mg every 12 weeks (Q12W) SC, with an additional 200 mg SC dose at Week 4, or placebo. To maintain blinding, participants randomized to the VIB7734 200 mg Q12W SC dosing regimen will receive SC placebo injections on dosing visits outside the Q12W schedule. Randomization will be stratified by SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) total score at Screening (â‰¥ 10 or < 10) and prednisone or equivalent oral GC (OGC) dose at Baseline (Day 1) (â‰¥ 10 mg or < 10 mg). Adults aged â‰¥ 18 to â‰¤ 70 years who have moderate to severely active (recent flares or chronic active disease) SLE as defined by the SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K), British Isles Lupus Assessment Group (BILAG) 2004 Index, and Physician Global Assessment (PGA). Stabilization of the SLE treatment regimen in SLE participants prior to Baseline (Day 1) decreases the confounding of the study results by the SoC (ie, changes in disease activity post- Baseline [Day 1] are more likely to be attributable to the introduction of VIB7734, rather than a change in background therapy). Rationale for study population: Severe central nervous system (CNS) lupus and LN may be less responsive to therapy than other manifestations or may require different treatment regimens (eg, cyclophosphamide, IV Ig, highdose mycophenolate) than typically used in extrarenal SLE. Therefore, these individuals will be excluded from participating in this study. Also, individuals with significantly impaired renal function are excluded since they may have advanced, fixed disease that will not be responsive to therapy, and furthermore, these individuals are at higher risk for AEs. A urine protein: creatinine ratio (UPCr) of up to 3 mg/mg is allowed. This limit is applied because higher levels of proteinuria increase the risk of AEs. column51: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory cutaneous disorder, affecting up to 2%-5% of the world population. The major manifestation of psoriasis is erythematous, scaly patches or plaques on the skin that are occasionally pruritic but have a significant impact on patientâ€™s Quality of Life due to chronicity of the disease and frequent remissions and relapses. Psoriasis is a predominantly a T-cell mediated disorder occurring in genetically susceptible individuals, influenced by environmental factors. Methotrexate is a standard, cheaper drug for psoriasis with excellent efficacy but limited safety profile while Apremilast is a newer molecule with excellent safety profile. Comparing the standard drug alone with addition of newer drug will help in identifying better treatment options for psoriasis in terms of efficacy and safety in a disease which requires long term treatment. Methotrexate acts on cell cycle so have higher side effects like Neutropenia, Bone marrow suppression, Liver fibrosis, etc. Apremilast is a biologic which acts via Cyclic AMP pathway. So it has lesser toxicity and side effects than methotrexate. Apremilast can cause increase URTI, Flu-like symptoms in few patients. Apremilast is out of reach for common people because of its prohibiting cost. But nowadays this drug is not that costly. So adding oral Apremilast in Patients with moderate to severe psoriasis, dose of the Methotrexate can be reduced and can be stopped early and low dose oral Apremilast will be continued for a longer time. Whenever disease exacerbates, we can either increase the dose of oral Apremilast or add oral Methotrexate to control the activity. column51: Surgical pain is a universal phenomenon affecting all patients perioperatively. Apart from the agonizing sensory experience associated with it, acute pain has several deleterious effects on the physiology and the psyche of the sufferer(3).An anticipation of these effects combined with a humanitarian urge to relieve pain, play a pivotal role in provision and optimization of postoperative analgesia. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is a minimally invasive procedure which is increasingly performed as a day care procedure. Though minimally invasive, pain experienced following laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the immediate postoperative period may vary from moderate to severe in intensity. Pain after laparoscopic cholecystectomy can be divided into three compartments; visceral, parietal and referred shoulder pain. The main sources of pain include pain from incision sites(50-70%),pnemoperitoneum(20-30%),and post cholecystectomy wound(10-20%) within the liver causing visceral pain. Postoperatively common location of the pain is right upper quadrant and port sites. The main objective of treating the post-operative pain is to eradicate or, to minimize the pain and to speed up the healing process without any side effects. As a part of multi-modal analgesia, various approaches are employed for achieving safe and effective post operative analgesia. Clinical application of conventional perioperative analgesic modalities(eg.opoids,epidural analgesia)was limited because of their own drawbacks. Transversusabdominis plane block (TAP) that delivers local anaesthetic into transversusabdominis plane has been shown to reduce perioperativeopoid use in elective abdominal surgery,including open appendicectomy,laparoscopic cholecystectomies,caesarean section and laparotomies. The use of point of care ultrasonography in abdominal blocks increases the success rate and safety of the block .A variant of TAP block is (SCTAP)block where the local anesthetic is deposited between the transverse abdominis plane inferior and parallel to the costal margin. The Subcostal transverses abdominis plane block provides adequate analgesia for supraumbilical surgeries because of its greater cranial spread(T6-T10). MULTIMODAL ANALGESIA-Is defined as the use of more than one pharmacological class of analgesic medication targeting different receptors along the pain pathway with the goal of improving analgesia while reducing individual side effects.(1) Multi-modal analgesia in the peri-operative period eliminates over reliance on opoids for pain control and to reduce opoid related side effects. Preemptive multi-modal analgesia,combining non-opoid analgesics,Paracetamol,non steroidalani-inflammatory drugs or coxib and local anaesthesia has a long history. Local anesthesia improves postoperative pain and facilitates discharge on the day of surgery(4). Thus the aim of the present study is to summarize the available best evidence and well established practice for perioperative analgesia in elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Background: Inherited ichthyoses are a Mendelian Group of disorders clinically characterized by scaling and occurring due to mutations in more than 30 different genes, mainly expressed in the upper epidermis. The treatment is conventionally based on retinoids, the long-term use of which is limited by serious adverse events like teratogenicity and skeletal toxicity. There are no therapies based on the growing understanding of what causes the disease. Recent discoveries of marked elevation of IL-17 related cytokines in the skin of individuals with ichthyosis has generated interest in the use of IL-17 targeting therapies in ichthyosis. In our recent work, we observed that oral vitamin D and acitretin were both moderately effective in reducing the clinical severity of disease and improving the quality of life in patients with congenital ichthyosis. Vitamin D had a faster onset of action in terms of reducing clinical severity as compared to acitretin but the effect is not sustained. Being is a natural ligand of ROR-gamma-t, Vitamin D decreased the IL-17 pathway via this receptor; and hence, it decreased the inflammation in patients of congenital ichthyosis. column51: This present study will be carried out to explore the implementation possibilities of Asinprachalayitam(napping in sitting position) in enhancing the work efficiency without any side effect of day time sleep as per the guidelines provided in Ayurveda. The primary object of the study is to assess the effect of Vihara Asinprachalayitam on work efficiency through an Interventional study on apparently healthy volunteers. A nap can be understood as a short period of sleep for the purpose of relaxing the mind, typically taken during daytime hours as an adjunct to the usual nocturnal sleep period. All the volunteers at the time of recruitment will be told about the health benefits of Asinprachalayitam and they will be counselled and encouraged to follow the study protocol and regular follow-up will be taken to ensure compliance with the method told to them. column51: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is defined as a chronic, relapsing disease of the brain, which is characterized by a high rate of relapse. (Koob and Volkow,2016) The prevalence of alcohol use in India is 14.6%. 5.7 crore problem users of alcohol exist in India and 2.9 crore are dependent on alcohol. (Ambekar et al., 2019). Life expectancy is reduced by 20 years for an alcohol dependent person (John et al., 2013). Alcohol contributes to the development and the course of more than 200 diseases (WHO,2014). Effectiveness of the current therapies for substance use disorders is limited (Franck and Jayaram & Lindstrom, 2013; Phillips et al., 2014) and the existing medications are not beneficial for all patients (Franck and Jayaram-Lindstrom, 2013. Lack of knowledge about the etiology and pathophysiology of any substance use disorder limits efficient treatment design (Belin and Deroche-Gamonet, 2012). Due to the lack of effective treatment alternatives, focusing on more innovative, novel, and potentially more beneficial therapies and research methods seems urgent and crucial (Yavari et al., 2016). tES (Transcranial electrical stimulation) is a generic term that designates several techniques based on the modality of the applied electricity, which can be direct (transcranial direct current stimulationâ€” tDCS), random noise (transcranial random noise stimulationâ€”tRNS), or alternating (transcranial alternating current stimulationâ€”tACS) currents. tDCS, as the most frequently studied modality of tES, involves delivering a weak electrical current (1â€“2 mA) directly to the scalp through two conductive electrodes, one anode and one cathode. Anodal tDCS generally enhances cortical excitability, while cathodal tDCS decreases it. (Nitsche and Paulus, 2000) The main advantages of tDCS among all forms of non-invasive brain stimulation are its low cost, portability, and potential for home-administered use, ease of use, and absence of severe adverse effects, which may increase the adherence of psychiatric patients to the treatment. (Moffa et al., 2018) tDCS can be used to induce focal and nonfocal changes in specific neural circuits to study brainâ€“behavior relationships. tDCS has great strength of establishing a causal (not just correlational) relation between cortical activity and behavior. It is possible to create disruptions and modulation of different brain areas to explore their significance as neurocognitive targets for addiction modification. (Pascual-Leone et al., 1999, 2000) Using a well-defined tDCS paradigm, it is possible to investigate the neurochemical/neuroelectric characteristics of the living human brain. tDCS can interfere with the cognitive processing of the targeted brain areas, effects of which can be evaluated using electrophysiological methods, brain imaging, cognitive or behavioral measures and provide a functional map of causal interaction between function and structure. Because of their modulatory effects on the brain, they can be used for therapeutic applications (Luber et al., 2013). Combination of non-invasive brain stimulation and functional near infrared spectroscopy can be used to monitor cerebral hemodynamic response associated with specific events. These types of multimodal studies in the field of addiction medicine are very rare, but strongly recommended. (Jones et al., 2015; Yavari et al., 2016) Recent literature has demonstrated that the role of non invasive brain stimulation in reducing craving in those with alcohol use and other addictive disorders (Martinotti et al., 2019). Craving, is a significant factor in continued use/relapse. The current pharmacological, behavioral and other psychological treatment are only moderately successful in addressing craving and are also relatively slow in reducing craving level. (Jacobs & McCall, 2019) Therefore, we hypothesize that interventions like tDCS that can increase the power and speed with which craving can be reduced could have significant benefits, including increased retention in treatment, reduction in against medical/clinical advice discharges, and earlier and more substantial engagement in treatment while giving us possible added benefits when assessed on measures of cognitive function. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Methodology: Detail history and physical examination of patients will be taken in pain clinic. After fulfilling the criteria, patients will be explained in details about the treatment modality and a written informed consent will be taken. Diagnostic work up includes complete blood count (CBC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), coagulation profile (PT/INR), random blood sugar, kindey function test, serum electrolytes, liver function test, X-Ray lumbosacral spine (AP and lateral view), Baseline NRS and PROMIS 29 survey for low back pain will be recorded prior to the procedure After full preparation of operation room, patient will be taken to Operating room (OR) and monitors will be attached and baseline hear rate, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure and oxygen saturation and ECG will be recorded and monitored. A 20G intravenous line will be established and infusion will be started with ringer lactate solution. Hemodynamic parameters will be measured on arrival and every 2 minutes thereafter till the end of procedure. Patients diagnosed clinically as pain arising from facet joint will be given diagnostic block with 0.5% intra articular lignocaine One week after the diagnostic block all the patients who report >50% relief of pain will be randomly allocated to three groups namely Group A,Group B and Group C. All patients will be blinded before treatment and after treatment to which drugs they were injected. column51: Periodontal disease is the sixth most prevalent health condition that affects humans. It is one of the important reasons for tooth loss, impacts the quality of life of individuals. Emerging evidence links it to several systemic life threatening conditions like cardiovascular disease and diabetes making it an important public health problem. The objective of the prospective intervention trial is to assess the effectiveness of intrapocket delivery of injectable platelet rich fibrin in the non surgical management of moderate to severe periodontitis when compared to conventional scaling root planing. These autologous platelet concentrate are suspensions of growth factors and when applied locally ,they can induce soft and hard tissue regeneration. Since the standard PRF is not entirely appropriate for injection ,a new injectable formulation of PRF(termed i-PRF)enables easier use of platelet concentrate in liquid state. Otherwise healthy adults with moderate to severe periodontitis who satisfies the inclusion criteria are included in the study.Eligible individuals are randomized into test and control groups by split mouth design. Conclusions will be drawn based on the results. Treatment of periodontal disease is complicated and expensive. Many patients require invasive procedures including regenerative therapy. Adjunctive approaches to conventional non surgical therapy has page been investigated widely to avoid invasive surgical interventions. This study is such an attempt, where by an adjuvant like autologous platelet concentrate is added to conventional nonsurgical therapy in order to assess whether there is any improvement in clinical outcomes when compared to non surgical therapy alone. although PPD reduction is considered as the primary outcome, pocket closure would be considered as a clinically relevant outcome. column51: Detail history and physical examination of patients will be taken in pain clinic. After fulfilling the criteria, patients will be explained in details about the treatment modality and a written informed consent will be taken. Diagnostic work up includes complete blood count (CBC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), coagulation profile (PT/INR), random blood sugar, kidney function test, serum electrolytes, liver function test, X-Ray knee (AP and lateral view). After full preparation of operation room, patient will be taken to Operating room (OR) and monitors will be attached and baseline heart rate, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure and oxygen saturation and ECG will be recorded and monitored. column51: As controversial as the origins of rotator cuff tendinosis are, so are the treatments. Various interventions can be done for treatment such as oral medications, corticosteroid injections, prolotherapy, manipulation and surgery. Medication and steroid injection therapy only help to reduce the pain, but exercise is effective as a treatment for regaining function in addition to the reduction of pain in RC tendinopathy. However, exercise takes a long time for recovery, and patient compliance is needed to attain the maximal effect. PRP has been used as a treatment option in other orthopaedic diseases since it contains growth factors that stimulate tissue repair. Prolotherapy is a nonsurgical regenerative injection technique that introduces small amounts of an irritant solution to the site of painful and degenerated tendon insertions (entheses), joints, ligaments, and adjacent joint spaces to promote the growth of normal cells and tissues. Recently, Platelet-rich plasma PRP and Prolotherapy have emerged as effective therapy in the treatment of rotator cuff tendinosis. column51: Patients attending outpatient and inpatient clinical services of NIMHANS will be screened for the eligibility criteria of diagnosis, presence of positive symptoms, and antipsychotic trial. Eligible individuals will be assessed for capacity to consent, and written informed consent will be sought from those having intact capacity. Age and sex-matched healthy controls will be recruited after screening for eligibility. All the recruited individuals will be comprehensively assessed using semi-structured and structured clinical tools and neuropsychological tools. They will also undergo Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and TMS-Evoked Potentials (TEP) protocols after ascertaining magnetic safety. The patients will be randomised to Verum or Sham tACS groups and will receive 5 days of tACS in the blinded trial. Patients, tACS treatment administrator, clinical rater, and data entry operator will remain blinded for the study group till the end of the study. Permutation block randomisation method with a variable block size of 4-6 will be followed for allocating individuals into the two groups. Allocation concealment, as well as blinding, will be maintained by using the codes provided by the device manufacturer for true/sham delivery of current. After 5 days (10 sessions) of tACS, patients would be offered 5 more days (10 sessions) of open-label extension with true-tACS. During this phase, participants and administrators will remain blinded to the intervention administered in the previous RCT phase. Adverse effects of tACS will be assessed after every session. Psychotropic medication will be maintained at stable doses during the trial. On development of any clinical situation necessitating a change in medications (apart from rescue medications), patients will be considered as drop-outs from the study. column51: This is a Phase III, prospective, multicenter, open-label, efficacy and safety study in AQP4 antibody seropositive NMOSD patients, either treatment-naÃ¯ve (who have not received any prior maintenance DMT or IST) or inadequate responders to previous treatment with RTX (or its biosimilar). The study will include the following two cohorts. â— Cohort 1: treatment-naÃ¯ve NMOSD patients (no history of DMTs or IST; n=60) â— Cohort 2: NMOSD patients who are inadequate responders to previous treatment with RTX (as last treatment and at least 2 infusions of RTX or its biosimilar; time since last RTX infusion is <6 months; n=40) The total length of the study, from screening of the first patient to the end of the study depends on the recruitment rate and is expected to be approximately 188 weeks. This includes an enrolment period of 76 weeks. Statistical Methods The analysis of this study is exploratory and will primarily make use of descriptive statistical methods. No formal confirmatory hypothesis test will be conducted. No adjustment for multiple testing will be made. The intent-to-treat (ITT) and Safety population will include all enrolled patients who received any dose of satralizumab. The per-protocol (PP) population will include all ITT patients without major protocol deviations deemed to potentially affect the efficacy endpoints. The PP population will be used for supportive efficacy analyses. Unless otherwise specified, all endpoints will be analyzed separately for each cohort and by visit, if appropriate. Details will be specified in the statistical analysis plan (SAP). Primary Analysis The TFR up to week 96 will be assessed using the Kaplan-Meier method. The proportion of relapse-free patients after week 96 will also be calculated using the Kaplan-Meier estimator (at Week 96) and Greenwoods formula for the confidence interval. The ARR after Week 96 will be calculated descriptively by dividing the total number of relapses for all patients by the total years of drug exposure. Severity of relapses assessed as hospitalization, use of corticosteroids, rescue therapy, need for plasma exchange, and residual disability will be summarized descriptively. EDSS and EDSS change from baseline will be summarized descriptively up to week 96. Time to onset of CDP sustained for at least 12 weeks and 24 weeks will be analyzed using the Kaplan Meier method. column51: Ulcerative Collitis (UC) is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory condition of the large intestine that is frequently associated with inflammation of the rectum but often extends proximally to involve additional areas of the colon. The absence of rectal involvement has been noted in fewer than 5% of adult patients with UC at diagnosis but may be seen in up to one-third of pediatric-onset colitis. Determination of the extent and severity of disease is important to select the appropriate treatment algorithm. Extent of the disease should be characterized according to the Montreal classification as proctitis (E1), left-sided colitis (E2), or extensive colitis (E3) (extension proximal to the splenic flexure). [4,5] Commonly, severity of UC has been classified according to the Truelove and Witts’ [6] criteria published in 1955. Mild colitis is defined as fewer than 4 bowel movements daily, normal temperature, heart rate, hemoglobin (>11 g/dL), and ESR (<20 mm/hr). Severe disease is defined by bowel frequency greater than 6 times a day in conjunction with fever, tachycardia, anemia, or an elevation in ESR. Tofacitinib, a JAK-STAT (Janus kinase-signal transducers and activators of transcription) inhibitor and an anti-inflammatory drug, is a new addition to the treatment modalities for UC. Janus kinases are intracellular tyrosine kinases which mediate the signal transduction of various cytokines involved in the inflammatory reactions in IBD, like IL- 6, IL-7, Il-10, IL-12, IFNÎ±, IFNÎ² 2, 4, 7, 9 etc. The advantages of JAK- STAT inhibitors over monoclonal antibodies include, the oral administration, predictable pharmacokinetics with reduced plasma half- life, rapid onset of action, quick clearance, lack of immunogenicity and an intracellular target. This is a placebo controlled randomized clinical study in subjects with ASUC. Patients with acute severe UC (defined as 6 or more stools with blood and 1 or more of the following hemoglobin <10.5 g/dL, erythrocyte sedimentation rate [ESR] >30 mm/hr or CRP > 30 mg/L, fever >37.8Â°C, or tachycardia >90/min; the modified Truelove Witts criteria) and fulfilling all other inclusion/exclusion criteria will be randomized. A computer-generated randomization schedule will be used to assign subjects to either of the two groups at a 1:1 allocation ratio. Group 1 : Intravenous hydrocortisone (300 mg per day in three divided doses) plus Tofacitinib (10 mg thrice daily) for 7 days Group 2 : Intravenous hydrocortisone (300 mg per day in three divided doses) plus Placebo (thrice daily) for 7 days. column51: There have been multiple invasive as well as noninvasive options to treat scars , yet no universally accepted treatment modality that can provide maximal benefits and minimal side effects. Platelet rich plasma is a new adjunct in the field of scar management that has showcased promising results. The ability to supply an increased concentration of growth factors to tissues targeted, forms the basis of its action. Minimal to no side effects have been found in the limited research done till now. This technique has shown good results in treating post burn, atrophic acne scars, posttraumatic and surgical scars individually. There is a dearth in research evaluating effect of autologous platelet rich plasma in healed scars due to multiple etiologies as compared to conventional methods such as silicon based products like gel and sheet. The purpose of this study is to assess the role pf platelet rich plasma during maturation phase of wound healing. By assessing the efficacy of platelet rich plasma as compared to silicone products in healed scars in terms of aesthetic outcome and complications, we can evaluate the advantages and potential of practical application of this newer modality over currently used methods of scar management. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Owing to the osteogenic potential, autogenous bone grafts (ABGs) have been widely used in periodontics for the treatment of intrabony defects (IBDs). The harvesting of autologous bone graft requires a secondary surgical site (i.e., a donor site) which increases postoperative patient discomfort. To address these problems, alternatives to autologous bone graft materials (alloplast bone graft) have been developed. Alloplast (B-OSTIN), is known to enhance the tissue regeneration. PRF in combination with bone mineral had the ability in increasing the regenerative effects in intrabony defects. Second-generation platelet concentrate, platelet rich fibrin (PRF), developed in France by Choukroun et al in 2001, is a fibrin-matrix in which platelet, cytokines and cells are entrapped that are released after a certain time and can serve as resorbable membrane. Injectable PRF (i PRF) is a PC in the liquid form that can be polymerized with bone graft. I-PRF mixed with bone graft is called sticky bone. To the best of our knowledge, there are only few clinical studies available to evaluate the efficacy of sticky bone with alloplastic bone graft in the treatment of intrabony defects. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Iron deficiency anemia(IDA) in infancy is of important concern because of its potential detrimental effect on physical and cognitive development. column51: INTRODUCTION- Post renal transplantation bone disease is characterized by changes in bone quality and density as well as mineral metabolism, which contribute to increased fracture risk. World Health Organization (WHO) criteria for osteoporosis is T score of less than -2.5 and a T score between â€“1 to â€“2.5 is classified as osteopenia. The novel anti-osteoporotic drug Denosumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody against RANKL. By inhibiting the development and the activity as well as reducing the survival of osteoclasts it decreases bone resorption and increases bone density. The hypothesis of the present study is that Denosumab has a beneficial effect on the loss of BMD after renal transplantation. The preservation of BMD is a surrogate parameter, generally predicting subsequent improvements in the occurrence rate of fractures. The hypothesis will be tested by studying the effect of denosumab on osteoporosis in post-renal allograft transplant recipients. In this open labelled, randomized, and controlled prospective intervention trial, we will compare the effect of denosumab along with calcium plus vit D3 versus calcium plus vit D3 therapy on bone mineral density by evaluating DEXA- T score in osteoporosis after renal transplant . column51: Platelet Rich Fibrin: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is a concentrate of cells and growth factors generated from the centrifugation of whole blood. It is a second generation platelet concentrate that has been introduced by Choukroun J in 2001. Since then it has been widely used in oral, dental and periodontal applications for its accelerated healing capacity. Platelet rich fibrin constitutes a fibrin matrix within which blood cells like platelets and leukocytes are entrapped during the clot formation (polymerisation). It also consists of growth factors like vascular endothelial growth factors, platelet derived growth factor, transforming growth factor, fibroblast like growth factor etc that are released from an activated platelet and white blood cells. Apart from these they also contain proteins like fibronectin, fibrinogen, thrombospondin and other immunomodulatory cytokines etc. Accumulating data supports that the beneficial effects of PRF is due to its 3 dimensional fibrin matrix that has platelets and leukocytes entrapped within it and an enormous amount of growth factors and other proteins released from these cells. PRF when used at surgical or infected wound site, mimics as a scaffold of fibrin matrix loaded with growth factors, proteins and cytokines that are released into the wound area as the fibrin matrix degrades. These released growth factors and proteins help in wound healing by enhancing cellular activity like proliferation, differentiation of cells like osteoblast, fibroblast, even stem cells and promote angiogenesis at the wound area. In addition to this PRF has an immunomodulatory effect through M1-to-M2 transition in macrophage polarisation and reduces osteoclastogenesis and suppresses inflammatory response. This together reduces the destruction at the inflammatory site and enhances regeneration. Injectable platelet-rich fibrin (I-PRF): Injectable platelet-rich fibrin (I-PRF) is the most recent and successful advancement in PRF. In brief, it was created by slowing down the liquid-based centrifugation approach and omitting the formation of a PRF membrane. It has the added advantage of being available as a liquid consistency period of 10 - 15 mins after centrifugation and gets polymerised slowly to form a fibrin clot.16 It can be injected into tissue for therapeutic purposes. I-PRF is referred to as an advanced type of PRF since it is injected (autologous PRF) into soft tissues, mucous membranes, or skin. Aim & Objective of the study: Local drug delivery systems are preferred in isolated periodontal pockets over systemic therapy. The search for the more suitable vehicle for the local drug delivery in periodontal pockets that can render controlled release of drugs are widely researched. Injectable platelet rich fibrin being autologous and injectable could be a suitable vehicle for local delivery of drugs. This study aims to evaluate the possibility of using i-PRF as a controlled release drug (Doxycycline) vehicle in periodontal therapy and its clinical and antimicrobial effectiveness compared to iPRF without doxycycline and only mechanical therapy (Scaling and root planing). | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Despite the protection of cartilage has traditionally been the main focus of research, the sub-chondral bone has become a potential therapeutic target in OA. The use of drugs that act in the subchondral bone such as alendronate, have shown improvements in the quality and structure of this tissue, preventing cartilage loss. Current approaches for the treatment of OA have recently incorporated the use of biologics that mediate the inflammatory process. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is increasingly used for its ability to affect tissue regulation from the growth factors present in elevated platelet levels and thereby reduce pain associated with OA. Following signing of Informed Consent, participants who fulfil ACR/EULAR 2016 classification criteria will be assessed for eligibility during Screening 1 period of up to 6 weeks. column51: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) represents a spectrum of neuropsychiatric abnormalities seen in patients with liver dysfunction after exclusion of other known brain diseases (1). The Working Party at the 11th World Congress of Gastroenterology, Vienna proposed a multi-axial definition of HE which included type of hepatic abnormality (type A, B or C) and presentation of neurological manifestations (episodic, persistent or minimal HE) in chronic liver disease (CLD). (2) Formerly called subclinical HE and now termed Minimal hepatic encephalopathy (MHE) is mild cognitive impairment of patients having cirrhosis and/or portosystemic shunts. MHE was included as third and final category of type B and C HE. MHE is a part of the clinical spectrum of HE rather than a separate phenomenon. (2,3) HE shows a wide spectrum of neuropsychiatric manifestations while minimal hepatic encephalopathy is largely under recognized. The subtle presentation of this disorder means that it is difficult to ascertain whether all patients with cirrhosis should be tested or whether testing should be limited only to patients who have complaints of mild changes in daily functioning. MHE diagnosis is important as affected patients may have impaired global functioning and driving ability, increased falls, and reduced quality of life. (7) Other than HE one of the other common complication associated with cirrhosis is sarcopenia or loss of skeletal muscle mass. Its prevalence in patients with cirrhosis is estimated to be 40-70%. Interestingly HE has a close correlation with the presence of sarcopenia. (15) The prevalence of MHE has been reported to vary between 24% and 80% in patients with cirrhosis of liver depending on both examinable dimensions of disease and fixed diagnostic cut offs. (2,3) The large variation in prevalence among different studies is related to the criteria used for the diagnosis and demographics of the patient population included. Factors associated with MHE include prior episodes of overt HE (13), presence of esophageal varices (13), severity of liver disease (CTP score), age, alcoholic etiology (13), TIPS and surgical porto-systemic shunts. The prevalence of MHE is lower in Child class A, 36% than in those with cirrhotics with advanced liver disease- Child class B, 45%, and Child class C, 72%. (14) European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) guidelines recommends use of non-absorbable disaccharides for management of MHE in patients with cirrhosis of liver. However, there is lack of robust data regarding the recommendation.(15) The available data from studies suggests that patients with MHE have poor outcomes in term of overall survival, sarcopenia and it further progress to development of HE as compared with general population. (16) There are 2 RCTs available which evaluated the role of FMT in HE. These studies suggest a possible beneficial role of change in gut microbiome secondary to FMT in the prevention of further episodes of HE. The limitation of the available FMT in overt HE include a small sample size, and use of antibiotics prior to FMT. There are no studies evaluating the role of FMT in patients with MHE. Therefore, in this RCT, we plan to compare the effect of FMT vs lactulose on the resolution of MHE | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: The purpose of this clinical trial is to learn about the safety and effects of the study medicine (called marstacimab) for the potential treatment of hemophilia in pediatric patients. column51: The intrauterine environment is relatively hypoxic compared with the extrauterine environment. column51: Children with cancer are prone to several infections including bacterial and fungal. This increased risk of infection can be due to cancer or due to treatment of cancer. Infections in cancer patients can result in several problems including prolonged hospitalization, interruption of treatment of cancer and in severe cases even death. The usual treatment for infections includes antibiotics for bacterial infections. Granulocytes are type of white blood cells that compose blood just like other components of the blood such as haemoglobin, platelets, etc. Granulocytes are responsible for combating infections. Children with cancer, because of aggressive chemotherapies or sometimes due to the nature of the disease observed to have benefitted through granulocyte transfusion especially in cases of septicemia along with standard antibiotics, oxygen support fluid transfusion etc. Granulocytes are collected, like blood or any other blood component donation, and here it will be done in a well-equipped facility of Department of Transfusion Medicine under controlled environment at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai. The granulocytes collected from voluntary donors through â€˜Apheresisâ€™ can be transfused in these patients. In this study we are looking at the benefits of granulocyte transfusion to pediatric cancer patients who are dealing with septicemia. For better assessments we will compare two sets of patient, one receiving granulocyte with other routine standardized supportive therapy while other set of patients will not receive granulocyte transfusion. This will be done through randomization. After consenting the granulocytes shall be given immediately after collection from voluntary donors, if randomized to study arm. The study is aimed at finding out the efficacy of granulocyte transfusion therapy in children with sepsis diagnosed with cancer and receiving treatment at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai. If the study results prove that granulocyte treatment is efficacious in treating infection in cancer patients, then it will be a major breakthrough and it might be established as one of the standards of care for viruses all over the country. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Topic : outcome of ultrasound guided platelet rich plasma injection in partial thickness rotator cuff tear. Research question: Is platelet rich plasma effective in the treatment of partial thickness rotator cuff tear patients? Research question: Platelet rich plasma is effective in the treatment of partial thickness rotator cuff tear patients. Aim: To study the outcome of platelet rich plasma injection in the treatment of partial thickness rotator cuff tear. OBJECTIVES: PRIMARY OBJECTIVES: To assess the outcome of platelet rich plasma injection in partial thickness rotator cuff tear in relation to: 1. Pain using VAS (Visual Analogue Scale). 2. column28: Arthrocentesis is performed with the standard double needle puncture technique with 150-200ml of Ringers lactate. After the arthrocentesis process is completed, the second needle will be removed with the first needle in place. i-PRF is injected through the first needle immediately after the arthrocentesis | Technique: Standard double puncture arthrocentesis Holmlund â€“Hellsing line (i.e canthotragus line) is taken as the landmark for the puncture sites. 2 guiding points are marked with reference to Holmlund â€“Hellsing line over the skin. The first point is 10 mm ahead of tragus and 2 mm below Holmlund â€“Hellsing line. The second point is 20 mm ahead and 10 mm inferiorly in the same line (indicates site of TMJ eminence). The Auriculotemporal nerve block is given, and 18-gauge needle is inserted from 1st point followed by injection of 2mL Ringers Lactate solution into the joint space. The second needle also of 18 gauge is inserted from the second guide point. The pressurized washing is done with 5% ringer lactate solution and volume of 150-200ml injecting from first needle and exit from the second needle | PREPARATION OF i-PRF Blood for the preparation is withdrawn from the medial cubital /cephalic vein under aseptic condition. Patient is seated erect with back supported with the supported forearm in supine position. The site is inspected to identify the suitable vein. The tourniquet is applied and the patient is made to make the fist. After identifying the suitable vein, the part was cleansed with the antiseptic solution. 10 ml needle was carefully inserted in the identified vein with bevel facing upward and when blood appears in the needle hub the needle is slightly pushed inside by about 1-4 mm and the blood was withdrawn. Thus, collected blood was transferred into the sterile glass tubes without anticoagulant. The tube was immediately centrifuged at 700rpm for 3 minutes with the help of PRF centrifuge machine . After centrifugation, two layers were identified the bottom layer of red blood cells and the top layer of i-PRF . The upper layer was collected with a 3 ml needle. block is performed with local anesthesia . The articular fossa is located at a point 10 mm anterior and 2 mm below the canthotragus line. . 2 mL i-PRF injected in the articular cavity and 1mL in the pericapsular tissue with 24gauge needle.

column51: Temporomandibular disorders appear to be common problem and have major impact in the quality of the life. Various management modalities such as splints, physiotherapy, arthrocentesis, intra-articular injections of agents like HA, PRP and i-PRF have been used for the relief of the symptoms primarily pain and reduced mouth opening. Arthrocentesis is minimal invasive procedure that can be performed without significant complications. The significant positive clinical outcomes, cost effectiveness and the minimal use of the armamentarium has increased its application in management of TMD. The development of the i-PRF and the studies related to i-PRF in the patients with TMD showed significant positive effects in reduction of the symptoms. i-PRF can be easily prepared and is obtained from the patientâ€™s own blood with no significant intra-operative and post intervention complication such as allergic reactions due to the blood concentrate used. Hence, it seems logical to use i-PRF individually or arthrocentesis combined with i-PRF. column51: As per International Diabetes Federation (IDF) 10th edition year 2021 global prevalence of diabetes was 10.5% projecting to 12.2 % by year 2045. For India, diabetes prevalence was reported as 8.3%. Diabetic foot ulcers are among the most challenging complications of patients who have diabetes mellitus which is not well controlled. Around 15 to 25% of patients with diabetes mellitus will develop a diabetic foot ulcer during their lifetime. It is usually the result of poor glycemic control, underlying neuropathy, peripheral vascular disease, or poor foot care. It is also one of the common cause for osteomyelitis of the foot and amputation of lower extremities. Zhang et al reported, 6.3 % global prevalence of diabetic foot in meta-analysis. As the number of newly diagnosed diabetics are increasing yearly, the incidence of diabetic foot ulcer is also bound to increase. Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are responsible for more admissions than any other diabetic complication. Diabetic foot and related sepsis was found out to be the second most common form of infection-related mortality (8.3%) in hospitalized patients. Loss of a limb leads to enormous morbidity and many patients are not able to afford a prosthesis. Most remain disabled for life and lead a poor quality of life. DFUs contribute to approximately 80% of all non-traumatic amputations in India, annually. Patients with a history of DFU have 40% higher 10-year death-rate, than those without. Average time required for healing of DFUs is 28 weeks (range 12-62 weeks). Platelet derived growth factor (PDGF) is a dimeric protein, composed of 2 disulfide â€“ linked polypeptide chain. PDGF is a protein normally found in platelets, macrophages, and endothelial cells. It promotes cell mitogenesis and migration and synthesis of protein and extracellular matrix components. It has been shown in preclinical and clinical studies to promote the formation of granulation tissue at the wound site and to stimulate wound healing. Microscopic examination of the wounds treated with topical PDGF showed a marked increased intensity of the inflammation phase of the wound healing cascade characterized by an increased presence of neutrophils, monocytes and fibroblasts grossly. It is hypothesized that PDGF positively promotes angiogenesis indirectly through its activities on other inflammatory cells. Extracellular matrix degradation is one of the healing processes that, if left uncontrolled, may result in non-healing or chronic wounds. PDGF, which includes promoting the chemotactic recruitment and proliferation of cells involved in wound repair. There are several centrifugation systems that allow point-of-care preparation of a highly concentrated platelet formula, rich in growth factors that are reintroduced to the wound in order to accelerate healing. Driver et al. (2006) (n=40) reported that 68.4% of patients with non-healing diabetic foot ulcers randomized to platelet gel healed compared to 42.9% in the control group. Wockhardt has developed Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate (AGFC) kit called as Healrex for use in diabetic foot ulcer. column28: Dextrose prolotherapy injection solution will be prepared by a combination of 1.5ml of 25% dextrose and 0.5 ml of 0.5% bupivacaine. Whole blood will be drawn in a 20ml syringe by venipuncture which is then transferred to Acid Citrate Dextrose tubes. These tubes are then centrifuged using a soft spin at 2400 rpm for ten minutes. The lower 1/3rd is platelet rich plasma (PRP) and upper 2/3rd is platelet poor plasma (PPP). 2ml of PRP is procured by removing the PPP. column51: Externalizing behaviours (EBs) are behavioural issues that manifest themselves in childrenâ€™s outward behaviour, such as rule-breaking, aggression, and delinquency. Because of the immediate and long-term negative consequences of those behaviours, they are regarded as highly problematic for society.A dimensional framework of â€œexternalizing psychopathologyâ€ encompasses poor impulse control, poor attention allocation, heightened emotional reactivity, verbal and physical aggression, violation of rules and substance abuse (American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5).The externalization construct would include the DSM-V disorder of attention deficit/ hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD) and Conduct disorder, Disruptive mood dysregulation disorders, mood disorders and substance use (American Psychiatric Association, 2022).Medial-prefrontal cortex (mPFC), notably the ventromedial-prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), and subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC), as well as additional salient regions in anterior/mid insula, are principally involved in implicit regulation of emotions (Abend et al.,2016; Adamazek et al.,2017). column51: Alcohol use in dependent pattern is a global problem, affecting individuals in almost every domain with its impact on family, society, and as a whole nation. Progressing disease is accompanied with neglect of alternative interest, social, family, and occupational activities. Attempts to quit are often unsuccessful and the patient continues to use the substance despite knowledge of physical and/or psychological harm (DSM-5, 2013; Daley,2013). A major problem jeopardizing recovery from alcoholism is high alcohol craving and the chronic, relapsing nature of the illness. Although pharmacologic treatments with Naltrexone, Topiramate and Acamprosate for alcohol dependence in primary care and specialty medical setting alone and in combination with brief or more extensive psychosocial therapies are available, these have often only modest or controversial effects (Assanangkornchai&Srisurapanont, 2007; Miller et al., 2011; Fox et al.,2007; Breese et al., 2011). column51: Alcohol dependence presently constitutes one of the most serious public health problems, as an estimated 3â€“8% of all deaths and 4% of all disability-adjusted life-years worldwide are attributable to alcohol consumption (Prince et al., 2007).Alcohol use disorder(AUD) is a chronic, relapsing illness and leads to significant morbidity and heavy social and financial burden.Most of the studies suggest that the prefrontal regions, particularly the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), play a major role in craving associated with drugs. Chronic alcohol use can lead to weakened connectivity ACC and mPFC reflecting as weakened ability of alcohol-associated incentive motivation signals to gain control over salience network activity and motor action. The deep TMS coil primarily targets the ACC and mPFC and has been for approved by FDA for treatment in OCD.Since both addictive behaviours and OCD fall under impulsive-compulsive spectrum of disorders, it could be effective in modulating the addictive behaviour in patients of alcohol dependence. Substance intake often starts out as impulsive but later because of the pleasurable experiences and negative affectivity in the absence of alcohol turns into compulsive behaviour. Not all patients diagnosed with alcohol dependence syndrome receive treatment due to lack of effective treatments with good patient acceptance and this could be a possible explanation for this treatment gap.The better option would be noninvasive neuromodulation targeting particular brain areas involved in alcohol addiction rather than phramacological agents with multitude of complications.
