column51: â€¢28.7% of the Indian population suffers from symptomatic Osteoarthritis knee. (4) â€¢Such a high prevalence is not always translated to all the patients seeking medical help, due to a lack of disease awareness and the prevalent low socio-economic status of the majority of these patients. â€¢Many a times such patients land up with severe knee problems which include pain as well as deformities, when joint replacement is the only option left. â€¢The currently chosen treatment modalities for the early stages of knee OA are mainly OPIOID (NSAIDs) and corticosteroids which have been proven to cause harm to patients in the long run. â€¢There is a huge void when it comes to disease-modifying and disease-reversing treatment modalities which are capable of stopping and reversing the cartilage degradation associated with knee osteoarthritis. â€¢As evidenced by numerous studies, the safety and efficacy of PRP and Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate in the treatment of osteoarthritis are well established. â€¢Does the established clinical improvement seen after IAIs of Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate and PRP correlate well with the radiological and biochemical findings noted after these injections? â€¢Which treatment modality out of PRP and Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate has a more prominent effect clinically, biochemically and radiologically in knees affected with osteoarthritis? â€¢Aim- To compare the efficacy of IA injections of PRP with those of IA injections of Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate in KL grade 2 and 3 of knee osteoarthritis. â€¢Objectives- Â·To identify the cases which can be managed with intra-articular injections of PRP and Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate . Â·To administer 2 IA injections of PRP/ Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate, 4 weeks apart. Â·To compare the VAS and WOMAC scores before each injection and at the 6-month and 9-month follow-up from the 1st injection. Â·To compare the change in biomarker of cartilage degeneration (serum Coll2-1No2) values after IA PRP injection vs IA Autologous Growth Factor Concentrate injection with the clinical improvement seen after the intervention. Â·To compare the articular cartilage changes on specialized MRI sequences(WORMS) before and after the intervention. â€¢Inclusion- â€¢Patients who are satisfying the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria (9) for diagnosis of osteoarthritis knee. â€¢Radiological findings of Grade II and III Osteoarthritis of the knee joint, according to the Kellgren-Lawrence scale (10). â€¢Exclusion- â€¢Any malignancy. â€¢Drug Abuse â€¢Gouty Arthritis /inflammatory arthritis, Secondary Osteoarthritis â€¢Active knee infection. â€¢Patient Suffering from Anemia, Disorders of Bleeding â€¢Rheumatoid Arthritis â€¢Genu varum/valgum >5 degree â€¢Uncontrolled Diabetes Mellitus â€¢Ligamentous instability of knee (Tested by Clinical examination) â€¢Osteoarthritis of any other joint â€¢Patient in whom MRI is contraindicated. Pre-Procedure Protocol â€¢An informed written consent will be obtained from all the patients willing to participate in the study on an Informed consent form (ICF) as per the guidelines of Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC). â€¢Following investigation will be done: Ã˜Complete blood count(CBC) . Ã˜Platelet count. Ã˜Random Blood Sugar(RBS). Ã˜X RAY KNEE ANTEROPOSTERIOR AND LATERAL VIEW ( IN STANDING POSITION). Ã˜Serum Coll2-1NO2 levels. Ã˜MRI of the single most affected knee(WORMS). Random allocation of all the recruited patients will be done into two groups, by a clinician who is not involved in the study: â€¢The randomisation of all the recruited patients will be computer generated â€¢ GROUP P: Patients in this group will be given 2 intra articular injections of platelet rich plasma in the single most affected knee â€¢GROUP G: Patients in this group will be given 2 intra-articular injections of growth factor concentrate in the single most affected knee â€¢The randomisation will be done by a clinician from the department who is not involved in the study via a computer-generated random allocation system. â€¢The triple-blinding will be maintained by blinding the patient concerning what modality is being administered to them (will be explained to them while taking consent), the clinician administering the injection will be blinded as to which injection he will be administering, also the statistician analysing the results will be blinded as to which group will receive which injection. â€¢Triple blinding will be broken if patient presents to us with any complications post intraarticular injections(such as infection, severe pain), if patient wants to discontinue treatment and opt out from the study. â€¢Platelet Rich Plasma will be made by PRP Method â€¢All aseptic precautions will be taken. â€¢We will Obtain 24-42.5 ml Whole blood in 8.5 ml acid citrate dextrose (ACD) Tubes by venipuncture from the antecubital vein. â€¢Then we will Centrifuge the blood using a soft spin @1500rpm for 10 minutes. column51: INTRODUCTION Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a new term for a condition more renowned as atrophic vaginitis. It is used to describe a variety of menopausal symptoms and signs that are related to the physical changes of the vulva, vagina and lower urinary tract. The etiology of GSM is secondary to decreased levels of endogenous estrogens and represents a common but underreported condition. In 45% of menopausal women, it is clinically manifested as a syndrome consisting mainly of vaginal dryness, itching, irritation and, if the woman is sexually active, dyspareunia.(1) Currently Intra-Vaginal application of estrogen has been considered an effective treatment of atrophic vaginitis.(2,3) Recently, PRP has becoming popular as a non-operative treatment option for GSM symptoms. The principle underlying PRP treatment has to do with its ability to reproduce natural mechanisms of cell regeneration through the sequential secretion of numerous growth factors.(4) However women are reluctant to use PRP due to the problems of thromboembolism and endometrial hyperplasia Following PRP injection, vaginal vascularity seems to increase with a subsequent improvement of sexual function. In addition, the mucosa becomes thicker and firmer, making the vagina look much more youthful.(4) RATIONALE The effects of PRP treatment have been evaluated in many clinical conditions, including wound healing, hair repair, skin regeneration, vulvar lichen sclerosis, stress urinary incontinence, episiotomy scars, and lubrication aging in the vagina with good results. It has better compliance, cheaper and less frequent dosing schedule as compared to intravaginal estrogen creams. AIM AND OBJECTIVES AIM We aim to study and compare the effectiveness of intravaginal PRP and estrogen cream in treatment of Genitourinary syndrome in post menopausal women. OBJECTIVES 1. To study the effectiveness of intravaginal PRP in treatment of GSM in postmenopausal women by studying the improvement in VHI and VAS 2. To study the effectiveness of intravaginal ESTROGEN in treatment of GSM in postmenopausal women by studying the improvement in VHI and VAS 3. To study and compare the improvement in GSM symptoms in both study groups. REVIEW OF LITERATURE (ROL) Present study is aimed to compare the clinical improvement in symptoms of GSM in post-menopausal women using estrogen creams and PRP therapy. The etiology of GSM is secondary to decreased levels of endogenous estrogens and represents a common and underreported condition due to sexual embarrassment or general disregard due to associating it as a liability of natural aging(6). The syndrome or its features manifest in approximately 15% of premenopausal(7) and 40-54% of postmenopausal women(8). The symptoms of GSM are particularly bothersome and usually require intervention, as vaginal health represents an essential component of active and healthy aging in women at midlife and beyond. In the literature, various hormonal products or vaginal lubricants or moisturizers are used in order to relieve patientâ€™s symptoms.(9) PRP is an autologous solution of human plasma that has an increased content of platelets (4-7 times the baseline concentration).(10) The principle underlying PRP treatment has to do with its ability to reproduce natural mechanisms of cell regeneration through the sequential secretion of numerous growth factors (platelet-derived growth factors, transforming growth factors b, epithelial growth factors, vascular endothelial growth factor, insulin-like growth factor, basic fibroblast growth factors), which modulate cell proliferation, differentiation, angiogenesis and chemotaxis.(11,12) A few pilot studies concerning GSM treatment using PRP have reported promising findings. Kim et al reported the use of autologous lipofilling mixed with PRP in a 67 year-old patient with vaginal atrophy. Lipofilling with PRP relieved symptoms, restored contour of the labia majora and achieved remission of lichen sclerosus on labia minora.(13) A similar study regarding the use of estrogen creams and PRP for the treatment of GSM in post menopausal women is conducted by Fayoum university Egypt by aboshama in 2021.(2) In conclusion, PRP is an innovative, affordable and easily performed therapeutic modality, which has been recently studied in women with various urogenital disorders. Although the specific mechanisms of action of PRP have not been completely elucidated, various studies have shown that the high concentration of growth factors in PRP may potentially initiate inflammatory reactions and promote the healing process(14,15). Efficacy appears promising and the risks of PRP therapy seem to be minimal. However, evidence is based on a few low-quality pilot studies(13,16), case reports and anecdotal series, including only a small number of patients and with a short-term follow-up. column51: Negative symptoms are an important predictor of poor functional outcome by negatively influencing patientsâ€™ ability to perform activities of daily living and tends to be more persistent and antipsychotic drugs have been only mildly effective in improving negative symptoms. Moreover, negative symptoms are consistently related to specific neuroanatomical correlates, especially with the prefrontal cortex. DLPFC is the most often used target for negative symptoms in schizophrenia, however recent studies revealed that the effect of rTMS on negative symptoms in schizophrenia was disputed and ambiguous. Moreover, the evidence-based guidelines have reduced the level of evidence from B to C for negative symptoms of schizophrenia. , the mechanism, underlying negative symptoms, may has a close relationship with DMPFC. Some evidences revealed that an aberrant reward pathway might contribute to negative symptoms, including anhedonia, social amotivation and voluntary impairments. DMPFC is an important joint of the reward circuit. Moreover, previous study had revealed the protocol of DMPFC-rTMS could improve the connectivity of reward pathway. There is dearth of literature in the utility of iTBS targetting mPFC to decrease the deficit symptoms in a schizophrenia patient and double cone coil iTBS has advantage over other techniques of non-invasive brain stimulation as it has better cortical penetration. column51: Dental caries is the among the commonest and highly prevalent diseases worlwide affecting 486million children with primary teeth and 2.4billion adults with permanent teeth globally.According to WHO, dental caries affects 60â€“90 % of schoolchildren globally, mainly in developing countries resulting in pain,infections,undernutrition thereby affecting growth and development and decrease in overall quality of life.Therefore it is of utmost importance to treat effectively and prevent dental caries from progressing, at an earlier stage, to avoid all the complications.The ideal way of treating moderately affected carious tooth is by removing the bacteria by cavity preparation followed by a cement or resin-based dental restoration. However,the complete eradication of bacteria prior to insertion of restoration plays an important role in determining the longevity of the restoration and correspondingly the success of the treatment. Bacteria can remain viable on the dentinal surface even after cavity preparation. They may survive and multiply in the presence of microleakage, which may lead to pulpal irritation, risk of recurrent caries and/or postoperative sensitivity and ultimately failure of the restoration. Attempts at the complete removal of deep carious dentin, by solely mechanical means, may result in pulp exposure and gross destruction of the tooth structure. To cope up with the above drawbacks, the concept of cavity disinfection has been introduced by some authors, which involves cleansing of the cavity with antimicrobial agents prior to placement of restoration. Multiple disinfectants(CHX,NaOCl,Laser,Ozone,Propolis etc.) have been used in clinical dentistry, to reduce or eliminate bacterial load and sterilize dentin during cavity preparation. Chlorhexidine digluconate in the form of 2% aqueous solution has been widely considered as a biocompatible,effective and toxicologically safe disinfectant. Chitosan, derived from the deacetylation of chitin, obtained from the shells of marine crustaceans is a natural nontoxic, biocompatible, biodegradable polysaccharide with tested antibacterial properties. Prior studies have described the antimicrobial potential of chitin, chitosan, and their derivatives against Streptococcus mutans and other streptococci bacteria. Among these derivatives, phosphorylated chitosan(p-chitosan) exhibits bactericidal, bioabsorbable, osteoinductive, and metal chelating properties. Since phosphate groups of p-chitosan can bind calcium ions to form nucleating sites, p-chitosan would induce the formation of a calcium phosphate layer favouring remineralization of the carious lesion. The aim of the present study is to evaluate the efficacy of p-chitosan as a potential cavity disinfectant which can decrease the bacterial load in the cavity and asses using fluorescence imaging and also compare the results with that of conventional 2%chlorhexidine disinfectant in retention and longevity of restorations. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Discussion of the Study Design i. Choice of Dose: The dose of Pertuzumab 420 mg concentrate for solution for infusion is chosen to achieve sufficient serum levels to characterize the pharmacokinetic profile of the drug. ii. Duration of sampling: Sampling duration of 2016.00 hours is considered sufficient for adequate pharmacokinetic profiling of analyte. iii. Design; Parallel design has been selected due to long half-life and pharmacokinetic study. iv. Study Condition: The present study will be conducted under fasting condition based on the EMA guideline (GUIDELINE ON THE INVESTIGATION OF BIOEQUIVALENCE), In general, a bioequivalence study should be conducted under fasting conditions as this is considered to be the most sensitive condition to detect a potential difference between formulations. v. Choice of volunteers: The healthy adult volunteers will consititute the study population. The choice and suitability of this population is discussed below. This selection of healthy volunteers is regarded as adequate in most instances to allow extrapolation of the results to populations. Opting for healthy subjects is in accordance with EMA guideline and previous similar studies. As it is stated in the EMA guideline, GUIDELINE ON THE INVESTIGATION OF BIOEQUIVALENCE: â€œthe subject population for bioequivalence studies should be selected with the aim of permitting detection of differences between pharmaceutical products. In order to reduce variability not related to differences between products, the studies should normally be performed in healthy volunteers unless the drug carries safety concerns that make this unethical. This model, in vivo healthy volunteers, is regarded as adequate in most instances to detect formulation differences and to allow extrapolation of the results to populations for which the reference medicinal product is approved. column51: Auditory hallucination is one of the most prevalent and devastating features of schizophrenia among various symptoms. For 25%â€“30% of schizophrenia patients, such hallucinations are refractory to drug treatment, resulting in persistent distress, functional disability, and frequent loss of behavioral control. System models suggest that abnormal levels of regional cerebral excitation and inhibition may occur. Gamma-frequency band neural activity (30â€“50 Hz or broader, centered on 40 Hz) has been hypothesized to reflect the synchronization of neural assemblies involved in binding or integration of various features of an object within a single sensory modality, across modalities, and across time. Failure or abnormality in gamma synchronization could result in a variety of perceptual and cognitive abnormalities, including abnormal perceptions, aberrant semantic association, hallucinations, and discontinuities in thinking, that occur in schizophrenia. There is a good deal of evidence implicating the language-related areas of the left cerebral hemisphere in auditory hallucinations in schizophrenia. In particular, patients with schizophrenia exhibit reduced neural oscillations involved in sensory and cognitive processing. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is a non-invasive brain stimulation modality that applies oscillating electrical currents to the brain via scalp electrodes. tACS applied in the EEG range is believed to mainly entrain with or synchronize neuronal networks, thus inducing changes in ongoing oscillatory brain activity. Indeed, spike synchrony of converging input has been shown to enhance information transfer and speed up processing. It could be that the modification of the synapse once exposed to a rapidly alternating electrical field, alters the associated biochemical mechanisms, such as the accumulation of calcium in the presynaptic nerve terminals leading to synaptic plasticity effects. The advantage of tACS, unlike other types of Non-invasive brain stimulation techniques, is that it enables manipulation and entrainment of intrinsic oscillations through the injection of sinusoidal currents. Yet, it has remained unknown if tACS, and in the particular repeated application of tACS, can alter or modulate networks in disorders associated with dysfunction of neural oscillations. Auditory hallucinations are considered the consequence of aberrant hyperactivity in the left temporo-parietal junction (TPJ). Moreover, patients with schizophrenia exhibit abnormal gamma neural oscillations. Therefore, this study using gamma tACS to target and modulate reduced neural oscillations may serve both as a tool to investigate the causal relationship between oscillation abnormalities and symptom manifestations and, ultimately, as a therapeutic intervention to treat auditory hallucinations in schizophrenia by restoring physiological oscillation dynamics. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Schizophrenia is a debilitating psychiatric condition that affects almost 1% of the global population. It is perplexing that the functional disability of schizophrenia has changed little over the last century, despite availability of drugs that reduce psychotic symptoms. Deficits in perception, non-social cognition and social cognition are additional characteristics of schizophrenia. Social cognition comprises the mental operations like empathy that underpin social interactions. Individuals with schizophrenia frequently exhibit dysfunctional empathy. The mirror neurons act as the neural basis of empathy which has been explored via EEG desynchronisation. column51: INTRODUCTION Free Gingival Graft (FGG) procedure is one of the surgical procedures used to create a wide zone of attached gingiva around the teeth and implants. As part of this procedure, a graft is harvested usually from palatal mucosa. The donor site heals by secondary intention, during which, post-operative complications like pain, discomfort and delayed wound healing are common.2 Donor site morbidity has been a concern and limiting factor for surgeons in such cases. To reduce the post operative discomfort at donor site and promote wound healing, various materials like, platelet rich fibrin, gelatine foam, cyanoacrylate have been used over the years, with not much definitive benefit.1 Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a high molecular weight, non-sulphated polysaccharide component of the family glycosaminoglycans. HA is present in various body fluids such as synovial fluid, serum, gingival crevicular fluid and saliva. Most cells of the body like fibroblasts, chondrocytes synthesize which is highly biocompatible and non-immunogenic. It has bacteriostatic, fungistatic, anti -inflammatory and proangiogenic properties which may lead to promotion of wound healing.3,4 HA is an essential component of the periodontal ligament matrix and plays various important roles in cell adhesion, migration and differentiation mediated by the various HA binding proteins and cell-surface receptors such as CD44. HA has been studied as a metabolite or diagnostic marker of inflammation in the gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) as well as a significant factor in growth, development and repair of tissues.3 In periodontology HA has been studied for its use as monotherapy or as an adjunct to non-surgical and surgical periodontal treatment to reduce inflammation. These known properties of HA may be utilized to reduce discomfort and promote healing at the donor site in situations where a free graft is harvested. This may be utilized in cases where there is a large intraoral open wound. Hence this study intends to assess effects of HA on palatal donor site.6 REVIEW OF LITERATURE Farnoush A (1978) in his review article discussed the rationale for the application of postsurgical dressings and suggested that a surgical dressing can provide patient comfort and protect the palatal wound from further injury during the early wound healing.1 Weigel PH, Frost SJ, Robert D. LeBoeuf, McGary CT (2007) proposed a model for the role of HA and fibrin during the early events of the inflammatory response and wound healing and concluded that the size of the HA has a direct relationship with how strongly it interacts with fibrin. He also opined that this molecular interaction may be important to human physiology, especially in the process of wound healing. The amount of HA present reduces the lag time and speeds up the formation and polymerization of thrombin-catalyzed fibrin. This effect of HA may also aid in the formation of blood clots following injury. Exposed HA in the wound margins may hasten clotting and aid in securing the expanding clot to the adjacent tissue.2 Dahiya P, Kamal R (2013) reviewed one hundred and eleven articles related to role of HA in periodontology and concluded that Hyaluronan has a multifunctional role in the wound healing process with a similar mechanism of healing potentially existing within periodontal tissues. column51: RATIONALE: Surgical site infections are complications associated with caesarean delivery which may lead to a substantial effect on the motherâ€™s health. column51: Schizophrenia is one of the most common psychiatric diseases affecting 0.7% of the world population (Saha S et al., 2005). Impairments of cognitive functions, including neurocognition, social cognition, and metacognition, may be present before the onset of psychosis, become pronounced in the first episode, and continue throughout the entire course of the illness(Yamada Y et al., 2019). Impairment in social functioning has been extensively documented in schizophrenia and is recognized as one of the hallmarks of the disorder (Brunet-Gouet and Decety, 2006; Thakkar et al.,2014). Over the last decade, considerable research has focused on social cognition, which is the ability to construct mental representations about others, oneself, and relations between others and oneself (Adolphs, 2001). Current consensus is to categorise social cognition in schizophrenia research into 5 distinct but overlapping constructs. These include theory of mind, social perception, social knowledge, attributional bias and emotional processing(Green et al., 2008). Theory of mind is the ability to infer intentions, dispositions and beliefs of others. Social perception is the ability to make inference about complex social situations such as social roles, societal rules and social context. Knowledge regarding the roles, rules and goals that characterize social situations which guide social interactions forms social knowledge which is the third construct. Attribution style or attribution bias is the way one makes inferences about causes of social events. Emotion processing is the cognitive ability to identify, perceive and manage emotions(Green et al., 2008). Social cognition is thought to facilitate social interactions and is considered a determinant of social dysfunction among people with schizophrenia (Fett et al.,2011; Green et al., 2012). Disturbances of social cognition, including ToM, have been shown to worsen the ability to perform well in occupation and interpersonal relationships in patients with schizophrenia(Couture et al., 2006; Penn et al., 2008; Brekke et al., 2005) To overcome social cognitive disturbances of schizophrenia, psychosocial (e.g., cognitive rehabilitation) (Nijman SA, 2020) and pharmacological (e.g., second-generation antipsychotic drugs) (Hill SK et al., 2010) approaches have been attempted with limited success. As an alternative approach, some types of neuromodulations, particularly non- invasive brain stimulation, e.g., transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), have been drawing attention (Yamada Y et al, 2021). tDCS modulates neural activities in the brain by delivering low-amplitude (usually no more than 2 mA) electrical currents over a short period (generally no more than 30 min) between electrodes, i.e., anode and cathode (Yamada Y et al., 2021). Transcranial direct current stimulation uses two scalp electrodes to induce low- amplitude direct currents strong enough to penetrate the brain and modify membrane potentials, thereby influencing neuronal excitability, but without triggering the depolarization of neurons (Wagner et al, 2007). It is speculated that tDCS may partially alleviate social cognition impairments that are resistant to antipsychotic drugs (Haime Z et al., 2021). Furthermore, as tDCS provides electrical currents via the skull, surface areas of the brain, such as STS, provide a feasible target for anodal stimulation(Sasamoto A et al., 2011). The neural network for social cognition may include the orbitofrontal cortex, medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), superior temporal sulcus (STS),and amygdala; functional connectivity of these brain regions is attenuated in schizophrenia (Yamada Y et al., 2021; Frith et al., 2007; Yamada Y et al., 2020). Accordingly, impaired connectivity between these brain regions is associated with poor social cognitive functioning (Brothers L et al., 1990; Pinkham et al.,2003). Among these brain regions, the STS is considered to play a pivotal role in multiple domains of social cognition. Oxytocin is a nonapeptide hormone produced in the brain that has been implicated in social behavior (Churchland and Winkielman, 2012). There is cumulating evidence for an important modulatory effect of oxytocin in the context of social stress, social anxiety, social cognition, and psychosis. The mechanism by which human prosocial behavior is altered by oxytocin, however, is not known. Three important hypotheses have been put forth. First, oxytocin may directly facilitate prosocial and approach behavior through its coupling with dopaminergic neural pathways mediating reward and reinforcement in the brain (Groppe et al. 2013; Riem et al. 2012; Ross et al. 2009). Second, the influence of oxytocin on social behavior may occur by attenuating defensive behaviors and stress reactivity, which would then facilitate approach and prosocial behavior (Cardoso et al. 2013;Ellenbogen et al. 2014; Kirsch et al. 2005). Third, oxytocin may influence social behavior by altering the processing of social information in the environment, perhaps by increasing the salience of social stimuli (Bartz et al. 2011b; Guastella and MacLeod 2012; Shamay-Tsoory and Abu-Akel 2016). column51: The aim of the present study is to examine the effect of transcranial direct current stimulation on ADHD. Children and Adolescent diagnosed as Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in the Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (CAP) clinic of the Department of Psychiatry, AIIMS, New Delhi will be included in this study. Diagnosis will be confirmed by a qualified psychiatrist by a thorough clinical evaluation. A total of 126 participants will be included using computer generated random numbers. The participants will be randomized into two groups, one group will receive active tDCS intervention and other group will receive sham tDCS therapy. Both the groups will receive the treatment as usual (TAU) from their primary treating team. The treating team and the rater will be blinded about the nature of the intervention. The children and adolescents referred or brought to child and adolescent psychiatry clinic of psychiatry OPD, AIIMS will be screened as per inclusion and exclusion criteria. column51: Headache is number six leading cause of disability across the world. So is a major public health problem. Treatment of headache is mainly focused on medicinal symptom management. A problem with medicinal headache management is the risk of serious harms including medication overuse headache, gastrointestinal bleeding (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs), liver damage (acetaminophen), addiction (opioids), memory impairment, depression (topiramate), weight gain, and precipitation of cardiac arrhythmias and seizures (amitriptyline). In the view of these concerns, safe, effective nonpharmacological treatments focusing on the cause of headache are needed. One approach could be to target chronic stress, which plays a major role in the development, maintenance, and chronification of headache. Stress reduction might be an important treatment strategy for headache. An important non-pharmacological treatment approach that has been shown to effectively reduce chronic pain stress and several other headache risk factors such as psychiatric conditions and obesity is yoga. Despite its potential benefits and popularity among distressed people, the effectiveness of yoga in relieving tension type headache has been addressed only in a few randomized controlled trials which are of poor methodological quality. The quality of evidence generated is downgraded to very low. Further high-quality trials are needed before concrete recommendations for yoga in headache can be made. So, we plan this study with high quality and better methodology with the aim to assess the effectiveness of yoga as a supportive treatment in patients with tension headache. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Understanding the perspectives of children and adolescents regarding addictive behaviours is critical in formulating appropriately tailored interventions. The dramatic expansion and easy accessibility of digital technology have resulted in exposure/use starting at an early age, perhaps contributing to increasing prevalence of addictive behaviours. Addictive behaviours negatively impact academic performance, mental health, and sleep quality. The pharmacological and psychotherapeutic treatments of addictions and of the craving in particular, have shown their limits which indicates the need for new treatment possibilities. Both substance use disorders and addictive behaviours have been shown to have problems with executive functions, including working memory and decision-making processes. Studies have shown that applying tDCS on prefrontal areas modifies the decision process in healthy subjects and also in addictive behaviours. Anodal tDCS over the DLPFC may improve executive functions and cognitive control, lowering the risk of drug relapse. It may also indirectly regulate dopaminergic pathways, which can have an impact on the signs and symptoms of addiction. Non-invasive methods of neuromodulation provide a safe, cost-effective and robust means to enhance PFC function. Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation has advantage over other techniques of non-invasive brain stimulation such as cost effectiveness, small size of the apparatus, allowing portability, possibility of modulating neuronal activity. Promising results have been obtained on the neuromodulation based effects of tDCS on prefrontal areas in modifying the decision process in addicted subjects which could further decrease impulsive behaviours observed in addictions. tDCS is found effective in reducing craving in addictive behaviours in controlled studies comparing stimulation vs. placebo. HD-tDCS, a technically enhanced version of tDCS gives a more focal stimulation and has better predictive stimulation output. HD-tDCS over the left DLPFC can have potential clinical applications because a deficit in inhibition control underlies most types of addictions. To the best of our knowledge, there has been no study assessing the effects of HD-tDCS on executive functions, decision making & impulsivity as measured by fMRI in young onset addictive behaviours. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Cognitive impairments have long been accepted as core features of schizophrenia that contribute significantly to disability and are generally treatment refractory. Numerous neuropsychological studies demonstrate a broad range of measurable cognitive deficits in Schizophrenia including impairments in attention, working memory (WM), episodic memory, processing speed and executive functions. Despite the enormous importance of cognitive symptoms, there are still no satisfying treatment options in clinical practice. Noninvasive brain stimulation (NIBS) techniques have been proposed as new treatment options for cognitive deficits. The term NIBS summarizes various techniques, including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and its variants. Hence, attempts have been taken to design specific strategies that improve the cognitive deficits. Most of the studies of cognition has been done on dLPFC for cognition. At present, repetitive intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) is a more novel form of rTMS. iTBS is a new form of NIBS, that is characterized by the delivery of 600 pulses within 3 minutes. It produces an increase in motor cortex excitability in a short time, and its excitatory effect may be superior to that of rTMS. Stimulating the dmPFC may increase the integration of information that would otherwise be processed in parallel to those important for self relevant processes. This embedding of information pertaining to the other could potentially explain how humans are able to represent the perspective of others and attribute observable behaviour to unobservable mental attributes. Based on an extensive review, Van Overwalle (2011) concluded that the mPFC is preferentially engaged in social cognition. Studies on rTMS on dmPFC for cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia are lacking. There is however one study been done on dmPFC stimulation on social cognition (Razafimandimby, A et al.,2016). column51: Many patients with bipolar disorder, fail to experience benefit even after adequate pharmacotherapy (Geddes and Miklowitz,2013). For the patients who do respond to pharmacotherapy, many experience frequent and intolerable side effects leading to medication non-adherence or discontinuation (Matson et al,2006; Shah et al.,2017) or suffer from an increased medical burden along with added problems of interactions among medications for co-morbid illnesses (Kemp et al,2014; Martin et al.,2005). Therefore, the limitations of pharmacotherapy suggest the importance of alternative treatment options that will help patients with bipolar disorder achieve and sustain remission (Martin et al,2005). There have been few studies on neuromodulation in mania. TMS studies in mania are few and mainly include traditional protocols targeting the right prefrontal region, stemming from an early clinical trial by Grisaru et al.,1998. Another study by Kaptsan et al.,2003 along similar lines to the previous study reported no difference between right-sided and sham TMS, proposing more intensive protocol for mania. To date, only one randomized study has suggested the potential benefit of a rTMS protocol over the right DLPFC for mania (Praharaj et al.,2009). column51: Niqris originated from the Greek word â€œAnquroosâ€ which means big toe (the first metatarsophalangeal joint). This is the classical site for the beginning of this disease, hence the disease got this name. Renowned Unani scholars Ibn-e-Sina, Majoosi, Jurjani, Antaki described that Madda-e-Niqrisiya (Morbid matter) accumulated in intra-articular space especially in big toe cause pain and inflammation. In modern system of medicine this disease is called â€˜GOUTâ€™. Gout is common inflammatory condition of joint. It is caused by deposition of monosodium urate crystals within the joints after chronic hyperuricemia. Prevalence of hyperuricemia varies according to the age, sex, race, geographical conditions and association with other diseases. It becomes common with increasing age: it is <0.5% in men under the age of 35 years and >7% in those aged over 75 years. It is rare in premenopausal women and increases to 2.5%-3.5% in those aged 75 years of age. Irsal-e-Alaq is an ancient regimen of Ilaj-bit-Tadbeer used for diversion and evacuation of Akhlat-e-Fasida (morbid matter) by application of Leech on the affected parts of the body surface. Blood letting in the form of leech therapy has been utilised for preventive as well as curative measures for thousands of years by ancient Unani scholars. Habb-e-Suranjan is the most common Unani medicine that is used in joints pain. It has anti inflammatory and analgesic actions. In Conventional system of medicine there is no permanent cure for Gout, only symptomatic treatment is available with analgesics and NSAIDs like Indomethacin and Urate lowering drugs like Allopurinol, Probenecid, Febuxostat etc.These drugs have many side effects. In Unani System of Medicine many single/ compound drugs like Zanjabeel, Muqil, Darchini, Majoon Chobchini, Habb-e-Suranjan, Habb-e-Asgand etc with regimenal procedures like Hijamah-bish-Shurt (wet cupping), Irsal-e-Alaq etc. are prescribed to treat gout with minimal/no side effects. Leech saliva has several bioactive substances that are anti-inflammatory, anticoagulant, vasodilator, anaesthetic etc. Leech therapy has no adverse effect in comparison to conventional medicine. column51: Postnatal growth failure, in very preterm neonates is one of the great concern as it is associated with long lasting adverse neurodevelopmental outcome. Suboptimal early parenteral and enteral nutrition received by Extremely Low Birth weight (ELBW) infants results in substantial protein and energy deficits that persist for weeks causing postnatal growth restriction and are associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcome. The study aims to evaluate the neurodevelopmental outcome at 1year of age in preterm babies (28-32weeks) receiving large volume vs standard volume feed during NICU stay. The primary outcome is survival without moderate or severe neurodevelopmental disability at 12 months of age, corrected for gestational age at birth. All preterm infants admitted and discharged from KEM hospital from May2023- May 2024 are included into the study. column51: RATIONALE- The success rate of intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovulation induction in patients is turning out to be low. One of the identifiable reasons for low success rate of IUI is low endometrial receptivity. One of the methods to improve endometrial receptivity is platelet rich plasma (PRP). Platelets are considered reservoir of cytokines, chemokines and growth factors. After intrauterine infusion, PRP increases vascularization of endometrium, blood supply to intervillous part of placenta and, thus, implantation rates. AIM: To study the effect of autologous intrauterine Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) therapy on endometrial receptivity and clinical pregnancy rate in unexplained infertility. OBJECTIVES Primary objectives: a) To assess the effect of platelet rich plasma therapy in unexplained infertility with previously failed IUI in form of clinical pregnancy rate. b) To assess change in endometrial receptivity parameters with PRP therapy in current cycle and without PRP therapy in failed IUI cycle. Secondary objectives: a) To compare the luteal phase serum EGF (Epidermal Growth Factor) level with and without PRP therapy. b) To study the association of endometrial receptivity with clinical pregnancy rate. c) To assess the side effects of intrauterine PRP therapy in the study, if any. PLACE OF STUDY: The study will be carried out in the Department of Obstetrics and gynecology, Department of Biochemistry and Radiodiagnosis at UCMS and GTBH, Delhi. STUDY DESIGN: Nested interventional comparative study DURATION OF STUDY: May 2023 â€“ November 2024 SAMPLE SIZE CALCULATION Since the pregnancy rate is around 34.8% in PRP group of IUI by Abaid et al1 done in 2019, with absolute precision of 7% and 95% confidence interval, the sample size comes out to be 178 cases for our study. As per the endometrial receptivity parameter done by Zhang et al2, the sample size comes out to be 155 cases in each group by taking Î± =5%, power =80% by taking receptivity score as 4.60Â± 1.55 and 4.11Â±1.53 in pregnant and non pregnant respectively. As per available hospital data, convenient sample size of 130 cases of unexplained infertility will be taken. RECRUITEMENT CRITERIA Diagnosed cases of unexplained infertility attending the infertility clinic of Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology who will be requiring IUI as a treatment modality will be recruited in the present study. INCLUSION CRITERIA: a) Diagnosed case of Unexplained infertility (documented ovulation, at least unilateral tubal patency, normal uterine cavity and normal semen analysis). b) Age: 21 -34yr c) BMI: 19-25 Kg/m2 EXCLUSION CRITERIA a) Patient on any hormonal therapy or NSAID b) Female with the diagnosis of hematological disorder and autoimmune disorder. c) Females with chronic medical disorder such as diabetes, hypertension and tuberculosis. d) Presence of active infection such Pelvic inflammatory diseases, vaginal or cervical infection METHODOLOGY Couples diagnosed with unexplained infertility will be considered in the study. The couple will undergo IUI without PRP therapy as per institutional protocol in the first cycle. IUI will be performed in all the patients after controlled ovarian stimulation with Inj Gonadotropin as per standard protocol. Transvaginal scan for endometrial receptivity score will be done on the day of hCG, after 2 days of IUI and after 4 days of IUI. After 4 days of IUI, 2 ml blood sample of patient will be withdrawn for serum EGF levels estimation. The couple who conceived after IUI will be excluded from the study. Those couples who will not conceive after IUI will be considered as failed IUI in the study. These couples will be enrolled as CONTROLS. These couples will be considered for another cycle of IUI with PRP therapy and will be enrolled as CASES in the consecutive cycle. In the second cycle of IUI, all the couples will undergo IUI with PRP therapy. All the steps of IUI in the first cycle will be followed in exactly the same way except 0.5-1 ml of intrauterine instillation of autologous PRP by IUI cannula will be done after 2 days of IUI. 13.5 ml of blood sample will be collected to make PRP using two steps centrifugation method on the same day of instillation. At the end of the study, 30 samples from each group will be randomly chosen for S.EGF levels assessment. column51: Rationale/gaps in existing knowledge As per WHO guidelines exclusive breastfeeding to be given till 6 months followed by initiation of complementary feeding (CF) alongwith breastfeeding till at least 2 years. In preterm neonates there are no guidelines when to start CF, whether by chronological age or corrected age. Hence this needs exploration to decide the best time to initiate CF in preterm neonates. Novelty RCTs looking at initiation of CF in preterm infants are scanty . The big debate remains whether to use chronological age vs corrected age to initiate CF feeding as starting too early (as per chronological age) may deprive the adequate nutrition in preterm neonates and may be developmentally immature. On the other hand, starting as per corrected age may be too late leading to poor growth and neurodevelopment. This study will at look various outcomes alongwith preparedness for accepting semisolids according to their chronological and corrected age and other outcomes . Objectives To study the growth , neurodevelopment , hematological and biochemical parameters in preterm neonates when CF is initiated at chronological age 6 months vs corrected age of 6 months. Methods Neonates < 35 weeks of gestation, randomized in 2 groups, early CF ( at chronological age of 6 months) vs late CF ( at corrected age of 6 months ) if neurologically normal and weight of 4.5 kg. column51: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is a chronic relapsing condition. Opioid agonist treatment, particularly Buprenorphine maintenance treatment (BMT), provides effective withdrawal management and increased treatment retention and abstinent days. Chronic use of mu-opioid receptor agonists is known to lower the pain threshold, presenting as pain complaints persisting beyond the withdrawal phase. Nearly 30% of BMT patients report muscular pain in lower limbs and paraspinal regions. Various neurobiologicalmechanisms have been proposed for pain. However, evidence-based intervention for the effective management of pain is still minimal. Most patients self-medicate with over-the-counter opioid agonists or NSAIDs while on BMT. Hence, there is a need to explore more novel neurobiologically-informed treatments. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is one of the most widely studied, non-invasive neuromodulatory procedures. Existing literature has shown that application of anodal tDCSover the primary motor cortex (PMC) may be effective in alleviating pain in chronic pain syndromes. This study aims to find out the feasibility and acceptability of anodal Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation and its anti-nociceptiveeffects in patients on BMT for OUD. In this study, 30 participants will be recruited and randomlyallocated into two arms. The first arm will receive anodal tDCS over the left PMC (M1).The second arm will receive sham tDCS on the same region. A total of ten sessions will be given over a period ofseven days. There will be 2 sessions a day that will be separated by a period of 3 hours. The patientâ€˜s pain symptom will be assessed during the procedure on a Brief Pain Inventory(BPI) scale. The primaryoutcome is the feasibility and acceptability of tDCS amongst OUD. The secondary outcome is pain, which will be assessed before, after the completion of 10 treatment sessions and 1 month after the treatment course on the BPI scale. Motor cortical excitability measures will be assessed using the TMS-EMG procedure to examine the correlation between their changes and the reduction in pain scores. column51: Hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is one of the major causes of neonatal mortality, morbidity and long term neurodevelopmental sequelae. Therapeutic hypothermia (TH) is likely to decrease death or severe disability and cerebral palsy at 18-24 months even in low middle income countries as compared to high income countries. Recent studies have shown that early enteral feeding in babies receiving TH does not increase risk of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and have better outcomes than withholding feeds. Rapid advancement of EEN in other high risk infants like preterms (not on TH) have shown beneficial outcomes on anthropometry, neuromotor and immune development. However there are no studies comparing slow vs rapid advancement of EEN in these neonates. Hence, we aim to do this novel RCT to compare rapid versus slow advancement of EEN in neonates with perinatal asphyxia on TH. The primary outcome will be to assess composite outcome of NEC â‰¥ stage 2 and or mortality in term infants with HIE on TH. The secondary outcomes include time to reach full feeds , length of NICU stay, incidence of feed intolerance and sepsis . The study will be conducted in NICU of KEM hospital after approval from institutional ethics committee for 2 years. Infants will be enrolled within 6 hours of life, considering that TH has to be initiated within first 6 hours of life. All babies with moderate to severe HIE requiring TH will be included in study. Given the fact that incidence of NEC or mortality in infants on TH is <3%, the sample size required to bring change by 1% will require a sample size of >7000 infants with power of 80% and alpha error of 0.05. Hence, we will do a pilot trial of the same in 40 infants (20 in each arm). Written informed consent will be taken from the parent following which infant will be enrolled. Computer based stratified randomization will be done by a statistician not included in study. Sequentially numbered opaque white sealed envelopes will be used for allocation concealment. The principal investigator, treating doctors and the statistician will be blinded. In rapid advancement group ,feed advancement will be done @ 30ml/kg/day for 3 days and then to full enteral feeds on day 4 vs feed advancement at @ 15ml/Kg/day for 3 days followed by advancement to full feeds @30ml/Kg/day in slow advancement group. column51: Dental plaque is a biofilm containing coaggregation of pathogenic microorganisms & is considered a major causative factor for the initiation of gingivitis and periodontitis resulting in loss of the tooth (1). Gingivitis is an inflammatory condition of the gingival tissue, most commonly caused by bacterial infection. Unlike periodontitis, there is no attachment loss and therefore no migration of the junctional epithelium (2). The condition is restricted to the soft-tissue area of the gingival epithelium and connective tissue. Among all the periodontal diseases, gingivitis is considered to be the commonest. There are various forms of gingivitis based on clinical appearance, duration of infection, severity, and etiology. However, the chronic form of gingivitis that is caused by plaque is considered to be the most frequent variant (3) Clinically, the gingival tissues are characterized by swelling, redness, tenderness, a shiny surface, and bleeding upon gentle probing. Gingivitis seldom generates spontaneous bleeding and is commonly painless, therefore many patients do not recognize the disease and fail to seek attention Antimicrobials have been researched to combat the pathogenicity of microbial plaque and thereby gingival infections, but they are tarnished with adverse effects, inefficiency & toxicity (4). This mandates the discovery of antimicrobial agents which are non-toxic, efficient & patient friendly. Antimicrobials have been delivered in the form of mouthwashes, gels, etc. These are not thoroughly acceptable to patients. Calendula officinalis has demonstrated antimicrobial & antioxidant properties and is herbal in nature with no toxicity. However, this herbal product has not been assessed for its antimicrobial property against dental plaque pathogens causing gingivitis. Hence this study is designed to assess the anti-microbial efficacy of Calendula officinalis incorporated in an oral dispersible film on oral pathogens causing gingivitis. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: INTRODUCTION According to the World Health Organisation, incidence of infertility is about 10% worldwide. According to a recent report globally, 48.5 million couples are affected by infertility. This report states that that nearly every 7th couple is infertile[1]. In India, the prevalence of primary infertility has been reported to be in the range of 3.9 to 16.8%[2]. The term infertility is used when â€œa couple fails to conceive after one year of regular sexual activity without contraceptionâ€. WHO defines this condition in following words, â€œa disease of the reproductive system defined by the failure to achieve a clinical pregnancy after 12 months or more of regular unprotected sexual intercourseâ€[3]. Eighty per cent of all women desiring children, conceive within 1 year of married life while another 10% within the second year. Another 10-12% of all the other couples have only one child and wish to have more[4]. The reasons for infertility could be multiple. Both males as well as females could be responsible for it. Identifiable factors affecting female infertility include: â€œhormonal or endocrine disturbances (menstruation or ovulation problems), tubal pathologies (occlusions, pelvic adhesions and other tubal abnormalities), non-tubal pathologies (cervical or uterine disturbances), sexual dysfunction and congenital abnormalitiesâ€[5].Among different causes of infertility, male factor besides being to sole cause of infertility in 20% of infertile couples may be contributing factor in as many as 40% of cases. Female factor contributes about 40% of the cases. Disorders of ovulation such as an ovulation account for about 20% to 40% of all cases of female infertility. Tubal factor such as tubal injury, blockage, or paratubal adhesions account for 30-40% of cases of female infertility. Cervical factor is estimated to be a cause of infertility in no more than 5% of infertile couples. Other factors include â€œdecreased ovarian reserve, peritoneal factors, uterine factors, immunologic factors, systemic conditions (including infections or chronic diseases such as autoimmune conditions or renal failure), and unexplained factors (including endometriosis with no evidence of tubal or peritoneal adhesions)â€. Over the last few decades, in vitro fertilization (IVF) has gained immense popularity and has emerged as a ray of hope for the infertile couples. Today, in developed countries like the USA and Europe, IVF is responsible for 1.6% and 4.5% of total live births respectively[6]. However, even in vitro fertilization is not always successful. Almost 20 to 25% of suitable women fail to respond to IVF even after five cycles despite significant improvements in its success rate over the last decade[7]. Among various factors associated with a failed implantation, endometrium plays an important role. Endometrial thickness is one of the contributory factors in determining the successful implantation and pregnancy[8],[9]. A number of studies report endometrial thickness >7 mm as the optimum for successful embryo transfer10,[10],[11]. From the point of view of IVF, thin endometrium is defined as <7 mm on the day of ovulation, or on the day of human chorionic gonadotrophin (HCG) injection in fresh in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles, or the day to start progesterone in frozen-thaw embryo transfer cycles[12],[13]. Therapies for thin endometrium include â€œlong-term administration of estrogen, low-dose of aspirin, vitamin E supplement, vaginal sildenafil citrate application, electroacupuncture and transvaginal endometrial perfusion of granulocyte colony stimulating factor (G-CSF)â€. Despite existence of so many treatment alternatives, a large proportion of women do not show response to these treatments. Thus, there is a need for other options for patients with thin endometrium13,[14],[15]. Estradiol valerate is one of the commonly used and established modalities for management of thin endometrium during IVF[16]. During the recent years, regenerative medicine has emerged as a process of replacing, engineering or regenerating human cells, tissues or organs to restore or establish the normal function. This process is done through stem cell isolates, recombinant growth factor amplification and platelets augmentation, respectively[17],[18]. In recent years, a preparation called Platelet rich plasma (PRP) is emerging as a platelet augmentation technique. PRP is characterized by its natural autologous nature that has been shown to have a large potential in ensuring tissue regeneration. The growth stimulus of PRP comes from the alfa granules found in platelet that speed up the tissue recovery by acting as catalyst to the natural healing and tissue repair processes. They also induce the production of new collagen by â€œthe fibroblasts, osteoblasts and chondrocytes as per need of the parent tissueâ€. The scope of PRP use has been described in a host of medical fields like orthopedics, cosmetology, reconstructive surgery, dentistry, orthopedic surgery and sports medicine by harnessing the inherent property of platelets by facilitating secretion of various growth factors. PRP has also gained popularity as an alternative option for treatment of thin endometrium[19],[20]. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) derived from fresh whole blood and has anti-inflammatory and pro-regenerative functions. After the activation of the platelets in PRP, â€œgrowth factors as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), transforming growth factor (TGF), platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) and epidermal growth factor (EGF) are actively secreted and transformed into their bioactive forms within 10 minutes after clotting. These growth factors are known to regulate cell functions such as attachment, migration, proliferation, differentiation and promote extracellular matrix accumulation. Therefore, PRP has been widely used for various therapeutic areas, for example, promoting healing process in orthopedics, ophthalmology and healing therapiesâ€[21],[22],[23]. Given the encouraging role of PRP in management of thin endometrium as evidenced in some of the recent studies, the present study is being planned to study the role of PRP (Platelet Rich Plasma) as compared to EV (Estradiol Valerate) in management of thin endometrium in patients with infertility using an open label randomized controlled trial. AIM AND OBJECTIVES AIM To study the role of PRP (Platelet Rich Plasma) as compared to EV (Estradiol Valerate) in management of thin endometrium in patients with infertility. OBJECTIVES 1. To study and compare the effect of PRP and EV on endometrial thickness among infertile women undergoing IUI. 2. To study and compare the effect of PRP and EV on successful implantation rates. 3. To study and compare the effect of PRP and EV on successful chemical and clinical pregnancy rates. 4. To study and compare the effect of PRP and EV in terms of adverse events like abortions. REVIEW OF LITERATURE Zadehmodarreset al. (2017)[24] in a pilot study that included 10 women with thin endometrium (ET<7 mm) undergoing assisted reproductive technology treatment used PRP for management of PRP. Before PRP injections, endometrial thickness ranged from 4 to 6 mm. After 48 hours of first PRP injection, endometrial thickness ranged from 5.2 to 6.8 mm. The patients were given a second PRP injection. After 48 hours of second PRP injection, endometrial thickness reached >7 mm in all the cases. Successful implantation was achieved in all the cases. Successful chemical pregnancy was achieved in 50%. Successful clinical pregnancy rate was 40%. The findings of the study showed a promising role of PRP in management of thin endometrium and subsequent favourable clinical outcomes. Eftekharet al. (2018)[25] in an RCT evaluated the effect of PRP injection on endometrial thickness and subsequently on successful implantation and clinical pregnancy rates as compared to controls. Mean increase in endometrial thickness within 48 hours of PRP injection was 2.58 mm as compared to 1.89 mm in the control group. Successful implantation was seen in 21% of PRP as compared to 9.37% of controls, thus showing a significant difference between the two groups. Per transfer and per cycle chemical, clinical and ongoing pregnancy rates were also higher in PRP as compared to the control group, but the difference between the two groups was found to be significant only for per cycle clinical pregnancy rates. No significant difference between the two groups was observed for abortion rates. Chang et al. (2019)[26]in their study that recruited 64 women with thin endometrium (<7 mm) undergoing frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles randomized them to two groups. In the case group (n=34) intrauterine infusion of autologous PRP was done on the 10th day and the day when progesterone was given in HRT cycle whereas women who did not receive PRP (n=30) were placed in control group. At the time of implantation, women receiving PRP had significantly thicker ET (7.65Â±0.22 mm) as compared to women in control group (6.52Â±0.31 mm). Cycle cancellation rate was also lower in PRP group (19.05%) as compared to that in control group (41.18%). The implantation and clinical pregnancy rates were also found to be significantly higher in PRP as compared to that in control group (27.94% vs 11.67% and 44.12% vs 20%, respectively). The findings of the study highlighted the role of PRP in â€œpromoting endometrium proliferation, improving embryo implantation rate and clinical pregnancy rate for women with thin endometrium in FET cyclesâ€. Kim et al. (2019)[27]in a prospective interventional study that included a total of 24 women who had a history of two or more failed IVF cycles. All thesewomen had refractory thin endometrium. They plannedintrauterine infusion of autologous PRP 2 or 3 times from menstrual cycle day 10 of their FET cycle as the intervention to manage thin ET.Assessment of ET was done 3 days after the final autologous PRP infusion. A total of 22 patients underwent FET. They found an average increase in ET to be 0.6 mm following PRP infusion. A total of 12.7% implantations were successful. Clinical pregnancy rate achieved was 30%. Ongoing pregnancy rate was 20% which was equal to live birth rate. There were 12 patients who showed an increase of ET by 1.3 mm following PRP infusion, however, they also noted a mean decline of 0.7 mm in ET of seven patients. There was one patient who did not show any change in ET following PRP infusion. No adverse effects were seen in any of the patients treated with autologous PRP. The authors found autologous PRP to be useful in restoring the endometrial receptivity of damaged endometrium in addition to increase in ET. Kusumiet al. (2020)[28]investigated the effectiveness of intrauterine administration of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) in frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycle in 36 women having endometrial thickness <7 mm. PRP was administrated on the 10thand 12thdays of the second HRT cycle. The authors observed a mean increase in endometrial thickness at day 14 was observed by 1.27 mm and 0.72 mm respectively on the basis of blinded and unblinded measurements. A total of 32 out of 36 (88.9%) women underwent FET. The authors noted a clinical pregnancy rate of 15.6%. No adverse event was encountered during the study. The authors found the PRP administration as an effective and safe procedure to increase the endometrial thickness and achieving clinical pregnancy. Zargeret al. (2021)[29]evaluated the effect of intra-uterine infusion of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) in frozen embryo transfer cycles on endometrial thickness and clinical pregnancy rates among a total of 24 women having thin endometrium (<7 mm). Before PRP administration, mean ET was 6.15Â±0.38 mm which became 7.49Â±0.61 mm after PRP administration, thus showing a mean increase of 1.34 mm. All the women except two women achieved ET >7 mm. They recorded clinical pregnancy rate of 45.8%. Ongoing pregnancy rate was 37.5%. There was no ectopic pregnancy. The authors found PRP to be an effective therapy in management of thin endometrium. Dogra et al. (2022)[30]reported a study in which a total of 20 women having endometrial thickness <7 mm undergoing IVF and FET cycles were subjected to intraueterine PRP administration. They received a total of 26 PRP cycles. Mean increase in endometrial thickness following first PRP administration was recorded as 1.07 and 0.83 mm respectively during fresh IVF and FET. PRP administration was helpful in increasing the endometrial thickness despite conditions like tuberculosis, low ovarian reserves and polycystic ovarian syndrome. Clinical pregnancy and live birth rates were 20% and 25% respectively. The authors did not note any adverse effect. On the basis of these findings, PRP was found to be a safe and effective measure to increase the endometrial thickness and improving clinical pregnancy rates. Desai et al. (2023)[31]in their study that included a total of 61 women aged between 22 and 40 years having endometrial thickness <7 mm even after receiving estradiol valerate therapy. There were 44 women having normal hysteroscopic findings while remaining 17 had abnormal hysteroscopic findings. In both the groups, prior to PRP administration, mean endometrial thickness was 6.49 and 6.00 mm respectively in the two groups. After 48 hours of PRP administration mean increase in endometrial thickness was 1.62 and 1.61 mm respectively and after 72 hours it was 2.42 mm and 3.28 mm respectively in the two groups. Clinical pregnancy rates were 50% and 52.9% respectively in women with normal and abnormal hysteroscopic findings. The implantation rate per embryo was 25.2% in normal and 26.8% in abnormal hysteroscopic groups. The findings of the study showed that PRP was helpful in increasing the endometrial thickness as well as in achieving good clinical pregnancy rates in women with or without hysteroscopic abnormalities. Informed consent will be obtained from all the patients. Method A total of 38 women falling in sampling frame will be enrolled in the study. At enrolment, sociodemographic details regarding age, place of residence (rural/urban), occupation, education, family income and type of housing will be noted. Medical history and exposure to risk factors like tobacco chewing, smoking, alcohol use will also be noted. Obstetric history, type of infertility, menstrual history and number of previous IVF attempts will also be enquired and noted. All the patients will be treated using the standard HRT protocol, the endometrial priming will be started on the day 2 to 3 of each patientâ€™s menstrual cycle. The patients will be then randomized into the following two groups: Group A (n=19; experimental group): Patients who will receive intrauterine infusion of autologous PRP on the 10th day of cycle in addition to routine estradiol valerate therapy. Group B (n=19; control group): Patients not receiving PRP and remaining on routine estradiol valerate therapy only. Method of Randomization: Sequentially Numbered Opaque Sealed Envelope (SNOSE) method. All the patients will receive estradiolvalerate orally administered with a start dose of 6â€Šmg/d. The dose of estradiolvalerate will be increased according to the endometrium responseupto a maximum dose of 12 mg/d. In the experimental group, PRP will be prepared from the peripheral blood drawn from the forearm. A total of 20 mL of blood will be collected in two 10 ml vacuum blood collection tubes. After centrifugation of blood at 2000g for a period of 6 minutes, a total of 1 mL of PRP will be obtained (0.5 mL from each tube). On day 10 of the cycle, the PRP collected by the above method will be infused into the uterine cavity using ET catheter under sonographic guidance. At day 10, sonographic measurement of endometrial thickness will be done in both the groups. The standard HRT protocol will continue unabatedly in both the groups. A repeat sonographic assessment for endometrial thickness will be done in both the groups 48 hours after the PRP infusion / first endometrial thickness assessment. Subsequently, â€œtwo good-quality blastocyst-stage embryos will be transferred to all patients. The criterion for embryo quality will be consulted from the embryo morphology assessment by the Istanbul consensus workshop, blastocysts scored as Grade 3 or 4 were considered as good-quality. After embryo transplantation, the luteal phase will be supported by daily intramuscular injection of 40â€Šmg progesterone, combined with 200â€Šmg vaginal progesterone soft capsules every night. Serum human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) level will be tested 14 days after embryo transfer. Vaginal ultrasonography will be performed 35 days after transfer in cases of a biochemical pregnancy, and a clinical pregnancy will be defined as the presence of an intrauterine fetalheart beat. Implantation rate will be determined by the number of gestational sacs over the total number of embryos transferredâ€. The process will be repeated upto a maximum of two cycles. The primary outcome measure for the study will be increase in endometrial thickness 48 hours after PRP administration. The secondary outcome measureswill be successful implantation, chemical and clinical pregnancy. Adverse events if any will also be noted. column32: Inclusion Criteria Screening Part I Participants must have histologically confirmed cervical adenocarcinoma, cervical squamous carcinoma, or cervical adenosquamous carcinoma and the following requirements: Participants must have histologically documented FIGO 2018 Stage IIIC to IVA cervical cancer (Appendix G); only participants with lymph node involvement will be included. Nodal involvement confirmation may be either histological eg, biopsy or by imaging PET CT, CT or MRI with pathological lymph node size defined by a short axis diameter of 10 mm axial plane. No evidence of metastatic disease M0. Screening Part II 1 Participants must have completed concurrent chemoradiotherapy as defined below: a. Completed within 1 to 56 days prior to randomization. b. Received weekly cisplatin 40 mg m2 for 5 to 6 cycles as concurrent chemotherapy with radiation therapy. If participants cannot tolerate toxicity, must have received at least 4 cycles of cisplatin. c. The last dose of cisplatin must be administered prior to, or concurrently with, the final dose of radiation. Consolidation chemotherapy after radiation is not permitted. d. Received EBRT and brachytherapy as part of the chemoradiation therapy, and brachytherapy can only be omitted if there is a medical contraindication. Prescription doses of radiotherapy are requested as below: i A total dose of 45 Gy for EBRT to the pelvis ii If brachytherapy is used, normal tissues should be limited with 2 cc rectal dose 75 Gy, sigmoid 2 cc dose 75 Gy, and 2 cc bladder dose 90 Gy. e.It is strongly preferred that participants complete CCRT within 8 weeks

column51: This is a split-mouth, double-blind, randomised controlled clinical trial for comparing the Platelet-Rich Fibrin Matrix (PRFM) and Coronally Advanced Flap (CAF) with and without Peripheral Blood Mesenchymal Stem Cells (PBMSCS) in the surgical management of gingival recession type â€“ 1 for the evaluation of the root coverage potential, regenerative effects, and the impact on gingival thickness.. The sites will be randomly assigned by computer-generated tabulation method into: 1. Test group: treated with CAF and PBMSCS + PRFM (SUPERCELL). 2. Control group: treated with CAF and PRFM alone. The period of study will be divided into a screening phase, a pre-treatment phase, a treatment phase, and a post-treatment phase. The subjects will be recruited after meeting the inclusion and exclusion criteria and obtaining the informed consent during the screening phase. In pre-treatment phase all patients will initially receive phase i therapy consisting of scaling, root planing, and oral hygiene instructions. Clinical parameters like Plaque Index (Pi): Silness And Loe, Gingival Index (Gi): Loe And Silness, Vertical Component Of The Gingival Recession, Horizontal Component Of The Gingival Recession, Probing Pocket Depth, Clinical Attachment Level, Width Of Attached Gingiva, Width Of Keratinized Gingiva, Gingival Thickness And Root Coverage Esthetic Score will be recorded at baseline, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year and 2 years. The treatment phase will involve withdrawal of blood for the procurement of PRFM and PBMSCs under aseptic conditions. This will be followed by obtaining optimum anaesthesia and reflection of a mucoperiosteal flap, followed by thorough debridement. Subsequently, the defect will be filled with PBMSCS + PRFM (SUPERCELL) in test sites and with PRFM in control sites. The surgical flaps which were elevated will be advanced coronally and sutured. A periodontal pack will be applied. All patients will be prescribed post-operative analgesics and antibiotics. In the post-treatment phase, recall examinations and maintenance therapy will be scheduled at 1 week, 3, and 6 months, 1 year and 2 years postoperatively. Clinical photographs will be recorded at various stages in the period of the study. column51: RATIONALE: Significant association has been observed between wound healing and human amniotic membrane in chronic non healing wounds, burn wounds, corneal ulcers, dry eye and many more. Autologous HAM patch is better than standard care for wound healing and reducing surgical site infections with no potential adverse events. So we plan to study autologous HAM patch dressing in primary caesarean wound healing. AIM: To study efficacy of autologous human amniotic membrane (HAM) patch dressing in primary caesarean wound healing. OBJECTIVES: Primary: To compare wound healing by REEDA (Redness, Edema, Ecchymosis, Discharge, Approximation) score on post-op day 3, day 8 and day 42 in HAM dressing group and non HAM dressing group. Secondary: 1. To compare the incidence of superficial and deep caesarean site infection in both the groups. 2. To determine adverse events like pain, swelling, discharge, dehiscence in both the groups. 3. To determine organisms associated with caesarean surgical site infection in both groups. 4. To compare length of hospital stay due to wound morbidity in both the groups. MATERIALS AND METHODS Study Design: Randomized controlled trial, A Pilot Study Study Type: Interventional Study. Setting: The study will be carried out in Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, UCMS and GTB Hospital Duration: May 2023 to November 2024 SUBJECTS: INCLUSION CRITERIA: 1. Pregnant women of any age and parity with gestational age more than 28 weeks scheduled for primary caesarean section. 2. Patients who are willing to follow up in UCMS & GTB Hospital. EXCLUSION CRITERIA 1. Patients with infections like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, HIV, Syphilis. 2. Patients with leaking per vaginum more than 18 hours or chorioamnionitis. 3. Any febrile illness. 4. Patients with moderate to severe anemia (Hb less than 10 gm%) or thrombocytopenia. 5. Any dermatological infection around surgical site. Sample Size: Even on extensive search of literature, we cannot find any article which is directly related to our study and meet out requirements for calculating the sample size. As per best of our knowledge it is to be taken as first attempt in obstetric patients and moreover there is a control group also. So we will randomize the patients in these two groups. Because of inability to calculate sample size keeping in view the time of study, we propose to take 50 women in each group. METHODOLOGY: Clinical trial registry for the study will be done at Clinical Trial Registry India (CTRI). Patients who are scheduled to undergo primary caesarean section satisfying inclusion and exclusion criteria will be enrolled from the labour room. An informed consent will be taken after which they will be divided into 2 groups by block randomisation. Group A: In Autologous HAM Patch Dressing group, after skin closure, HAM patch will be put as dressing over the suture line. Normal saline soaked gauze will be placed over HAM patch to prevent drying of the membrane followed by a dry gauze over it. If the wound is healthy, no further dressing will be done and caesarean site will be left open as such, and if unhealthy, then appropriate dressing will be done. Group B: Control group will be managed according to standard hospital protocol. After skin closure, sterile dry gauze dressing will be done on caesarean site which will be changed at Day 3. Follow up by REEDA scale on: Day 3 (change of dressing), Day 8 (at suture removal) and Day 42 (during PNC follow up). OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcome measure 1. REEDA (Redness, Edema, Ecchymosis, Discharge, Approximation) score in HAM dressing and non-HAM dressing group. Secondary outcome measures 1. Total number of patients with superficial and deep caesarean site infection in both the groups. 2. Adverse events like pain, swelling, discharge, dehiscence in both the groups. 3. Organisms associated with caesarean surgical site infection in both the groups. 4. Total length of hospital stay due to wound morbidity in both the groups. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: The scores of wound healing by REEDA score will be compared in both groups by unpaired T tests. Incidence rate of surgical site infection and other parameters between the two groups will be compared by Chi-squared test/Fisherâ€™s exact test.
