column51: This study is a single-center, randomized controlled trial designed to compare the effectiveness of wet versus dry collagen sheets in the healing of split-thickness skin graft donor sites in adult patients. Donor site morbidity remains a persistent clinical problem, contributing to delayed epithelialization, pain, and poor aesthetic outcomes. Although collagen sheets are widely used for donor site management, there is no clear evidence or consensus regarding the superiority of wet or dry formulations. A total of 132 adult patients (18–50 years) undergoing split-thickness skin grafting for burns sequelae or trauma at AIIMS Nagpur will be enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either wet collagen sheets (pre-moistened with sterile saline) or dry collagen sheets applied directly to the donor site. The primary outcome is time to complete epithelialization (>95%), while secondary outcomes include postoperative pain scores and donor site complicationssuch as infection, hypertrophic scarring, and delayed healing. Outcomes will be assessed at predefined postoperative intervals up to 8 months. The findings of this trial aim to generate evidence-based guidance for optimal donor site dressing selection, with the potential to reduce morbidity, improve patient comfort, and standardize donor site care practices in reconstructive surgery. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Rationale The administration of Rabies Immunoglobulin RIG is a painful procedure. Local application of painrelieving medications has been used for many other procedures effectively. Assessing antibody titres helps to see whether a lignocaine medicated pad interferes with immune response. It also provides an opportunity to determine effective immune response and factors affecting it. Novelty No previous studies other than a small clinical trial by our team. Objectives To find the effect 2 percent Lignocaine Medicated Pad LMP on pain relief and antibody response during Rabies Immunoglobulin administration factors determining antibody response, frequency of adverse events following RIG administration and cost effectiveness of procedure. Methods A randomized triple blind controlled trial will be done in three sites in India in tertiary care settings. Patients with Category III animal bite wounds will be randomized to intervention and placebo arms based on a previously generated random number sequence. Sterile gauze pads soaked with 2% lignocaine and normal saline will be intervention and placebo, respectively. Pain relief and antibody response will be the primary outcomes measured. Pain relief will be assessed using a numeric rating scale NRS and sound, eye and motor pain SEM scale. Costeffectiveness will be assessed by calculating the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio ICER determining the willingness to pay WTP threshold by the contingent valuation method. If the ICER falls below this WTP threshold the intervention will be considered cost-effective. A volume of 10cc of venous blood will be collected from the patient using a catheter into sterile, glass vacuum tubes. The samples will be promptly subjected to centrifugation at 2400 rpm for 12 minutes. Upon completion of this process, three distinct layers will be formed: the bottom layer will consist of red blood cells, the top layer will contain acellular plasma, and the middle layer will comprise the PRF coagulate. Utilizing sterile forceps, the PRF will be extracted from the tube and carefully separated from the adjacent red blood cell layer. The PRF serum will be absorbed onto a gauze pad, resulting in a membrane that is rich in fibrin and exhibits high tensile strength. This membrane will be trimmed to a size approximately 1.5 times larger than the perforation. Using a 0-degree endoscope under local anesthesia, the margins of the perforation will be freshened with a sickle knife. The PRF membrane will then be inserted into the perforation, and the ear will be packed with povidone iodine-soaked gel foam. column51: The Selecting Therapeutic Targets in Inflammatory Bowel Disease (STRIDE) initiative by the International Organization for the Study of Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IOIBD) first published in 2015 (STRIDE-I) and updated as STRIDE-II in 2021, provides a treat-to-target (T2T) framework for the management of UC and Crohn’s disease. The STRIDE-II represents a paradigm shift in UC management, providing a structured T2T approach that integrates clinical, biomarker, endoscopic and patient-centered outcomes. There have been only a very few studies which have assessed the benefit of treating to target by STRIDE II guidelines in Crohn’s disease, the two largest studies being the CALM study and the STARDUST study with contrasting results. In Ulcerative Colitis, the OPTIMISE study did not show an advantage of treating to target with biomarkers over standard of care in mild to moderate UC. Therefore, robust data on treat to target in Ulcerative colitis is still lacking. Evaluating how STRIDE-II can be implemented in real-world UC populations is crucial. column51: Long duration of orthodontic treatment is a major problem in adult patients. Thus Orthodontic professionals are constantly looking for ways to accelerate orthodontic tooth movement thereby reducing the treatment duration. Adults show lagging cell mobilization rates, irregular arrangement of collagen fibers, and are more prone for periodontal diseases in comparison to the younger patients. Therefore, shortening the duration of treatment by hastening the tooth movement is challenging for orthodontists. There are number of techniques available to augment the rate of orthodontic tooth movement and they can be invasive or non-invasive. Presently, leucocyte platelet rich fibrin (L-PRF) has been used to enhance the bone remodeling. The benefits of L-PRF remain for 4 weeks. Few studies have mentioned the benefits of blood concentrates on the acceleration of orthodontic tooth movement using sliding mechanics. But the literature is still lacking in studies that explored the effect of blood concentrates in orthodontic canine retraction using frictionless mechanics. column51: Postpartum anaemia remains a significant global health concern with prevalence rates varying between 10-40 percent of women globally. A prospective non-randomized quasi-experimental study conducted by Dhaka Medical College Hospital found that intravenous iron sucrose (600 mg administered over three days) was as effective as blood transfusion in improving haemoglobin levels and iron stores in women with moderate postpartum anaemia (Hb 7-8 g/dl). Their results showed mean Hb level increased by 4.2 g/dl in the IV iron group and 4.5 g/dl in the blood transfusion group at six weeks post-intervention, with no significant differences between groups.A study from Saudi Arabia reported postpartum anaemia prevalence of 52.percent with 55.4 percent classified as moderate anaemia. Risk factors identified include anaemia during pregnancy, primiparity, and childbirth complications. Another comparative study found intravenous iron sucrose to be safe, efficacious, and cost-effective for treating postpartum anaemia, with minimal adverse reactions compared to blood transfusion. Research on iron sucrose therapy has demonstrated significant improvements in haemoglobin levels, serum ferritin, reticulocyte count, and other haematological parameters with negligible side effects. The average dose requirement reported in studies ranges from 300-600 mg with administration protocols typically involving divided doses given on alternate days. Multiple studies have confirmed that iron sucrose is well-tolerated, with minor side effects including nausea, vomiting, mild fever, and rare instances of thrombophlebitis. This study will provide evidence based guidance on the optimal management strategy for moderate postpartum anaemia, potentially improving maternal care protocols. Intravenous iron sucrose therapy may prove to be an effective alternative to blood transfusion, reducing transfusion-associated risks such as transfusion reactions, infections, and alloimmunization. These mosquitoes are primary vectors for diseases like dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus, making their control critical for public health. The research involves applying this larvicidal mixture in artificial water-holding containers within the community during the rainy season. Additionally, safety evaluations will be conducted through community surveys and health assessments to ensure that the product poses no significant risks to humans, animals, or the environment. column51: This study is a prospective randomized controlled clinical trial designed to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of platelet rich fibrin alone, platelet rich fibrin combined with gelfoam, platelet rich fibrin combined with chitosan, and natural healing in mandibular third molar extraction socket healing. The study will be conducted in patients requiring surgical extraction of mandibular third molars attending the outpatient department of oral and maxillofacial surgery. Eligible participants aged 18 to 40 years with good general health will be recruited based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria and randomly allocated into four groups, PRF alone, PRF with gelfoam, PRF with chitosan, and control where no adjunct is used. The study will follow a standardized surgical extraction protocol and PRF preparation protocol, and it will be single blinded with assessor blinding, as patient and operator blinding are not feasible due to the visible nature of the materials and ethical considerations. Follow up assessments will be conducted at 30 minutes and 60 minutes post extraction, Day 1, Day 3, Day 7, Day 14, 1 month, and 3 months after surgery. The primary objective is to evaluate soft tissue healing and bone regeneration of extraction sockets among the four groups using clinical examination and radiographic assessment with intraoral periapical radiographs and grid analysis. Outcome parameters include soft tissue healing assessed using modified Landry healing index, bone regeneration assessed using radiographic measurements of alveolar bone height and anteroposterior socket width, hemostasis assessed by time to cessation of bleeding and modified bleeding severity scale, postoperative pain assessed using visual analogue scale, facial swelling assessed using standardized linear measurements between anatomical landmarks, trismus assessed by maximum inter incisal distance, and incidence of dry socket assessed clinically using standard diagnostic criteria. column51: To evaluate and compare the analgesic effect of local injection of Platelet Rich Plasma vs Bupivacaine with Triamcinolone in Chronic Achilles Tendinopathy. This is a prospective, randomised, comparative, single blinded, interventional study done in Department of Anaesthesiology and Critical Care, Pt.B.D.Sharma PGIMS Rohtak. A total of 80 patients of age group 18-70 years of either gender with ASA grade 1 and 2 suffering from chronic pain due to Achilles Tendinopathy for atleast three months having Visual Analog Scale score of more than 5 without satisfactory pain relief from conservative treatment presenting to the pain clinic OPD will be included in this study after approval from Institutional Biomedical Research Ethics Committee. The patients will be enrolled and randomly devided into two groups using a sealed envelope method. Group A will recieve Platelet Rich Plasma (4 ml) and group B will recieve Bupivacaine with Triamcinolone (4 ml). Patients with history of previous local anaesthetic infiltration at the site of lesion, malignancy, active local infection, patient on anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs, history of bleeding disorders, patients on immunosuppressants or steroids, Diabetes Mellitus, unwillingness to participate, patients on treatment for psychiatric illness, pregnant and lactating women will be excluded from the study. Evaluation of pain score= Using a Visual Analog Scale will be done before and after the injection of study drug and at intervals of one day, one week, two weeks, four weeks, eight weeks and after twelve weeks will be done. Total consumption of rescue analgesia ( oral tablet Paracetamol 500 mg 6 hourly) over twelve weeks will be noted. Other parameters like patient satisfaction will be noted.Any side effects will be noted and managed accordingly. OBJECTIVES:To evaluate the efficacy of intra-articular Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP)injection in reducing pain and improving functional outcomes in patients with osteoarthritis KL Grade II-III of the knee joint using validated scoring systems such as the WOMAC (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index)&To evaluate the duration of symptomatic relief (based on VAS Score)provided by a single PRP injection over a defined follow-up period for 1 year.To Standardised the Quantity,Dosing,Volume of PRP. column51: Wound healing is a complex biological process that can be impaired by infections, inflammation, and delayed tissue regeneration. Traditional wound care treatments often face limitations in preventing infections and accelerating healing, necessitating innovative therapeutic approaches. Copper nanoparticles (CuNPs) have gained attention due to their strong antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative properties. Similarly, plasma-rich proteins (PRPs) are rich in growth factors that enhance cell proliferation and tissue repair. This research integrates CuNPs with PRPs to develop a novel nanocomposite for improved wound healing. By combining the antimicrobial effects of copper with the regenerative potential of plasma-derived proteins, this formulation aims to enhance healing outcomes while minimizing infection risks. The need for such an advanced biomaterial is critical, especially for patients with chronic wounds, surgical site infections, and trauma-related injuries. This study addresses a significant clinical challenge, contributing to the advancement of nanomedicine and regenerative therapies for effective wound management.with above mentioned inclusion, exclusion and statistical data, expecting outcome of enhanced wound healing by promoting faster tissue regeneration and reducing infection rates. column51: Research Question This study aims to determine whether injectable platelet rich fibrin shows comparable clinical efficacy to intralesional corticosteroids in the management of oral lichen planus OLP. Research Hypothesis Null Hypothesis H0 There is no statistically significant difference between i PRF and intralesional corticosteroids in the clinical management of OLP. Alternative Hypothesis H1 Injectable platelet rich fibrin is more effective than intralesional corticosteroids in reducing pain, burning sensation, and lesion severity in patients with oral lichen planus. Aim To evaluate the efficacy of injectable platelet rich fibrin in oral lichen planus and compare it with intralesional Triamcinolone acetonide therapy. Objectives To assess the clinical effectiveness of i PRF in oral lichen planus. To evaluate reduction in pain and burning sensation using the Visual Analog Scale VAS. To assess reduction in lesion size using the Thongprasom classification. To observe any adverse effects of i PRF. To compare i PRF and intralesional corticosteroids in terms of pain reduction and lesion size improvement. Materials and Methods This is a prospective randomized comparative experimental clinical study conducted over two years in the Department of Oral Medicine and Radiology Rural Dental Hospital Loni starting March 2026 after IEC approval. Thirty patients with symptomatic bilateral oral lichen planus lesions will be included after obtaining informed consent. Patients must be 18 years or older clinically and when required histopathologically diagnosed with OLP and systemically healthy. Pregnant or lactating women patients with systemic diseases smokers patients on anticoagulant or immunosuppressive therapy and those with epithelial dysplasia or malignant transformation will be excluded. Venous blood will be collected and centrifuged at 700 rpm for 3 minutes to prepare i PRF. Each patient will receive 1 ml intralesional i PRF injection on one side of the buccal mucosa and 1 ml intralesional Triamcinolone acetonide injection on the opposite side. Injections will be administered once weekly for four weeks. Clinical evaluation will be done at baseline immediately after the last injection and at 1 month 2 months and 6 months post treatment using Visual Analog Scale VAS for pain and Thongprasom classification for lesion severity. Sample Size Using a 99 percent confidence level and standard sample size formula for frequency in a population N equals 10000 the calculated sample size is 30 participants. Statistical Analysis Descriptive statistics will be expressed as frequency and percentage. Pearson chi square test will assess inter and intra group differences. Independent sample t test will compare pain lesion size and adverse effects. ANOVA will evaluate associations between pain lesion size and adverse effects. column51: This study aims to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of Platelet Rich Plasma and Injectable Platelet Rich Fibrin with conventional Triamcinolone acetonide combined with Hyaluronidase injections in patients suffering from Oral Submucous Fibrosis. The research hypothesizes that Platelet Rich Plasma and Injectable Platelet Rich Fibrin provide greater therapeutic benefits than Triamcinolone acetonide with Hyaluronidase in managing Oral Submucous Fibrosis. A prospective randomized comparative clinical study will be conducted in the Department of Oral Medicine and Radiology after obtaining approval from the Institutional Ethics Committee. The total study duration will be approximately three years including patient selection treatment and follow up. Sixty patients clinically diagnosed with Grade Two to Grade Three Oral Submucous Fibrosis will be selected and randomly divided into three equal groups. Group A will receive Platelet Rich Plasma therapy Group B will receive Injectable Platelet Rich Fibrin therapy and Group C will receive conventional Triamcinolone acetonide with Hyaluronidase therapy. Patients aged between fifteen and sixty years with a history of areca nut or betel quid chewing and who provide informed consent will be included in the study. Patients with systemic diseases bleeding disorders pregnancy oral malignancy previous treatment for Oral Submucous Fibrosis or temporomandibular joint disorders will be excluded. The Platelet Rich Plasma group will receive weekly intralesional injections for six weeks following preparation through centrifugation of the patients blood. The Injectable Platelet Rich Fibrin group will also receive weekly intralesional injections for six weeks prepared without anticoagulant using low speed centrifugation. The conventional therapy group will receive weekly intralesional injections of Triamcinolone acetonide with Hyaluronidase for four weeks. Clinical evaluation will be done at baseline during treatment and post treatment follow up at one month three months and six months. Assessment will include subjective evaluation of burning sensation and objective evaluation of mouth opening cheek flexibility and presence of fibrotic bands. Patient safety comfort recurrence rate and overall treatment effectiveness will also be assessed. The study aims to establish a safe effective biocompatible and minimally invasive treatment approach for the management of Oral Submucous Fibrosis. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. The time of functional loading is dependent upon both the primary and secondary stability. Literature evidence suggest a dip in secondary stability following implant placement during the 4 to 8 week duration especially in immediate implant placement situation( Haitham Abdel Karim El komi 2021). Tonsillectomy remains one of the most frequently performed otolaryngologic operations and post operative pain and healing remains major problems for the patients. Pain is due to mucosal injury, muscle injury and exposed cranial nerve endings leading to inflammation and spasm of pharyngeal musculature. After tonsillectomy high degree of swelling within 24 hours in uvula and anterior tonsillar pillar and posterior tonsillar pillar may hinder with healing and is associated with increased post operative complication. It can lead to decreased oral intake, vomiting, difficulty breathing and dehydration requiring hospital re-admission. Bupivacaine is a long acting local anaesthetic of the amino amide group. It is indicated for infiltration anesthesia, nerve block, epidural and intrathecal anesthesia. It can also be used in surgical area by infiltration or by local application . By blocking the afferent nerve endings through the inhibition of voltage gated ion channels it decreases the onset of post operative pain. Platelet rich plasma (PRP) have been used for various indications for many years, resulting in interest in potential autologous PRP in regenerative medicine. It is a suitable option with clinical benefits, with positive clinical outcomes. PRP which is also known as platelet enriched plasma, platelet rich concentrate, autologous platelet gel and platelet releasate. It is defined as part of plasma fraction of autologous peripheral blood that has a platelet concentration above baseline. The serum contains epidermal growth factor, tumor growth factor beta firbronectin, all of which have the property of speeding the process of epithelisation. It also has antibacterial properties because of immunoglobulin G and lysozyme ingredients. The objective of the study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy of PRP and bupivacaine in reducing postoperative pain and promoting tissue healing following tonsillectomy. By systematically assessing pain levels and the healing process in the postoperative period, this study aims to generate evidence that may guide future clinical practice. column51: Plantar fasciitis is one of the most common conditions characterized by heel pain, which is usually exacerbated by the first step of the day, especially after standing for a long period of time. Although there is significant improvement with the help of medication, exercises, and shoe changes, there remain some patients who continue to suffer from pain. Different injections, such as steroid injections, platelet-rich plasma, growth factor concentrate, and dextrose prolotherapy, can be used for the treatment of plantar fasciitis, especially after the failure of conservative treatment options. All of these injections provide relief from plantar fasciitis, although by different mechanisms. column28: Preparation & StorageSourcing: Collected from screened healthy donors following NACO guidelines to ensure safety from transfusion-transmitted infections (TTIs). Processing: Prepared via a two-spin centrifugation technique and aliquoted into 10ml sterile vials. Cryopreservation: Vials are stored at -80°C. Activation is achieved through a double freeze-thaw cycle (24 hours at -80°C, followed by thawing at 37°C for 8–12 minutes). The final thaw occurs one hour before clinical application. Clinical ApplicationDosage: Local infiltration at the wound margin (0.2text{ ml/cm}). Frequency: Administered every 4 days until complete wound healing is achieved. Standard Care: Applied in conjunction with conventional sterile dressing and standard wound management. | Standard Protocol Debridement: Initial and periodic surgical debridement to remove necrotic tissue as clinically indicated. Cleansing: Irrigation with sterile normal saline to maintain a clean wound bed. Dressing: Application of conventional sterile gauze dressings using aseptic techniques. Frequency & Monitoring Schedule: Wound dressings will be changed every 4 days (to match the intervention arms schedule) or as required by clinical exudate levels. Standard Care: Patients will receive systemic antibiotics, analgesics, and fracture stabilization according to standard institutional orthopedic protocols.

column51: The proposed study is a prospective, single-blind, randomized controlled trial to be conducted at SCB Medical College and Hospital, Cuttack, evaluating the therapeutic potential of allogenic Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) in accelerating soft tissue healing for Gustilo-Anderson Type II compound fractures. Traumatic injuries, particularly those resulting from road traffic accidents, frequently lead to open fractures where delayed wound healing significantly increases patient morbidity and healthcare costs. While autologous PRP is a recognized regenerative tool, its application in acute trauma is often precluded by the patient’s clinical status, such as anemia or sepsis. This research addresses this gap by utilizing allogenic PRP—sourced from healthy, screened donors and prepared under standardized conditions in the Department of Transfusion Medicine—as a scalable, "off-the-shelf" biological intervention. The study aims to determine if local infiltration of allogenic PRP every four days, in conjunction with conventional wound care, results in superior healing compared to standard care alone. The primary outcome will be measured using the Bates-Jensen Wound Assessment Tool (BWAT) scores over a three-week period. The methodology involves a precise two-spin centrifugation and a double freeze-thaw activation protocol at 80°C to ensure high growth factor concentration and safety. With a calculated sample size of 38 participants, the study seeks to provide evidence that allogenic PRP can safely reduce time to epithelialization and infection rates. Ultimately, this research highlights the expanding role of Transfusion Medicine in regenerative therapy, offering a cost-effective and evidence-based strategy to improve clinical outcomes in resource-limited trauma care settings. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Oral Submucous Fibrosis is a chronic potentially malignant disorder of the oral cavity associated with reduced mouth opening, burning sensation, and progressive fibrosis of oral mucosa. Various treatment modalities have been tried with variable results. The present prospective randomized clinical trial aims to compare the efficacy of intralesional Triamcinolone injection with Autologous Platelet Rich Plasma injection in the management of Oral Submucous Fibrosis. Thirty patients clinically diagnosed with OSMF will be randomly allocated into two groups. Group A will receive intralesional Triamcinolone acetonide injection once weekly for six weeks, while Group B will receive autologous Platelet Rich Plasma injection once weekly for six weeks. All patients will be advised standard physiotherapy exercises. The primary outcome measure will be improvement in interincisal mouth opening. Secondary outcomes will include reduction in burning sensation, improvement in tongue protrusion and cheek flexibility, and assessment of adverse effects. column51: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) was first described in 1938. Because CSF leakage is the reason of SIH, this disease also has been named spontaneous intracranial hypovolemia. Mostly leaking sites are in the thoracic spine or at the cervicothoracic junction. Patients may have a history of trivial traumatic injury, or may have no definite history of injury. The imaging findings of SIH derived from CSF volume depletion usually show brain sagging and related complaints. SIH is characterized by orthostatic headache (OH), and DPME (diffuse pachymeningeal gadolinium enhancement) on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), evidence of CSF leakage on conventional myelography, CT myelography or cisternography, CSF opening pressure LESS THAN 60 mmH2O in sitting position unrelated to lumbar puncture and definite trauma. OH, as defined by the International Headache Society, is a headache that occurs within 15 minutes of an upright position and is relieved within 30 minutes of recumbency. The OH characteristics may change over time, resulting in a daily chronic headache or paradoxical headache, with worsening in supine position. Various additional symptoms, like neck pain, neck stiffness, nausea, photophobia, vomiting, tinnitus, diplopia, and decreased level of consciousness have been described . Three causes, first described by Schievink et al. in 2016, that may lead to spinal CSF loss include ventral dural tear (type 1), leaking nerve root diverticulum (type 2) or a CSF-venous fistula (CVF; type 3) SIH is primarily treated conservatively. When more aggressive treatment is required i.e. initial conservative measures failed, an epidural blood patch (EBP) is the modality of choice. Historically, lumbar EBP has been used regardless of leak site because of its low risk and the ability of blood to travel many levels from the site of injection. Mokri B explained mechanisms that are involved in relieving the headache. The immediate headache-relief occurs when the blood inflow presses the dura mater and causes CSF volume replenishment. The secondary long-lasting relief is achieved by sealing of leak by blood inflow. The amount of blood injected in SIH patients has varied in different reports. Usually, 20 ml of autologous blood is used in the lumbar spine level in case of non-targeted EBPs. Performing an EBP on SIH patients has shown persistent symptomatic relief in up to 90% of the cases in previous studies. Ultrasound evaluation of the optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) has emerged in recent years as a useful non-invasive tool for estimating ICP or detecting intracranial hypotension and hypertension. It is a safe technique that can be conducted at the bedside, in real time, and is reproducible, relatively low cost, and does not carry the risks of radiation and CNS infections. ONSD is currently considered the best non-invasive modality for dynamic estimation of ICP . POCUS measurements have shown ONSD to be significantly correlating with ICP . ICP can be calculated using the formula ONSD: nICPONSD = 5.00 × ONSD - 13.92 mmHg . This is thus necessary in assessing patients in whom invasive ICP monitoring is either unavailable or is contraindicated or resource-poor areas where MRI or CT myelography/ cisternography is not easily available. An increase or decrease in fluid in the subarachnoid space can cause the ONSD to widen or narrow. The validity of using ultrasound measurements of the ONSD to assess intracranial pressure has been demonstrated, and this non-invasive and safe method has been used to assist in clinical diagnosis. It is hypothesized that the resolution of SIH can be predicted by ONSD. This study is thus being conducted to observe the correlation between ONSD measured non-invasively with symptom relief after EBP. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: BACKGROUND: Periodontitis is a disease of the tissue surrounding the tooth structure that may lead to involvement of areas between roots of tooth called as furcation. On the other hand, Chitosan is a biopolymer with numerous properties including antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and wound healing. column51: Pulpotomy is a conservative treatment option for managing irritated crucial pulp.It entails the surgical amputation of the inflamed coronal portion of the pulp while preserving the vitality of the radicular pulp. The most commonly used material is formocresol, but it has the disadvantage that it is linked to carcinogenic potential, cytotoxicity, and systemic distribution. It shows activate inflammatory responses in pulp tissues. The second commonly used is Mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) has gained considerable attention in dentistry due to its excellent sealing ability, biocompatibility, bioactivity, hydrophilic nature, and capacity to stimulate dentin regeneration. Its application in pulpotomy procedures has demonstrated high clinical success rates, thereby establishing MTA as a preferred material among pulp therapy. Recent research has led to the emergence of materials with improved regenerative properties and optimal pulpotomy materials. These alternative materials include natural derived silk fibroin, biologically derived simvastatin gel. Simvastatin is a lipid-lowering drug that acts by inhibiting 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase. Its long-term clinical use has established it as a safe and cost-effective therapeutic agent. In addition to its cholesterol-lowering action, simvastatin exhibits pleiotropic effects, including anti-inflammatory activity, promotion of angiogenesis. It improves osteoblast function while decreasing osteoclast activity, leading to increased bone production and mineralisation. It has regenerative effects on human dental pulp stem cells, resulting in the creation of reparative dentin. Silk fibroin, a natural protein generated from silkworm silk, shows promise as a biomaterial for tissue engineering in dentistry. Silk fibroin has various benefits, including great biocompatibility, predictable biodegradability, low immunogenicity, and high mechanical strength. Silk fibroin is affordable, eco-friendly, and abundantly available. Silk fibroin scaffolds promote cell adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation, and are well-tolerated in vivo with low immunological reaction Thus, this study will be conducted to compare and evaluate rhe clinically and radiographic effectiveness of silk fibroin and simvastatin gel in comparison to mineral trioxide aggregate as a pulpotomy material in primary molars in terms of the presence of normal mucosa without abnormal mobility,pain and sensitivity to percussion. column51: Chronic diabetic ulcers are a major cause of morbidity and risk of amputation due to delayed healing poor vascularity and infection. Conventional wound care often results in prolonged healing time. Platelet rich plasma is an autologous concentration of platelets containing growth factors that promote tissue repair and angiogenesis. This study is a randomized controlled trial conducted in the department of general surgery at a tertiary care center. The aim is to evaluate the efficacy of platelet rich plasma therapy in healing of chronic diabetic ulcers as compared to standard wound care. A total of one hundred sixty four patients will be randomly allocated into two groups. One group will receive platelet rich plasma along with standard wound care while the other group will receive standard wound care alone. Patients will be followed up regularly for assessment of ulcer healing. The primary outcome is complete ulcer healing at twelve weeks. Secondary outcomes include time to healing reduction in ulcer size pain reduction and adverse events. The study is expected to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of platelet rich plasma in management of chronic diabetic ulcers. | Complications during pregnancy( anaemia, pre- eclampsia, and gestational diabetes) | i.Severe Sepsis is a life threatening condition which is defined by the presence of severe infection and systemic inflammatory response to the infection, leading to one or more organ failures. ii.Mortality remains very high, about 25-50%, in severe sepsis patients in spite of advanced antibiotics therapy and supportive care in the form of vasopressors, and fluid infusions. iii.Sepsis is the most common cause of death in the ICU. column51: Preterm birth remains a significant global health concern. Among these, infants born between 28 and 34 weeks of gestation constitute a substantial proportion and face considerable challenges during the immediate cardiopulmonary transition after birth. A large majority of these preterm neonates require some form of resuscitation in the delivery room, making optimal management at birth crucial for improving survival and reducing both short- and long-term morbidity. Delayed cord clamping (DCC) is now considered the standard of care for vigorous preterm infants, as it facilitates placental transfusion and improves hemodynamic stability. However, its implementation in non-vigorous infants remains difficult, since conventional practice emphasizes rapid cord clamping to allow immediate resuscitation. At birth, the umbilical cord contains approximately 80–90 mL/kg of fetal blood volume, and early cord clamping (ECC), particularly in asphyxiated infants, can result in significant losses—up to 30% of total blood volume and 60% of red blood cell volume—thereby exacerbating hypoxia-ischemia and negatively impacting outcomes. Umbilical cord milking (UCM) has emerged as a potential alternative, offering a rapid method of placental transfusion while enabling timely transfer to the resuscitation area. column51: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if giving intravenous immunoglobulin directly to the fetus during intrauterine transfusion can improve newborn outcomes in pregnancies affected by rhesus isoimmunization.Rhesus isoimmunization happens when a pregnant woman’s immune system attacks her baby’s red blood cells. This can cause severe anemia (low red blood cell levels) before birth. Doctors treat this condition with intrauterine transfusion, a procedure that gives blood to the fetus before birth. However, this treatment does not stop the immune attack. Many newborns still develop anemia and high bilirubin levels after birth and may need phototherapy or exchange transfusion. The main questions this study aims to answer are: 1. Does adding fetal intravenous immunoglobulin increase the baby’s blood count at birth? 2. Does it lower the need for phototherapy or exchange transfusion after birth? Researchers will compare: Intrauterine transfusion with fetal intravenous immunoglobulin to Intrauterine transfusion alone in order to see if adding immunoglobulin improves newborn outcomes. Participants will Undergo intrauterine transfusion as part of routine care and be randomly assigned to receive either standard transfusion alone or transfusion with added fetal immunoglobulin. All participants will be followed until delivery and during the newborn hospital stay until discharge. The main outcome is the baby’s blood count at birth. Researchers will also measure: 1. How quickly the baby’s blood count falls before birth 2. Need for and duration of phototherapy 3. Need for exchange transfusion or blood transfusions after birth 4.
